notes: Raycast-hosted models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Perplexity), AI Credits, Good/Bad feedback sent to Raycast, and chat sync are cloud/Pro features. A local build can run on BYOK APIs, Ollama, GGUF chat models on the llama.cpp+Metal runtime DigUp already vendors (Vendor/llama.cpp), or Apple FoundationModels (LanguageModelSession, macOS 26). The source page does not mention a web-search toggle for Quick AI.

functions.name: Ask with Tab from Root Search
functions.what: Pressing Tab in the launcher sends whatever was typed to Quick AI and starts answering inline. With an empty query it opens a blank prompt.
functions.macos_build: In DigUp's SearchPanel NSTextField delegate, implement control(_:textView:doCommandBy:) and catch #selector(insertTab(_:)). Swap the panel's SwiftUI content to a QuickAIView seeded with the query. Stream tokens with URLSession.bytes(for:) by parsing SSE 'data:' lines from OpenAI /v1/chat/completions (stream=true) or Anthropic /v1/messages (stream=true), or by calling llama.cpp in-process. Keep conversations in SQLite (DigUp already links SQLite3).
functions.permission: network (none if the model is local)

functions.name: Quick AI command
functions.what: A root-search command that opens Quick AI with an empty prompt.
functions.macos_build: Register a built-in command item in the root-search provider that pushes QuickAIView.

functions.name: Quick AI as Fallback Command
functions.what: When root search finds nothing, pressing Enter sends the unmatched text to Quick AI.
functions.macos_build: When the ranked result list is empty, render the configured fallback rows (Quick AI first) and route the query string into the selected fallback.

functions.name: Streaming inline answer
functions.what: The prompt is submitted and the reply streams into the launcher window as rendered Markdown.
functions.macos_build: Append deltas on the MainActor to an observable message. Render with swift-markdown or MarkdownUI (AttributedString(markdown:) covers inline only). Cancel with Task.cancel().

functions.name: Primary Action: paste or copy the response
functions.what: Pressing Enter on an answer pastes it into the app that was focused before the launcher opened. A setting switches this to copy.
functions.macos_build: Save NSWorkspace.shared.frontmostApplication before showing the panel. On ↵, call NSPasteboard.general.clearContents() and setString, orderOut the panel, and call prevApp.activate(). Then post ⌘V with CGEvent(keyboardEventSource:nil, virtualKey:CGKeyCode(kVK_ANSI_V), keyDown:true/false), set flags=.maskCommand, and post to .cghidEventTap. Restore the previous clipboard after about 300 ms if desired.
functions.permission: Accessibility (named Device Control and Data Access on macOS 27) for the synthetic ⌘V

functions.name: Code blocks with language, copy, and line wrap
functions.what: Code in answers shows the detected language, a copy button, and an 'Enable line wrap' toggle. Long lines scroll sideways by default.
functions.macos_build: Parse fenced blocks and take the language from the info string or a heuristic. Use ScrollView(.horizontal) or an NSScrollView with wrapping toggled through NSTextContainer.widthTracksTextView. Optional highlighting via tree-sitter or Highlightr.

functions.name: Regenerate
functions.what: Re-runs the last answer with the same model.
functions.macos_build: Drop the last assistant message and resend the same message history.

functions.name: Regenerate with different model
functions.what: Re-runs the last answer on a model you pick.
functions.macos_build: Show a model picker popover, then resend the history to the chosen provider adapter.

functions.name: New conversation
functions.what: Starts a fresh Quick AI chat.
functions.macos_build: Insert a new conversation row and clear the view state.

functions.name: Navigate recent Quick AI chats
functions.what: Steps backward and forward through earlier Quick AI conversations.
functions.macos_build: SQLite query on conversations ordered by updated_at, keeping a cursor index.

functions.name: Rate response Good/Bad
functions.what: Marks an answer good or bad. Raycast sends the rating to its servers.
functions.macos_build: Store the rating locally in a message_feedback column. There is no server to send it to.

functions.name: Dictate prompt
functions.what: Speech-to-text into the Quick AI composer. Accept with ⌃M or ↵, cancel with Esc.
functions.macos_build: Reuse the Dictation engine (SpeechAnalyzer/SpeechTranscriber on macOS 26, or SFSpeechRecognizer) and stream partial results into the composer text.
functions.permission: Microphone (+ Speech Recognition if SFSpeechRecognizer is used)

functions.name: Add Context menu / @ attach
functions.what: Attaches the Focused Window, Selected Text, a Selected Area screenshot, or the Entire Screen to the next message. Attachments carry over to AI Chat.
functions.keys: @ in composer, or the Add Context button
functions.macos_build: Typing '@' opens a popover. Reuse the Screen Awareness capture code. Images go in as base64 vision content blocks, text as extra user-message parts.

functions.name: Collapsed long messages
functions.what: Your own messages over about 10 lines collapse, with Show more and Collapse controls.
functions.macos_build: SwiftUI .lineLimit(10) with an expand toggle.

functions.name: Ask User Question
functions.what: The model can pause to ask a multiple-choice clarifying question in the chat. This is always on.
functions.macos_build: Expose an ask_user_question tool (JSON Schema: question, options[]). When the model calls it, suspend the tool loop, render the options as buttons, and return the pick as the tool_result.

functions.name: Auto model with preference
functions.what: 'Auto' picks a model per request based on a Lightweight, Balanced, or Flagship preference, and tries to keep follow-ups on the same model.
functions.macos_build: A heuristic router (prompt length, attachments, code detection, or a small local classifier) maps the tier to configured model IDs. Pin the chosen model on the conversation.

functions.name: Change Model / Regenerate with Model…
functions.what: Switches the model mid-conversation from the Action Panel.
functions.macos_build: Update conversation.model and send later requests to that adapter.

functions.name: Continue in AI Chat
functions.what: Moves the Quick AI conversation, with its history, model, and attachments, into the full AI Chat window.
functions.macos_build: Open the AI Chat NSWindow with the same conversation ID. Both views read one SQLite store.

functions.name: Auto new chat after inactivity
functions.what: Quick AI starts a fresh chat after a timeout: 5, 10, 15, or 30 min, 1 h, always, or never. The same timer decides whether Send to AI reuses the open chat.
functions.macos_build: Compare the conversation's last_activity timestamp with a UserDefaults setting each time the panel is shown.

functions.name: Quick AI settings
functions.what: Primary Action (paste or copy), hiding the Tab hint, and whether Quick AI history is combined with AI Chat or kept separate.
functions.macos_build: UserDefaults values plus a filter on the conversations query by surface.

notes: Cross-device chat sync (encrypted Cloud Sync), Raycast-hosted models, and server-side tools such as Raycast web search and image generation (which costs credits) are cloud features. Locally, image generation needs an OpenAI Images or Gemini API key, and web search needs a search API (Brave, Tavily, Exa, Perplexity) or a provider's native search tool. Keep the history in SQLite with FTS5, which DigUp already uses.

functions.name: AI Chat window
functions.what: A standalone chat window opened from the AI Chat command, with ⌘J from Quick AI, or by a Send to AI command.
functions.macos_build: A titled, resizable NSWindow hosting a SwiftUI NavigationSplitView (history sidebar, transcript, composer). DigUp is an agent (LSUIElement) app, so call NSApp.activate(ignoringOtherApps:) then makeKeyAndOrderFront.

functions.name: Always on Top
functions.what: Keeps the chat window above other apps.
functions.macos_build: Toggle window.level between .floating and .normal, and add .canJoinAllSpaces to the collection behavior.

functions.name: Zoom
functions.what: Scales chat text.
functions.macos_build: Store a zoom factor and apply it with .font scaling or .dynamicTypeSize in the environment.

functions.name: Send / new line / send-key setting
functions.what: ↵ sends and ⇧↵ inserts a newline. A setting can make ⌘↵ the send key instead.
functions.macos_build: An NSTextView subclass that intercepts insertNewline: and checks NSEvent.modifierFlags.

functions.name: Queue or Steer follow-ups
functions.what: While a reply streams, a new message either waits in a queue (default) or steers by interrupting the run. ⌘↵ uses the other behavior once, and a queued message can be promoted to Steer.
functions.macos_build: Keep a per-chat pending queue. Steer cancels the streaming Task, keeps the partial assistant text, appends the new user message, and restarts the request.

functions.name: Cancel running response
functions.what: Sending an empty input stops the response that is streaming.
functions.macos_build: Call Task.cancel() on the stream and close the URLSession bytes stream.

functions.name: Edit message and re-run
functions.what: Edit an earlier message from its pencil icon. Messages after it are replaced and the chat re-runs from that point.
functions.macos_build: Truncate messages after the edited index (soft-delete) and resend.

functions.name: Recall messages with arrows
functions.what: With an empty composer, ↑ loads your last message and ↑/↓ step through earlier ones. Esc restores the draft.
functions.macos_build: In the composer's doCommandBy, handle moveUp: and moveDown: when the text is empty.

functions.name: Regenerate last response
functions.what: Re-runs the last answer.
functions.macos_build: Same as Quick AI.

functions.name: New Chat
functions.what: Starts a new conversation.
functions.macos_build: Insert a conversation row.

functions.name: Find in Chat
functions.what: Searches text inside the open chat with next and previous match.
functions.keys: ⌘F; ↵ or ⌘G next; ⇧↵ or ⇧⌘G previous; Esc close
functions.macos_build: For an NSTextView transcript, set usesFindBar=true (NSTextFinder). For a SwiftUI list, do a custom range search, highlight matches, and scroll with ScrollViewReader.

functions.name: Model picker
functions.what: Choose the model from the title bar or by typing / in the composer. The / menu also sets Model Preference.
functions.macos_build: A Picker bound to conversation.model, plus a slash-command popover in the composer.

functions.name: Creativity level
functions.what: Per-chat creativity: None, Low, Medium, High, or Maximum.
functions.macos_build: Map the levels to temperature, for example 0, 0.3, 0.7, 1.0, 1.3, clamped to each provider's range.

functions.name: Reasoning effort
functions.what: Sets reasoning effort for models that support it.
functions.macos_build: Map to OpenAI reasoning_effort (Responses API: reasoning.effort), Anthropic thinking.budget_tokens, or Gemini thinkingConfig.thinkingBudget.

functions.name: Web Search tool toggle
functions.what: Lets the model search the web and cite sources.
functions.macos_build: A web_search tool that calls the Brave, Tavily, or Exa REST APIs and shows source cards. Alternatively, enable the provider's native search (OpenAI web_search tool, Anthropic web_search server tool).

functions.name: Attachments
functions.what: Attach files, Notes, Clipboard History items, browser tabs, web search results, the Focused Window, Selected Text, a window, area, or full-screen screenshot, and calendar events.
functions.macos_build: Files: NSOpenPanel or drag-and-drop. Reuse DigUp's Extractors and PDFKit for text, and send images as base64. Browser tabs: NSAppleScript (Safari 'URL of tabs of windows'; Chrome, Arc, and Brave 'URL of tabs'). Calendar: EventKit. Screens: ScreenCaptureKit. Oversized content is written to a file, and the model gets the head of it plus the path.
functions.permission: Calendars, Automation (browsers), Screen Recording, Accessibility depending on source

functions.name: Image generation tool
functions.what: The model can generate images in the chat, and you can drag them into other apps.
functions.macos_build: A tool that calls the OpenAI Images API (gpt-image) or Gemini image generation. Save the PNG under Application Support and use .onDrag { NSItemProvider(contentsOf: fileURL) } to drag it out.

functions.name: Terminal command tool
functions.what: The model can run shell commands, subject to tool permissions.
functions.macos_build: Process with executableURL=/bin/zsh and arguments ['-lc', cmd], currentDirectoryURL set to the project working directory, stdout and stderr through Pipe, and a timeout. The app must not be sandboxed.

functions.name: Per-chat tool toggles
functions.what: The chat sidebar turns individual tools and extensions on or off for that chat.
functions.macos_build: Store an enabled-tool set on the conversation and filter the tools array sent to the model.

functions.name: Change Agent / Ask Anything
functions.what: Applies a saved Agent's instructions, model, and extensions to the chat, or clears it.
functions.macos_build: Set conversation.agentId and rebuild the system prompt and tool list.

functions.name: Auto-summarize long chats
functions.what: Near the context limit, older turns are summarized in the background ('Summarizing chat…'). Oversized tool results are saved to a file.
functions.macos_build: Estimate tokens (about 4 characters per token, or the llama.cpp tokenizer for local models). Above a threshold, summarize the earliest N turns with a cheap model and store a summary message that replaces them in the prompt.

functions.name: History sidebar, search, and quick jump
functions.what: Toggle the chat list, search titles and content, and hold ⌘ to show numbers for jumping to the first ten chats.
functions.macos_build: SQLite FTS5 virtual table over message text. A flagsChanged local monitor shows the number badges.

functions.name: Pin chat
functions.what: Keeps a chat at the top of the sidebar.
functions.macos_build: A pinned flag column.

functions.name: Archive chat / Auto-Archive
functions.what: Archives a chat manually or automatically after a configurable age.
functions.macos_build: An archived_at column plus a daily sweep for auto-archive.

functions.name: Delete / Recently Deleted / Delete All
functions.what: Deleted chats go to Recently Deleted for 60 days, where you can preview them read-only, Restore, Delete Permanently, or Empty. Delete All Chats keeps pinned ones.
functions.macos_build: A deleted_at column with a purge job for anything older than 60 days.

functions.name: Rename chat
functions.what: Rename a chat by double-clicking the title. ↵ saves, Esc cancels.
functions.macos_build: Inline TextField. Auto-title new chats with a cheap model call.

functions.name: Copy Chat
functions.what: Copies the whole conversation as text.
functions.macos_build: Serialize the messages to Markdown and put them on NSPasteboard.

functions.name: Branch Chat
functions.what: Creates a new chat that contains the history up to a chosen message.
functions.macos_build: Copy the message rows up to the index into a new conversation.

functions.name: Move to Project
functions.what: Files the chat under a Project, from a menu or by dragging.
functions.macos_build: Update conversation.project_id. Accept drops in the sidebar with .dropDestination.

functions.name: Background Notifications
functions.what: Sends a system notification when a chat finishes while you are in another app. Off by default.
functions.macos_build: Call UNUserNotificationCenter.requestAuthorization. Post when the chat window is not key.

functions.name: Prevent Sleep During AI Runs
functions.what: Keeps the Mac awake while an AI run is in progress.
functions.macos_build: IOPMAssertionCreateWithName(kIOPMAssertionTypePreventUserIdleSystemSleep) or ProcessInfo.processInfo.beginActivity(options:[.idleSystemSleepDisabled]) for the duration of the run.

functions.name: Resume interrupted stream
functions.what: A reply that was still streaming when the window closed is restored the next time it opens.
functions.macos_build: Persist partial deltas every N tokens. Keep the stream Task alive in an app-level service that is independent of the window.

notes: Share AI Command (shareable link), organization-shared commands, and Quick Fix always run through Raycast AI and spend credits, even with BYOK. Locally, share as exported JSON or a custom-URL deeplink. Built-in commands can be edited and duplicated but not deleted.

functions.name: Improve Writing
functions.what: Rewrites the selected text so it reads more clearly.
functions.macos_build: A prompt template with {selection}. Read the selection through AX: AXUIElementCreateSystemWide() → kAXFocusedUIElementAttribute → kAXSelectedTextAttribute. Fall back to posting ⌘C, waiting for NSPasteboard.changeCount to change, reading the text, and restoring the clipboard.

functions.name: Fix Spelling and Grammar
functions.what: Corrects spelling and grammar in the selection.
functions.macos_build: Same selection pipeline. NSSpellChecker can pre-check, but the LLM does the fix.

functions.name: Explain This in Simple Terms
functions.what: Explains the selected text in plain language.
functions.macos_build: Prompt template with {selection}, opened in the Quick AI view.

functions.name: Change Tone to Professional
functions.what: Rewrites the selection in a formal tone.
functions.macos_build: Prompt template, Replace Selection output.

functions.name: Change Tone to Friendly
functions.what: Rewrites the selection in a warmer, casual tone.
functions.macos_build: Prompt template, Replace Selection output.

functions.name: Find Bugs in Code
functions.what: Reviews the selected code and points out bugs.
functions.macos_build: Prompt template with {selection}, using a code-capable model.

functions.name: Summarize Webpage
functions.what: Summarizes the page open in the frontmost browser.
functions.macos_build: {browser-tab}: get the URL and text with NSAppleScript. Safari: 'do JavaScript "document.body.innerText" in current tab of front window', which needs Develop › Allow JavaScript from Apple Events. Chrome, Arc, Brave, Edge: 'execute active tab of front window javascript …'. Otherwise fetch the URL with URLSession and extract readable text.

functions.name: Ask About Webpage
functions.what: Answers questions about the current browser page.
functions.macos_build: Same browser-tab capture as Summarize Webpage, plus an {argument} for the question.

functions.name: Quick Fix
functions.what: One hotkey fixes spelling and grammar in place in any focused field, using the selection (default) or the whole field. An experimental option preserves rich formatting.
functions.macos_build: A CGEvent.tapCreate(.cgSessionEventTap, .listenOnly) on flagsChanged that detects keycode 60 (kVK_RightShift) twice within about 350 ms. Read kAXSelectedTextAttribute or kAXValueAttribute. Write back with AXUIElementSetAttributeValue(kAXSelectedTextAttribute) when settable, otherwise pasteboard plus ⌘V. To preserve formatting, copy as .html or .rtf, have the model edit the HTML, and paste it back as HTML.

functions.name: Create AI Command
functions.what: A form with prompt, name and icon, model, creativity, reasoning effort, output behavior, highlight-changes, and tags. Saved commands appear in Root Search.
functions.macos_build: A SwiftUI Form in the panel. Store as Codable JSON or a SQLite row and register each command as a root-search item with its own alias and hotkey.

functions.name: Output Behavior
functions.what: Show the result in the launcher ('Open in Raycast') or replace the selected text directly.
functions.macos_build: Replace through AX set selected text, or pasteboard plus a synthetic ⌘V into the previous app.

functions.name: Highlight Editing Changes
functions.what: Marks what the AI changed when it rewrites selected text.
functions.macos_build: Word-level diff using Swift CollectionDifference over tokenized words, rendered as an AttributedString with insert and delete colors.

functions.name: Prompt placeholders and @-tools
functions.what: Prompts can include {selection}, {argument name=…}, other dynamic placeholders (inserted by typing {), and @ AI Extensions.
functions.macos_build: A placeholder tokenizer and resolver shared with Snippets and Quicklinks. Values are wrapped in triple quotes by default. Argument placeholders become search-bar input fields.

functions.name: Run AI Command on selection
functions.what: Select text, open the launcher, pick a command, and press ↵. The result can be copied, pasted, or continued in chat.
functions.macos_build: Capture the selection before the panel takes focus, because AX reads must happen while the other app is frontmost.

functions.name: Edit AI Command
functions.what: Opens a command in the editor.
functions.macos_build: Reuse the create form.

functions.name: Duplicate AI Command
functions.what: Clones a command, including built-ins.
functions.macos_build: Copy the row with a new ID.

functions.name: Share AI Command
functions.what: Creates a shareable link to a command.
functions.macos_build: Raycast's version is cloud-hosted. Locally, export JSON or a digup://ai-command/import?data=<base64> deeplink handled by application(_:open:).

functions.name: Import AI Commands
functions.what: Imports commands from a JSON file.
functions.macos_build: NSOpenPanel and a JSONDecoder.

functions.name: Search AI Commands
functions.what: Lists all AI commands, filterable by tag.
functions.macos_build: A list view with a tag filter dropdown.

functions.name: Per-command model / default model
functions.what: Each command stores its own model. Settings set the default for new custom commands, and changing it does not update existing ones.
functions.macos_build: A model ID column, defaulted from UserDefaults at creation time.

functions.name: Delete custom command
functions.what: Removes a user-created command.
functions.macos_build: Delete the row, with a confirmation alert.

notes: Third-party Store AI Extensions (Linear, GitHub, Notion, Slack, Figma, Things, and others) run on Raycast's Node/React extension runtime and cannot be loaded natively. Replace them with MCP servers. @raycast-feedback and @manual target Raycast services. Organization-private extensions are a Teams cloud feature. @file-explorer is Windows-only. In Raycast, Auto permission mode is the default on paid plans.

functions.name: @-mention picker
functions.what: Typing @ in AI Chat, Quick AI, or Root Search lists the installed extensions, MCP servers, and skills, and inserts a pill.
functions.macos_build: Composer completion popover. Store mentions as token ranges and send the mentioned tools as preferred or forced.

functions.name: Tool-calling loop
functions.what: The model picks a tool and its arguments, each call is shown in the chat, and calls can chain across several @-mentioned sources.
functions.macos_build: A provider-agnostic Tool protocol (name, JSON Schema, readOnly/destructive flags, async run). Translate to OpenAI 'tools', Anthropic 'tools', and Gemini functionDeclarations, and loop until there are no more tool calls.

functions.name: @apple-health
functions.what: Reads recent activity, workouts, sleep, and other Health metrics.
functions.macos_build: Health data generally isn't available on the Mac. Check HKHealthStore.isHealthDataAvailable(), which has returned false on macOS. A real version needs an iOS companion that syncs data via CloudKit.

functions.name: @browser
functions.what: Reads and reasons about the open browser page.
functions.macos_build: NSAppleScript to Safari and Chromium browsers for title, URL, and innerText. Raycast uses its Browser Companion extension. The alternative is your own WebExtension with a native-messaging host.

functions.name: @calculator
functions.what: Math, unit and currency conversion, and date calculations as a tool.
functions.macos_build: A custom expression parser (avoid NSExpression on untrusted input), Foundation Measurement and UnitConverter for units, Calendar.date(byAdding:) for dates, and an ECB or Frankfurter API for currency rates.

functions.name: @calendar
functions.what: Reports your schedule, free slots, and upcoming events.
functions.macos_build: EventKit: EKEventStore().requestFullAccessToEvents() (macOS 14+), then events(matching: predicateForEvents(withStart:end:calendars:)). Find free slots by scanning gaps.

functions.name: @clipboard
functions.what: Searches clipboard history by text or category, reads an entry, or replaces an entry's text.
functions.macos_build: Needs a clipboard history store: poll NSPasteboard.general.changeCount about every 0.5 s, store items in SQLite with type and source app, and skip concealed or transient types (org.nspasteboard.ConcealedType).

functions.name: @file-search
functions.what: Finds files across indexed folders.
functions.macos_build: Reuse DigUp's FTS5 and EmbeddingGemma semantic index (Searcher.swift). Add NSMetadataQuery for Spotlight name search.
functions.permission: none (Full Disk Access for protected folders)

functions.name: @finder
functions.what: Searches and manages files and folders: move, rename, create, trash.
functions.macos_build: FileManager moveItem, createDirectory, and trashItem. NSWorkspace for open and reveal. Get the Finder selection via NSAppleScript 'tell application "Finder" to get selection as alias list'.
functions.permission: Automation (Finder), Full Disk Access for protected paths

functions.name: @raycast-focus
functions.what: Starts, completes, or pauses Focus sessions and reports past session activity.
functions.macos_build: Expose the Focus module's API as tools, backed by a session-history table.

functions.name: @location
functions.what: Answers 'what's nearby?' questions.
functions.macos_build: CLLocationManager (requestWhenInUseAuthorization) plus MKLocalSearch or MKLocalPointsOfInterestRequest.

functions.name: @manual
functions.what: Answers questions about the app from its documentation.
functions.macos_build: RAG over bundled docs, embedded with the existing EmbeddingGemma runtime.

functions.name: @memory
functions.what: Recalls earlier AI chat discussions and decisions.
functions.macos_build: Hybrid FTS5 and embedding search over the chat history tables.

functions.name: @raycast-notes
functions.what: Creates, reads, and searches notes.
functions.macos_build: Expose the Notes DB as tools.

functions.name: @quicklinks
functions.what: Creates, searches, and opens Quicklinks.
functions.macos_build: Expose the Quicklinks store. Open with NSWorkspace.shared.open(url).

functions.name: @reminders
functions.what: Creates, searches, and completes Apple Reminders.
functions.macos_build: EventKit: requestFullAccessToReminders(), fetchReminders(matching: predicateForIncompleteReminders(…)), EKReminder save, and isCompleted=true.

functions.name: @screen-awareness
functions.what: Lets the model look at the frontmost app's content, selection, and window screenshot when it decides to.
functions.macos_build: Wrap the Screen Awareness capture as a tool.

functions.name: @selected-text
functions.what: Pulls in text highlighted in another app.
functions.macos_build: AX kAXSelectedTextAttribute on the focused element.

functions.name: @snippets
functions.what: Creates, searches, and manages snippets.
functions.macos_build: Expose the snippets store.

functions.name: @terminal
functions.what: Runs shell commands and reasons about their output.
functions.macos_build: Process with /bin/zsh -lc, Pipe capture, a timeout, and a working directory.

functions.name: @weather
functions.what: Answers weather questions.
functions.macos_build: WeatherKit WeatherService.shared.weather(for: CLLocation), which needs the WeatherKit capability and an Apple Developer account, or the free Open-Meteo REST API.

functions.name: @automations
functions.what: Lists, creates, updates, and deletes automations from chat.
functions.macos_build: Expose the Automations store as tools, with a confirmation card before saving.

functions.name: @raycast-feedback / Ask Feedback
functions.what: Files bug reports, feature requests, or support questions after confirming with you.
functions.macos_build: Map to a prefilled GitHub issue URL or a mailto: link.

functions.name: Ask Manual / Open Manual
functions.what: Root commands that ask questions about the manual or open it.
functions.macos_build: Quick AI prefilled with @manual, and NSWorkspace.open on the docs URL.

functions.name: Permission modes: Ask / Auto / Always Allow
functions.what: A global policy for tool calls. Ask prompts for anything not read-only. Auto approves read-only tools, edits inside the working directory, and everyday shell commands, but always asks before reading credentials or doing anything destructive. Always Allow runs everything.
functions.macos_build: Tool metadata flags plus a classifier for shell commands (allowlist of commands like ls, cat, git status; deny patterns for .env, ~/.ssh, rm -rf). Store the policy in UserDefaults.

functions.name: Auto-review Rules & Globally Allowed Tools
functions.what: Pairs specific actions with 'Allow automatically' or 'Ask first'. The allow list can be viewed and Reset All clears it.
functions.macos_build: A rules table matched before the default policy.

functions.name: Approval card
functions.what: Describes a pending tool action, with Show Command for shell commands, and offers Allow, Always Allow, or Deny. Allow All and Deny All handle several pending calls.
functions.macos_build: An inline SwiftUI card that suspends the tool loop with a CheckedContinuation.

functions.name: Per-chat permission override
functions.what: Change Permissions… sets a per-chat policy or inherits the global one.
functions.macos_build: A nullable policy column on the conversation.

functions.name: Per-extension Custom Instructions
functions.what: Free text on an extension's Ask tool that steers how the AI uses it.
functions.macos_build: Append to the tool description or system prompt.

functions.name: Store AI Extensions filter
functions.what: Filters the Store to extensions that include AI tools.
functions.macos_build: Not replicable, since it depends on the Raycast Store. Show installed MCP servers instead.

notes: Servers bundled with Store extensions and Raycast's curated OAuth client registrations are Raycast-specific. iOS supports only HTTP servers. The official Swift SDK (github.com/modelcontextprotocol/swift-sdk) covers the client side. The page does not describe importing a Claude Desktop config, raw JSON editing, or legacy SSE.

functions.name: Install MCP Server
functions.what: A form for name and icon, transport, connection details, custom instructions, and description. Saving connects to the server and loads its tools.
functions.macos_build: SwiftUI Form. Persist to JSON in Application Support, with secrets in the Keychain.

functions.name: stdio transport

Walk kAXChildrenAttribute collecting kAXValue, kAXTitle, and kAXDescription with depth and character caps, skipping AXSecureTextField. notes: Raycast transcribes in the cloud (audio is not retained), and Report a Problem, organization-shared Styles, and Style sync are cloud features. The iOS Raycast Keyboard dictation does not apply to a Mac app. A local version can use SpeechAnalyzer/SpeechTranscriber (macOS 26, on-device) or whisper.cpp built on the ggml that DigUp already vendors, with a local LLM pass for cleanup. The page does not say whether Raycast transcribes on-device or in the cloud.

functions.macos_build: Added to the cleanup prompt.

functions.name: Application search and launch
functions.what: Type part of an app's name in the root search bar. Enter opens the app, or brings it to the front if it is already running.
functions.macos_build: Build the app catalog with NSMetadataQuery (predicate kMDItemContentType == 'com.apple.application-bundle', scopes /Applications, /System/Applications, /System/Applications/Utilities, ~/Applications, /System/Library/CoreServices) and keep it live through NSMetadataQueryDidUpdate. Names come from kMDItemDisplayName plus localized CFBundleDisplayName/CFBundleName. Icons come from NSWorkspace.shared.icon(forFile:), cached. Launch with NSWorkspace.shared.openApplication(at:configuration:) (activates if already running). Get running state from NSWorkspace.shared.runningApplications, refreshed on didLaunch/didTerminate notifications.

functions.name: Fuzzy matching with acronyms and alternate names

functions.macos_build: Write your own subsequence scorer (fzf-style) with bonuses for word starts, camelCase humps, consecutive runs and prefix matches. Also match against kMDItemAlternateNames and kMDItemKeywords from Spotlight metadata, plus a small built-in synonym table (e.g. Preferences maps to System Settings). Run in-memory over a few thousand items on each keystroke, debounced to about 10 ms.

functions.name: Frecency ranking with learned query associations
functions.what: Items you choose often and recently rise for the queries you typed when choosing them. Exact alias matches rank first, then alias prefixes, then fuzzy title score, then subtitle/keyword matches, then frecency.
functions.macos_build: Add SQLite tables (DigUp already ships SQLite): usage(item_id, count, last_used) and query_assoc(query_prefix, item_id, count, last_used). Score with exponential time decay (e.g. half-life of a week), combined lexicographically with match tier. Update on every launch from the panel.

functions.name: Reset Ranking
functions.what: Clears the learned usage history and remembered search terms for one command, so it ranks only on text match again.
functions.macos_build: Action Panel action that deletes rows for item_id from the usage and query_assoc tables.

functions.name: Root Search Sensitivity
functions.what: A Low/Medium/High setting that trades breadth against precision. Low shows anything containing the letters, High shows only close matches.
functions.macos_build: Minimum fuzzy-score threshold stored in UserDefaults and applied before ranking.

Pass values to the command handler. Manage focus with makeFirstResponder.

functions.what: In form views, ⌘Enter submits, Tab and Shift+Tab move between fields, and Esc cancels.
functions.macos_build: Set NSView nextKeyView chain. Submit via key equivalent on the default button.

notes: Fully local. The manual is inconsistent about a few shortcuts (Add to Favorites ⌘F vs ⇧⌘F, Disable Command ⇧⌘D vs ⌃⇧⌘D, Configure Extension), so pick one scheme and keep it consistent.

functions.name: Launcher hotkey
functions.what: Global shortcut that shows or hides the launcher. The default is ⌥Space, and it can take over ⌘Space once Spotlight's shortcut is turned off.
functions.macos_build: Carbon RegisterEventHotKey + InstallEventHandler(kEventHotKeyPressed), which DigUp's Hotkey.swift already does (default ⇧⌘Space). If ⌘Space is taken, RegisterEventHotKey returns eventHotKeyExistsErr, so tell the user to disable Spotlight in System Settings › Keyboard Shortcuts (AppleSymbolicHotKeys id 64).

functions.name: Command aliases
functions.what: Short lowercase keywords (letters, digits and spaces, possibly several words) that push a command to the top. An exact match beats a prefix match, the alias shows as a badge, and alias + Space jumps into the command's arguments.
functions.macos_build: Dictionary alias → item ID in SQLite/UserDefaults. Lowercase on input and validate with the regex ^[a-z0-9 ]+$. Exact and prefix tiers feed the ranking function.

functions.name: Per-command global hotkeys (standard combos)
functions.what: Any command, app, quicklink or script can get a global shortcut that runs it even when the launcher is hidden.
functions.macos_build: One Carbon RegisterEventHotKey per binding, with an EventHotKeyID carrying an index into the command table. These work without TCC permission and still fire under Secure Input.

functions.name: Modifier-only, double-tap and side-specific hotkeys
functions.what: Supports hotkeys made only of modifiers (⌥⌘), double taps (⌘⌘), single taps of one side (Right ⌘), and both sides held together (L⌘ R⌘). Left and right sides can be distinguished or treated as the same.
functions.macos_build: Listen-only CGEventTap (CGEvent.tapCreate with .listenOnly) for .flagsChanged. Identify sides by keyCode (54/55 ⌘, 56/60 ⇧, 58/61 ⌥, 59/62 ⌃, 63 fn) or NX_DEVICE*KEYMASK bits in flags. Implement a state machine with a ~300 ms double-tap window that cancels if any non-modifier key goes down in between.

functions.name: fn / Globe key and F13–F18 single-key hotkeys
functions.what: The fn key alone, or an extended-keyboard key like F13, can be a hotkey. fn requires setting macOS 'Press fn key to' to Do Nothing.
functions.macos_build: F13–F18: RegisterEventHotKey with zero modifiers. fn: watch the flagsChanged keyCode 63 / .maskSecondaryFn in the event tap.

functions.name: Hotkey recorder with conflict detection
functions.what: Shows keys live as you press them and saves after about 1.5 s or on Enter. Conflicts are shown in red with the conflicting command's name, and you can overwrite a binding from another command. Backspace or ✕ clears.
functions.macos_build: Recorder NSView that becomes first responder and captures keyDown/flagsChanged via a local monitor while focused. Check conflicts against your own registry, against macOS symbolic hotkeys read via CFPreferencesCopyAppValue('AppleSymbolicHotKeys', 'com.apple.symbolichotkeys'), and against eventHotKeyExistsErr from a trial RegisterEventHotKey.

functions.name: Physical key vs key equivalent (international layouts)
functions.what: A hotkey can follow the physical key position, or the character it produces on the current layout.
functions.macos_build: Translate between keyCode and character with UCKeyTranslate using TISCopyCurrentKeyboardLayoutInputSource → kTISPropertyUnicodeKeyLayoutData. Re-register on the kTISNotifySelectedKeyboardInputSourceChanged distributed notification.

functions.name: Shortcuts overview in Settings
functions.what: One table of every command with its alias and hotkey, editable inline. You can search it and filter by category (Applications, Extensions, Quicklinks, System) or by status (Hotkey Set, Alias Set, Enabled, Disabled).
functions.macos_build: SwiftUI Table or NSTableView bound to the command registry, with an embedded recorder cell and alias text cell.

notes: Fully local. Modifier-only and double-tap hotkeys can't be built with Carbon hotkeys alone and need an event tap. Hotkey and alias settings sync only through Raycast Cloud Sync (Pro).

functions.name: Remap a key to Hyper (⌃⌥⌘)
functions.what: Turns Caps Lock, one side of a modifier, or F1–F12 into a key that sends ⌃⌥⌘ together, so you get a whole namespace of shortcuts that collide with nothing.
functions.macos_build: Remap the physical key with `hidutil property --set '{"UserKeyMapping":[{"HIDKeyboardModifierMappingSrc":0x700000039,"HIDKeyboardModifierMappingDst":0x70000006D}]}'` (Caps Lock to F18; runs as the user, reset at reboot, so reapply at launch and clear on quit). Then an active CGEventTap tracks F18 down/up and ORs .maskControl|.maskAlternate|.maskCommand into the flags of other key events while it is held. Alternatively map directly to Right Control and synthesize the extra modifiers.

functions.name: Include Shift
functions.what: Optionally adds ⇧ so Hyper sends ⌃⌥⇧⌘.
functions.macos_build: Add .maskShift to the injected flags.

functions.name: Quick press action
functions.what: For Caps Lock or F-key sources, a lone tap can do nothing, send the original key (real Caps Lock), or send Escape.
functions.macos_build: In the tap, if down→up happens with no other key in between and under ~200 ms, post a kVK_Escape keyDown/keyUp via CGEvent.post(tap: .cghidEventTap). For real Caps Lock, toggle the lock with IOHIDSetModifierLockState(connect, kIOHIDCapsLockState, !state) on an IOServiceOpen'd IOHIDSystem connection.

functions.name: Secure Input compatibility
functions.what: Keeps Hyper shortcuts working while another app holds Secure Input (e.g. a password field). In this mode Right Control is reserved for Hyper.
functions.macos_build: Event taps go blind under Secure Input, but Carbon RegisterEventHotKey does not. So map Caps Lock → Right Control (HID 0x7000000E4) with hidutil and register Hyper shortcuts as real ⌃⌥⌘ Carbon hotkeys. Detect the state with IsSecureEventInputEnabled(), and find the holding process via the kCGSSessionSecureInputPID key in `ioreg -l -w 0`.

functions.name: Hyper glyph display
functions.what: Shows ⌃⌥⌘ combos as ✦ throughout the UI.
functions.macos_build: String formatting in the shortcut renderer.

functions.name: Per-keyboard mapping and diagnostics panel
functions.what: Applies the mapping to each connected keyboard, skips keyboards that can't be remapped (such as Universal Control), restores Caps Lock when turned off, and offers a diagnostic panel that shows status and conflicts and can restart Hyper.
functions.macos_build: Enumerate keyboards with IOHIDManager (kHIDUsage_GD_Keyboard). Apply per device with `hidutil property --matching '{"ProductID":…,"VendorID":…}' --set …`. Watch for hot-plug with IOHIDManagerRegisterDeviceMatchingCallback. Flag Karabiner's virtual HID device as a conflict.

notes: Fully local. hidutil user key mappings don't survive a reboot or logout, so the app must reapply them at launch and remove them on quit or crash (e.g. a watchdog or a LaunchAgent cleanup).

functions.name: Open Application
functions.what: Launches the app, or brings it forward if it is already running.
functions.macos_build: NSWorkspace.shared.openApplication(at:configuration: .init(activates: true)).

functions.name: New Application Window
functions.what: Opens a fresh window of the app instead of just activating it.
functions.macos_build: Activate the app (NSRunningApplication.activate()), then post ⌘N with CGEvent keyboard events to .cghidEventTap. Or send the AppleEvent kAEReopenApplication ('rapp') via NSAppleEventDescriptor, which many apps answer by opening a window if none is open.

functions.name: Open Recent Files…
functions.what: Lists the documents the app opened recently so you can reopen one.
functions.macos_build: There's no public API for other apps' recent lists. Options: parse ~/Library/Application Support/com.apple.sharedfilelist/com.apple.LSSharedFileList.ApplicationRecentDocuments/<bundleid>.sfl3 (NSKeyedArchiver bookmark data, undocumented and may need Full Disk Access), or query Spotlight for kMDItemLastUsedDate on files whose content types the app declares in CFBundleDocumentTypes. Open with NSWorkspace.open([url], withApplicationAt:).
functions.permission: Full Disk Access (sfl3 route) or none (Spotlight route)

functions.name: Show in Finder
functions.what: Reveals the .app bundle in Finder.
functions.macos_build: NSWorkspace.shared.activateFileViewerSelecting([appURL]).

functions.name: Show Info in Finder
functions.what: Opens Finder's Get Info window for the app.
functions.macos_build: AppleScript/NSAppleScript: tell application "Finder" to open information window of (POSIX file path as alias).

functions.name: Show Package Contents
functions.what: Opens the inside of the app bundle in Finder.
functions.macos_build: NSWorkspace.shared.open(appURL.appendingPathComponent("Contents")).

functions.name: Copy Path / Copy Name / Copy Bundle Identifier
functions.what: Copies the app's file path, display name or bundle ID.
functions.macos_build: Bundle(url:)?.bundleIdentifier, FileManager.displayName(atPath:), NSPasteboard.general.setString.

functions.name: Hide Application
functions.what: Hides all of the app's windows.
functions.macos_build: NSRunningApplication.hide().

functions.name: Quit Application
functions.what: Asks the app to quit normally.
functions.macos_build: NSRunningApplication.terminate().

functions.name: Force Quit Application
functions.what: Kills an unresponsive app.
functions.macos_build: NSRunningApplication.forceTerminate().

functions.name: Restart Application
functions.what: Quits the app and launches it again.
functions.macos_build: terminate(), observe isTerminated via KVO or NSWorkspace.didTerminateApplicationNotification, then openApplication(at:).

functions.name: Uninstall Application / Uninstall Applications
functions.what: Browse installed apps and remove one, including leftover support files.
functions.macos_build: Move the bundle to the Trash with NSWorkspace.shared.recycle([url]) or FileManager.trashItem. Root-owned App Store apps need authorization, so fall back to an AppleScript 'tell Finder to delete' that triggers the admin prompt. Optionally find leftovers in ~/Library/{Application Support,Caches,Preferences,Containers,Group Containers,Saved Application State,HTTPStorages} that match the bundle ID.
functions.permission: Full Disk Access (for Containers leftovers); admin prompt for root-owned apps

functions.name: Per-app hotkey with Toggle Visibility or Always Show
functions.what: A global hotkey per app that either toggles it (activate if hidden or background, hide if frontmost) or always brings it forward.
functions.macos_build: Carbon hotkey. Handler: if NSWorkspace.frontmostApplication == app then app.hide() else openApplication/activate.

functions.name: Application search scopes and Deep Search
functions.what: Adds or removes folders scanned for apps. Deep Search looks up to three levels into added folders.
functions.macos_build: Configurable NSMetadataQuery.searchScopes, or a FileManager.enumerator with a depth limit filtering .app bundles.

functions.name: Hide app from root search
functions.what: Per-app checkbox that keeps an app out of results.
functions.macos_build: Add the bundle ID to the disabled set.

notes: All local. Run as Administrator, Run as Different User and Show Advanced Options are Windows-only.

functions.name: Enable / Disable Auto Quit for an app
functions.what: Marks an app to be quit automatically after it has sat in the background unused for a while.
functions.macos_build: Store a set of bundle IDs with optional per-app timeouts in UserDefaults.

functions.name: Inactivity timer with default duration
functions.what: A timer starts when the app leaves the foreground and resets whenever it becomes frontmost. The default is 3 minutes, with options of 1/3/5/10/15 minutes, and apps can override it.
functions.macos_build: Observe NSWorkspace.didActivateApplicationNotification / didDeactivateApplicationNotification / didHideApplicationNotification. Run a per-app DispatchSourceTimer that calls NSRunningApplication.terminate() on expiry. Never quit Finder or yourself.

functions.name: Skip while recording or playing media
functions.what: Postpones quitting while the system is capturing audio/video or while Spotify/Music is playing.
functions.macos_build: Mic/camera in use: CoreAudio kAudioDevicePropertyDeviceIsRunningSomewhere on input devices; for camera, CoreMediaIO kCMIODevicePropertyDeviceIsRunningSomewhere. Media: ask Music/Spotify `player state` via AppleScript, or listen for distributed notifications com.apple.Music.playerInfo and com.spotify.client.PlaybackStateChanged.

functions.name: Manage Auto Quits
functions.what: Command that opens the Auto Quit list to add or remove apps and set timeouts.
functions.macos_build: Settings pane or list view bound to the store.

notes: Local. The 'Quit Apps Closed to Tray' option is Windows-only. The manual doesn't cover unsaved documents, but terminate() lets apps show their own save prompts.

feature: Navigation: Switch Windows and Search Menu Bar Items

functions.name: Switch Windows
functions.what: Searchable list of every open window across apps, showing title and app name. Enter brings that window forward, and the list updates live.
functions.macos_build: Enumerate NSWorkspace.runningApplications (.regular), then AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid) → kAXWindowsAttribute → kAXTitleAttribute. Raise with AXUIElementPerformAction(win, kAXRaiseAction) + NSRunningApplication.activate(). AX only lists windows on the current Space for most apps, so add CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo(.optionAll) for other Spaces. Reading kCGWindowName from that list requires Screen Recording. Mapping AX elements to CGWindowID uses the private _AXUIElementGetWindow.
functions.permission: Accessibility (+ Screen Recording for titles of windows on other Spaces)

functions.name: Window actions: Minimize, Close, Enter Fullscreen, Hide Application
functions.what: Acts on the selected window from the switcher.
functions.macos_build: Set kAXMinimizedAttribute true. Press the kAXCloseButtonAttribute element with kAXPressAction. Set the "AXFullScreen" attribute to true. NSRunningApplication.hide().

functions.name: Search Menu Bar Items
functions.what: Flattens every menu command of the frontmost app into one searchable list (e.g. 'Export as PDF') and runs the chosen one. Enabled and disabled states are kept.
functions.macos_build: AXUIElementCreateApplication(frontmost pid) → kAXMenuBarAttribute, then walk kAXChildrenAttribute recursively, collecting AXMenuItem kAXTitleAttribute, kAXEnabledAttribute, kAXMenuItemCmdCharAttribute and kAXMenuItemCmdModifiersAttribute (to show shortcuts) and the parent path. Execute with AXUIElementPerformAction(item, kAXPressAction). Cache per app with a short TTL, since the walk can take 100–500 ms.

notes: Local. Capture the frontmost app before the launcher panel takes focus (non-activating NSPanel or record NSWorkspace.frontmostApplication at hotkey time).

functions.name: Clipboard capture (text, images, files, links, emails, colors)
functions.what: Records everything you copy, keeps every original pasteboard format, and groups multi-item copies into one entry.
functions.macos_build: Poll NSPasteboard.general.changeCount on a ~0.3–0.5 s timer (there is no change notification). On change, snapshot every NSPasteboardItem and type (pasteboardItems → types → data(forType:)). Classify: public.file-url → files, public.png/public.tiff → image, a URL string → link, an email regex → email, a hex/rgb string → color. Record the source app from NSWorkspace.shared.frontmostApplication. Store in SQLite with blobs on disk. On macOS 26+, check NSPasteboard.general.accessBehavior and guide the user to allow 'Paste from Other Apps' for your app.
functions.permission: Pasteboard privacy approval on macOS 26+ (reading changeCount is free; reading contents may prompt)

functions.name: Ignore passwords, transient data and disabled apps
functions.what: Skips concealed or transient items (password managers) and anything copied from apps on a block list (Passwords and Keychain Access by default).
functions.macos_build: Skip if types contain org.nspasteboard.ConcealedType, org.nspasteboard.TransientType, org.nspasteboard.AutoGeneratedType, com.agilebits.onepassword or de.petermaurer.TransientPasteboardType, or if the source bundle ID is in the user's disabled list (default com.apple.Passwords, com.apple.keychainaccess).

functions.name: Browse and search history with detail pane
functions.what: Type to filter entries, with a right-hand pane showing the full content and metadata (source app, time, size, dimensions). Text recognized in images is searchable too.
functions.macos_build: SQLite FTS5 over text and OCR text (DigUp already compiles FTS5). Split view with an NSTableView list and a preview (NSTextView / NSImageView / QLPreviewView).

functions.name: Filter by type
functions.what: Narrows the list to Text, Images, Files, Links, Emails or Colors.
functions.macos_build: Dropdown (NSPopUpButton) adding a WHERE kind = ? clause.

functions.name: Paste to active app
functions.what: Puts the entry back on the clipboard and pastes it into the app you were using.
functions.macos_build: Write all saved types back with NSPasteboard.clearContents() + setData(_:forType:). Hide the panel and reactivate the previous app. Post ⌘V via CGEvent(keyboardEventSource:virtualKey: kVK_ANSI_V, keyDown:) with .maskCommand to .cghidEventTap.

functions.name: Copy to Clipboard
functions.what: Restores the entry to the clipboard without pasting.
functions.macos_build: NSPasteboard write only.

functions.name: Paste as Plain Text / Prefer plain text
functions.what: Pastes only the string flavor and drops formatting. A setting can make this the default.
functions.macos_build: Write only .string, then ⌘V.

functions.name: Paste as PNG
functions.what: Converts TIFF-only images to PNG before pasting, for apps that reject TIFF.
functions.macos_build: NSBitmapImageRep(data:)?.representation(using: .png, properties: [:]) and write as .png.

functions.name: Open link in browser
functions.what: Opens a link entry in the default browser.
functions.macos_build: NSWorkspace.shared.open(url).

functions.name: Pin / unpin entry
functions.what: Keeps an entry at the top and protects it from pruning and from clear-all.
functions.macos_build: pinned flag and sort key in SQLite. Retention and delete-all queries skip pinned rows.

functions.name: Rename entry
functions.what: Gives an entry a custom title.
functions.macos_build: title column.

functions.name: Edit content
functions.what: Edits the text, link or color of an entry in place.
functions.macos_build: Form view with NSTextView, then update the row.

functions.name: Save as Snippet
functions.what: Turns a clipboard entry into a reusable snippet.
functions.macos_build: Prefill the Create Snippet form.

functions.name: Copy Text from Image (OCR)
functions.what: Extracts text from an image entry on-device and copies it.
functions.macos_build: Vision VNRecognizeTextRequest (recognitionLevel .accurate, usesLanguageCorrection) via VNImageRequestHandler(cgImage:). On macOS 26, RecognizeDocumentsRequest is also available.

functions.name: Text Recognition indexing (Fast / Accurate)
functions.what: Runs OCR on every copied image in the background so you can search by text inside images. Fast mode uses less CPU and Accurate catches small or low-contrast text.
functions.macos_build: Background OperationQueue running VNRecognizeTextRequest with .fast or .accurate, saving the result into the FTS table. DigUp's extractor pipeline already OCRs screenshots.

functions.name: Copy Text from QR Code
functions.what: Decodes a QR code in an image entry and copies its payload.
functions.macos_build: Vision VNDetectBarcodesRequest (symbologies [.qr]) → payloadStringValue.

functions.name: Share…
functions.what: Sends text, links, images or files through the macOS share sheet.
functions.macos_build: NSSharingServicePicker(items:).show(relativeTo:of:preferredEdge:).

functions.name: Send / Attach to AI Chat
functions.what: Hands an entry to the AI chat as context.
functions.macos_build: Pass the content into the local LLM chat (see AI feature).

functions.name: Delete entry / Delete entries in time window / Delete all
functions.what: Removes one entry, everything from the last 5/15/30 min or 1/24 h, or the whole unpinned history.
functions.macos_build: SQL DELETE with time predicates and blob cleanup. Confirm with NSAlert.

functions.name: Paste Sequentially
functions.what: Each press pastes the next older entry, so you can paste a run of items in order. The sequence resets after a timeout (default 30 s) or a new copy, and can add a newline after each paste.
functions.macos_build: Global Carbon hotkey. A cursor index into history resets on a changeCount change or timer. Each press writes entry[i] and posts ⌘V, plus Return if the newline option is on.

functions.name: Reset Paste Sequence
functions.what: Moves the sequence cursor back to the newest entry and shows a 'Paste sequence reset' HUD.
functions.macos_build: Reset the index and show a transient HUD NSPanel.

functions.name: Retention period
functions.what: How long history is kept: 1 day, 1 week, 1 month or 3 months (free), and 6 months, 1 year or unlimited (Pro).
functions.macos_build: Periodic DELETE WHERE created < now - retention AND pinned = 0.

functions.name: Encrypted local storage
functions.what: History is encrypted at rest on disk.
functions.macos_build: CryptoKit AES.GCM per blob/row, with a SymmetricKey stored in the Keychain (SecItemAdd kSecClassGenericPassword, kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly). Alternatively, rely on FileVault plus file protection.

functions.name: Universal Clipboard: save immediately
functions.what: Optionally records items arriving from iPhone/iPad as soon as they arrive, not only after you paste them.
functions.macos_build: Handoff pasteboard items appear as a changeCount bump with com.apple.is-remote-clipboard in the types. Reading the data forces the download, so do it only when the option is on.

functions.name: Link visual previews
functions.what: Fetches favicons and social-card images for link entries.
functions.macos_build: LinkPresentation LPMetadataProvider.startFetchingMetadata(for:) → iconProvider/imageProvider. Cache the results.

functions.name: Move used item to top
functions.what: Optionally bumps an entry to the top after you paste or copy it.
functions.macos_build: Update last_used and sort by it.

functions.name: Ask Clipboard (AI extension)
functions.what: Natural-language questions over history, e.g. 'the tracking number I copied yesterday', which can read entries and rewrite one.
functions.macos_build: Expose search, read and update over the SQLite store as tools to a local LLM (FoundationModels Tool protocol or llama.cpp function calling). Use EmbeddingGemma embeddings of entries for semantic retrieval.

notes: Clipboard history is never cloud-synced by Raycast. Raycast offers retention beyond 3 months only with Pro. Ask Clipboard uses Raycast AI (cloud, Pro), but a local LLM plus DigUp's embeddings can replace it. The v1 manual mentions a per-entry text cap of 32,768 characters.

functions.name: Create Snippet
functions.what: Form for a new snippet: name, text (up to 65K characters, with dynamic placeholders), optional keyword for auto-expansion, and tags.
functions.macos_build: Form view writing to a SQLite snippets table (id, name, text, keyword UNIQUE, tags, pinned). Validate the keyword: no whitespace, quotes or backticks.

functions.name: Search Snippets
functions.what: Finds snippets by name, keyword or content, filters by tag, and pastes or copies the chosen one. Snippets can also be pinned, edited, duplicated and deleted.
functions.keys: ↵ paste (configurable primary action); ⌘↵ copy; ⌘. pin; ⌘E edit; ⌘D duplicate; ⌃X delete; tag dropdown
functions.macos_build: FTS5 search plus a tag filter. Expand placeholders, then paste via pasteboard + synthetic ⌘V, restoring the previous clipboard afterwards.

functions.name: Keyword auto-expansion in any app
functions.what: Typing a snippet keyword anywhere (browser, editor, chat) replaces it with the snippet text.
functions.macos_build: CGEventTap on .keyDown. Read typed characters with event.keyboardGetUnicodeString and keep a rolling buffer (cap = longest keyword). Reset it on mouse down, arrows, ⌘ shortcuts and app switches. On a suffix match: post N × Backspace (kVK_Delete), save the clipboard, write the expanded text, post ⌘V, restore the clipboard after ~150 ms. Use CGEvent.keyboardSetUnicodeString for very short outputs. Skip when IsSecureEventInputEnabled().

functions.name: Expansion mode: immediate vs after delimiter (keep/discard)
functions.what: Expand as soon as the keyword matches, or only after a delimiter such as space or punctuation, either keeping or removing that delimiter.
functions.macos_build: Matcher state machine. In delimiter modes, wait for a word-boundary character, then delete keyword + delimiter and re-type the delimiter if kept.

functions.name: Expand within words
functions.what: When off, a keyword only fires as a standalone word, not inside a longer word.
functions.macos_build: Check that the character before the match is a boundary (whitespace/punctuation) or the buffer start.

functions.name: Override System Snippets (experimental)
functions.what: Expands before macOS's own text replacements when keywords conflict, or skips conflicting keywords.
functions.macos_build: Read the user's text replacements (NSUserDictionaryReplacementItems in the global domain via CFPreferencesCopyAppValue) to detect conflicts. Override means acting on keyDown before the app's NSSpellChecker substitution runs.

functions.name: Injection Delay and Response Time tuning
functions.what: Adjusts how long to wait between deleting the keyword, pasting and restoring the clipboard (None to Extra Long / Instant to Extended), for fast typists and slow apps.
functions.macos_build: Configurable usleep/DispatchQueue delays between the backspace burst, the paste and the clipboard restore.

functions.name: Enable Snippet Expansion master toggle and completion sound
functions.what: Turns auto-expansion off without removing snippets, and can play a sound on each expansion.
functions.macos_build: Enable/disable the CGEventTap (CGEvent.tapEnable). NSSound(named:)?.play().

functions.name: Disabled applications for expansion
functions.what: Blocks expansion in chosen apps (1Password and Keychain Access are listed by default).
functions.macos_build: Check NSWorkspace.shared.frontmostApplication?.bundleIdentifier against a set.

functions.name: Cursor placement after expansion
functions.what: The {cursor} placeholder puts the caret at a chosen spot in the expanded text.
functions.macos_build: After pasting, post kVK_LeftArrow × (characters after the cursor marker).

functions.name: Import Snippets
functions.what: Imports from a JSON array ({name, text, keyword}) or from TextExpander, aText, Espanso or PhraseExpress exports. Duplicates are skipped and the counts are reported.
functions.macos_build: NSOpenPanel + JSONDecoder. TextExpander .textexpander is a plist (PropertyListSerialization). Espanso match/*.yml needs a YAML parser (e.g. Yams). aText CSV. Dedupe on name+text(+keyword).

functions.name: Export Snippets
functions.what: Saves all snippets to a JSON file for backup or sharing.
functions.macos_build: JSONEncoder + NSSavePanel.

functions.name: Tags
functions.what: Group snippets with one or more tags and filter by them.
functions.macos_build: tags table with a many-to-many link, plus a token field in the editor.

functions.name: Delete confirmation
functions.what: Optional warning before deleting a snippet (on by default).
functions.macos_build: NSAlert gated by a setting.

notes: Shared Snippets require Raycast for Teams (cloud, team server), so they can't be replicated locally; a shared folder or Git repo of JSON could stand in. Snippet sync is Cloud Sync (Pro). Clipboard-based injection loses rich text unless you also write .rtf/.html types.

functions.name: {clipboard} and {clipboard offset=N}
functions.what: Inserts the current clipboard text, or an older clipboard history entry (offset=1 is the second newest).
functions.macos_build: NSPasteboard.general.string(forType: .string). Offsets read from the clipboard-history store.

functions.name: {snippet name="…"}
functions.what: Embeds another snippet's text, one level deep only.
functions.macos_build: Look up by name and expand without recursion.

functions.name: {cursor}
functions.what: Marks where the caret ends up after the snippet is inserted (one per snippet).
functions.macos_build: Strip the marker, count the trailing characters, then post that many left-arrow keys after pasting.

functions.name: {date} {time} {datetime} {day} with offset, format, locale
functions.what: Inserts the current date, time, both, or weekday. Supports offsets like +2y +5M, -3d, +3h +30m, custom formats like yyyy-MM-dd, and locales like fr-FR or en-US-u-hc-h23.
functions.macos_build: Calendar.current.date(byAdding:) per offset token (m, h, d, M, y). DateFormatter with dateFormat (ICU pattern) or locale + dateStyle/timeStyle. Locale(identifier:) supports -u-hc-h23 extensions.

functions.name: {uuid}
functions.what: Inserts a fresh unique identifier.
functions.macos_build: UUID().uuidString.

functions.name: {selection}
functions.what: Inserts the text selected in the frontmost app (used in quicklinks and AI commands).
functions.macos_build: AXUIElementCreateSystemWide() → kAXFocusedUIElementAttribute → kAXSelectedTextAttribute. If that fails (Electron/web views), save the pasteboard, post ⌘C, read it, then restore.

functions.name: {argument name default options}

functions.name: {calculator}
functions.what: Evaluates a math expression inside the template and inserts the result.
functions.macos_build: Call the calculator engine.

functions.name: {browser-tab format selector}
functions.what: Inserts the active browser tab's content as markdown, text or HTML, optionally only the part matching a CSS selector.
functions.macos_build: Apple Events: Safari `do JavaScript "document.querySelector(sel).innerText" in current tab of front window`. Chrome/Arc/Brave/Edge: `execute active tab of front window javascript "…"`. Both need the browser's 'Allow JavaScript from Apple Events' developer setting. Convert HTML to markdown in-app.

functions.name: Modifiers: uppercase, lowercase, trim, percent-encode, json-stringify, raw
functions.what: Pipe-chained transforms on any placeholder, e.g. {clipboard | trim | uppercase}. raw turns off the default per-context escaping (quicklinks percent-encode, AI prompts wrap values in triple quotes).
functions.macos_build: Small template parser: tokens of the form {name attr="…" | mod | mod}. String.uppercased(), trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines), addingPercentEncoding(withAllowedCharacters: .urlQueryAllowed minus &+=?), JSONEncoder for json-stringify.

functions.name: Inline arithmetic and natural-language math
functions.what: Type an expression in root search and the answer appears inline. Supports words like 'square root of 625' and '2 power 10', trig (incl. cot, csc), hyperbolic and inverse functions, and K/M shorthand like 10K or USD1K.
functions.macos_build: Raycast licenses SoulverCore, a commercial Swift framework that can be licensed. Otherwise write a recursive-descent parser over Double/Decimal with a function table and natural-language rewrites ('square root of x' → sqrt(x)). NSExpression is too limited for words and units. Number formatting via NumberFormatter with Locale.current (decimal and grouping separators follow System Settings › Language & Region).

functions.name: Percentages
functions.what: Phrases such as '52% of 900', '20% off 80', and percent added to a quantity ('19m + 47%').
functions.macos_build: Grammar rules in the parser.

functions.name: Unit conversion
functions.what: Length, volume, temperature, mass, data and more ('10ft in m', '3 teaspoon in ml', '23C to F'), plus design units ('2rem in px', '32px in rem', '2 inches in px at 72 ppi').
functions.macos_build: Foundation Measurement with Dimension subclasses (UnitLength, UnitVolume, UnitTemperature, UnitMass, UnitArea, UnitSpeed, UnitInformationStorage, UnitDuration…) and converted(to:). Alias table for unit words and abbreviations. Custom CSS units from a REM base setting (default 16) and a ppi factor.

functions.name: Currency conversion
functions.what: Converts between fiat currencies, including rates such as '8 dollars/hour in gbp'. Rates refresh in the background.
functions.macos_build: Fetch rates periodically, e.g. ECB daily XML https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/eurofxref/eurofxref-daily.xml (EUR base, about 30 currencies), and cache them for offline use. Recognize symbols and names via Locale.commonISOCurrencyCodes and Locale.localizedString(forCurrencyCode:).

functions.name: Cryptocurrency conversion
functions.what: Converts crypto to fiat, e.g. '5 btc in gbp'.
functions.macos_build: Price API such as CoinGecko /simple/price, cached with a TTL.

functions.name: Time zones and world clock
functions.what: 'time in tokyo', '5pm ldn in sf', 'time diff Paris', 'time in 4 hours in San Francisco' and 'time in brisbane + 4 hours', with DST handled. Places can be cities, airports (JFK) or landmarks.
functions.macos_build: Bundle a city/airport → IANA time zone table (GeoNames cities15000 + OurAirports IATA list) with nicknames (ldn, sf, nyc). Use TimeZone(identifier:) and Calendar with .timeZone set for arithmetic across DST. Format with DateFormatter.

functions.name: Date arithmetic and countdowns
functions.what: 'monday in 3 weeks', '35 days ago', 'days until 31 Mar', 'August 5 + 5' (days), '3:45pm + 5' (hours), and keywords now/today/tomorrow/yesterday.
functions.macos_build: NSDataDetector(types: .date) for absolute dates plus a custom grammar for relative phrases. Calendar.date(byAdding:) and Calendar.dateComponents([.day], from:to:).

functions.name: Durations and work time
functions.what: '145 mins to timespan' gives a readable duration. 'workhours in 2023' and '55h in workdays' compute working time.
functions.macos_build: DateComponentsFormatter (unitsStyle .full). Count work days by iterating Calendar and skipping weekends (holidays optional).

functions.name: ISO 8601 / timestamp parsing
functions.what: Pasting a Zulu timestamp like 2024-03-15T14:30:00Z shows it in local time.
functions.macos_build: ISO8601DateFormatter, plus Unix epoch detection for 10/13-digit numbers.

functions.name: Color conversion (Copy Color as…)
functions.what: Hex (3/4/6/8 digit), rgb(a), hsl(a), hwb, lab, lch, oklab and oklch inputs. Copy as Hex, Hex+Alpha, RGBA, RGBA %, RGB CSS4, HSL variants, HWB, Lab, LCH, Oklab, Oklch, NSColor or UIColor code.
functions.macos_build: Hand-written color-space math (sRGB ↔ linear ↔ XYZ D65 ↔ Lab/LCH and OKLab/OKLCH) with string formatters. Can be disabled in settings.

functions.name: Answer actions
functions.what: Copy the answer, paste it into the active app, copy the unformatted number, copy question and answer, or swap the question with the answer to keep calculating.
functions.keys: ↵ copy; ⌘↵ paste to active app; ⌥⌘C copy raw; ⌥⇧⌘C copy question + answer; ⌘⇧↵ swap question/answer
functions.macos_build: NSPasteboard + synthetic ⌘V. Swap rewrites the search field text.

functions.name: Calculator History
functions.what: Keeps past calculations so you can look them up and reuse them.
functions.macos_build: SQLite table of (expression, result, timestamp) written when an answer is copied or pasted, browsable as a list command.

functions.name: Calculator settings
functions.what: Syntax highlighting toggle, color conversion toggle, and the REM/EM-to-pixel base (default 16).
functions.macos_build: UserDefaults. Highlight with NSAttributedString colors in the search field.

notes: Math, units, dates and time zones work offline. Currency and crypto need network rate feeds. Raycast's engine is SoulverCore, which is licensable and the fastest route to parity.

functions.macos_build: AX: set y/height only.

functions.what: Enters or leaves native macOS fullscreen for the focused window.
functions.macos_build: AXUIElementSetAttributeValue(win, "AXFullScreen" as CFString, !current as CFBoolean).

functions.what: Puts the window back where it was before the last window command.
functions.macos_build: Before each move, save the previous frame keyed by CGWindowID (private _AXUIElementGetWindow, or pid + title as a fallback), then restore it.

functions.what: Slides the window flush to that screen edge, keeping its size.
functions.macos_build: AX: set position only, clamped to visibleFrame.

functions.what: Places the window at given coordinates, e.g. 100,100.
functions.macos_build: Inline argument fields, then set kAXPositionAttribute.

functions.macos_build: Inline arguments, then set kAXSizeAttribute.

functions.what: Moves the window to the neighboring monitor, keeping its relative position and size.
