functions.name: Minimize on This Display
functions.what: Minimizes the windows on the current display.
functions.macos_build: For each regular app, list kAXWindowsAttribute, keep windows whose frame intersects the screen, and set kAXMinimizedAttribute true.

functions.name: Move to Previous Space / Next Space / Move to Desktop 1–9
functions.what: Sends the focused window to another macOS Space.
functions.macos_build: There's no public API. Workarounds: (a) synthesize a mouse-down on the window's title bar with CGEvent, post the Mission Control 'Move left/right a space' or 'Switch to Desktop N' shortcut (⌃←/⌃→/⌃N, must be enabled), then mouse-up. This is fragile and used by Amethyst. (b) private SkyLight calls (CGSMoveWindowsToManagedSpace), which no longer work on other apps' windows on recent macOS without SIP disabled (yabai).

functions.name: Focus Next App Window / Focus Previous App Window
functions.what: Cycles focus through the windows of the current app.
functions.macos_build: AX kAXWindowsAttribute of the frontmost app, then kAXRaiseAction on the next window and set kAXMainAttribute true.

functions.name: Window gaps
functions.what: Sets spacing between tiled windows and around screen edges (v1: 0–128 px). Custom commands ignore gaps.
functions.macos_build: Inset the computed rects by the gap and half-gap on shared edges.

functions.name: Half cycling
functions.what: Repeating Left/Right Half either cycles through widths (1/2 → 2/3 → 1/3) or carries the window to the next screen.
functions.macos_build: Remember the last command and timestamp. If the same command repeats on the same window within N seconds, advance the cycle state.

functions.name: Respect Stage Manager
functions.what: Leaves room on the left for the Stage Manager strip when tiling.
functions.macos_build: Check CFPreferencesCopyAppValue("GloballyEnabled", "com.apple.WindowManager"). When it is on, shrink the usable rect by about 190 pt on the strip side.

functions.name: Hotkey presets from other window managers
functions.what: Applies the default shortcut set of other window-management apps in one step.
functions.macos_build: Bundled preset tables (e.g. Rectangle's ⌃⌥ arrows) bulk-registered as Carbon hotkeys.

functions.name: Create custom window command
functions.what: Defines your own command with size, a pinned position (corner, edge or center) and offsets, in points or percent (offsets may be negative).
functions.macos_build: Form storing a spec (anchor, width/height abs or rel, x/y offset). Evaluated by the AX engine.

functions.name: Create window layout
functions.what: Arranges up to 8 windows per display in one command. Each slot can launch an app with a quicklink, file or folder, URL or CLI arguments. Other windows can be left, minimized or closed, and adjacent tiles share a draggable divider.
functions.macos_build: Launch apps with NSWorkspace.openApplication (OpenConfiguration.arguments) or open([url], withApplicationAt:). Wait for the AX window (poll kAXWindowsAttribute or AXObserver kAXWindowCreatedNotification), then place it. Close or minimize other windows via AX. A shared divider needs an AXObserver on kAXResizedNotification to resize the neighbor.

functions.name: Save Current Layout / Add Visible Windows
functions.what: Captures the windows currently on screen into a prefilled layout draft.
functions.macos_build: CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo(.optionOnScreenOnly) for order and bounds, joined with AX windows for app identity. Convert bounds to relative rects per display.
functions.permission: Accessibility (+ Screen Recording for window titles via CGWindowList)

functions.name: Duplicate built-in command as custom
functions.what: Starts a custom command from a built-in layout.
functions.macos_build: Copy the spec.

functions.name: Custom window command deeplink
functions.what: Runs a saved or ad-hoc layout from a URL with name, position and absolute/relative width, height and offset parameters.
functions.macos_build: URL scheme handler parsing the query items into a spec. Callers should use `open -g` so the launcher doesn't steal focus.

notes: Local except Spaces control (no public API). Raycast v1 made custom commands and layouts Pro features. Open/Close/Rename Desktop 1–9 and 'Auto Close Empty Desktops' are Windows virtual-desktop features and can't be done publicly on macOS. Some apps ignore resize requests or enforce minimum sizes.

functions.name: My Schedule
functions.what: Agenda view with a summary of your next meeting, grouped as this week by day, next week, the rest of the month and later months. Searchable by title.
functions.keys: ↵ open in default calendar app; ⌘↵ join call
functions.macos_build: EventKit: EKEventStore().requestFullAccessToEvents (macOS 14+), events(matching: predicateForEvents(withStart:end:calendars:)), grouped by Calendar.dateComponents. Refresh on .EKEventStoreChanged.

functions.name: Join meeting
functions.what: Finds the conference link in an event and opens it, in the native app when installed. Supports Zoom, Google Meet, Teams, Slack Huddles, Webex, FaceTime, Skype, BlueJeans, Chime, Whereby, Jitsi, Around, Chorus, Riverside and StreamYard.
functions.macos_build: Regex over event.url, location and notes for provider URL patterns. Rewrite to native schemes where possible (zoommtg://zoom.us/join?confno=…&pwd=…, msteams:…). NSWorkspace.open. A setting picks the browser for Google links via open(_:withApplicationAt:).

functions.name: Create Event
functions.what: Adds an event with title, time, calendar, attendees, location, URL, notes and alerts.
functions.macos_build: EKEvent(eventStore:) with fields and EKAlarm, then store.save(_:span:.thisEvent). EventKit can't add attendees (EKEvent.attendees is read-only), so attendee invites need Google Calendar or Microsoft Graph APIs or an .ics mailto.

functions.name: Accept / Decline invitation
functions.what: Responds to a pending RSVP.
functions.macos_build: Not possible with EventKit (participantStatus is read-only). Either open the event in Calendar.app (NSWorkspace open with ical:// or Calendar's AppleScript `show`) or call the provider API with OAuth.

functions.name: Block Time
functions.what: Quickly reserves a busy slot on your calendar.
functions.macos_build: Create an EKEvent with availability .busy.

functions.name: Email All Attendees
functions.what: Starts an email to everyone invited.
functions.macos_build: Collect EKParticipant.url (mailto:) for all attendees and open mailto:a,b?subject=title.

functions.name: Copy Availability
functions.what: Copies your free time slots as text to share.
functions.macos_build: Compute gaps between busy events in working hours over the next N days and format with DateIntervalFormatter.

functions.name: Copy Event Details / Title / Attendees
functions.what: Copies different parts of the event.
functions.macos_build: String formatting + NSPasteboard.

functions.name: Delete Event
functions.what: Removes the event.
functions.macos_build: store.remove(event, span:).

functions.name: Menu bar agenda
functions.what: Shows the upcoming or current event in the menu bar with a countdown (never, at start, 2–60 min before, upcoming, or always). Can limit to events with a conference link and auto-hide after start. The menu offers Join, Dismiss, Open My Schedule and Open Calendar.
functions.macos_build: NSStatusItem with button.title updated by a 30–60 s timer, and an NSMenu with actions.

functions.name: Root search display window
functions.what: Sets how long before and after start the event stays pinned in root search (2–30 min, default 10).
functions.macos_build: Filter for the empty-state section.

functions.name: Auto Join Meetings with confirm and camera preview
functions.what: Optionally opens the call automatically at start time, after confirmation and an optional camera check.
functions.macos_build: Schedule a timer at event.startDate. UNUserNotificationCenter notification with Join/Skip actions, or an NSPanel. Camera preview via AVCaptureSession + AVCaptureVideoPreviewLayer.

functions.name: Enabled calendars and default calendar app
functions.what: Choose which calendars to include, and whether Calendar, Fantastical, Notion Calendar, Amie, BusyCal or Outlook opens events.
functions.macos_build: store.calendars(for: .event) list with checkboxes. Detect installed apps by bundle ID via NSWorkspace.urlForApplication(withBundleIdentifier:).

notes: Data comes from the macOS calendar store (EventKit), so it's local. Ask Calendar (@calendar) uses Raycast AI (cloud, Pro). Auto Transcribe Meetings depends on the third-party Granola app.

functions.what: Turns the displays off.
functions.macos_build: Process `/usr/bin/pmset displaysleepnow`.

functions.name: Restart
functions.what: Restarts the computer.
functions.macos_build: Send AppleEvent kAERestart ('rrst') to loginwindow (Apple QA1134), or `tell application "System Events" to restart`. Needs the hardened-runtime entitlement com.apple.security.automation.apple-events.

functions.name: Shut Down
functions.what: Powers off the computer.
functions.macos_build: AppleEvent kAEShutDown ('shut') to loginwindow, or System Events `shut down`.

functions.name: Log Out
functions.what: Logs out of the current user.
functions.macos_build: AppleEvent kAEReallyLogOut ('rlgo') to loginwindow, or System Events `log out`.

functions.name: Hibernate
functions.what: Saves memory to disk and powers down.
functions.macos_build: Requires `pmset hibernatemode 25` (root) and then sleep, so it needs an SMAppService privileged daemon. Rarely worth it on Apple Silicon.

functions.name: Toggle Energy Saver (Low Power Mode)
functions.what: Turns Low Power Mode on or off.
functions.macos_build: Read the state with ProcessInfo.processInfo.isLowPowerModeEnabled. Setting it requires `pmset -a lowpowermode 0/1` as root, through an SMAppService daemon or AuthorizationExecute-style prompt.

functions.name: Show Screen Saver
functions.what: Starts the screen saver.
functions.macos_build: NSWorkspace.shared.open(URL(fileURLWithPath: "/System/Library/CoreServices/ScreenSaverEngine.app")).

functions.name: Play / Pause, Next Track, Previous Track
functions.what: Controls whatever media is playing.
functions.macos_build: Post system-defined media key events: NSEvent.otherEvent(with: .systemDefined, …, subtype: 8, data1: (NX_KEYTYPE_PLAY<<16)|(0xA<<8)) and its keyUp twin, via .cgEvent?.post(tap: .cghidEventTap). Use NX_KEYTYPE_NEXT/PREVIOUS (or FAST/REWIND) for tracks. Private MediaRemote is locked down since macOS 15.4.

functions.name: Toggle Mute
functions.what: Mutes or unmutes system output.
functions.macos_build: CoreAudio: default output device (kAudioHardwarePropertyDefaultOutputDevice), then AudioObjectSetPropertyData kAudioDevicePropertyMute (scope output, element main). If the device lacks a mute control, fall back to `set volume output muted` AppleScript.

functions.name: Turn Volume Up / Turn Volume Down
functions.what: Steps the volume a few percent.
functions.macos_build: Read and set kAudioHardwareServiceDeviceProperty_VirtualMainVolume (AudioToolbox) on the default output device, or post NX_KEYTYPE_SOUND_UP/DOWN events to get the system HUD.

functions.name: Set Volume / Set Volume to 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%
functions.what: Jumps to a specific volume level.
functions.macos_build: Set VirtualMainVolume to a scalar 0–1.

functions.name: Volume Mixer
functions.what: Per-app volume and mute for apps playing audio, split into Playing and Idle.
functions.macos_build: Requires CoreAudio process taps (AudioHardwareCreateProcessTap, macOS 14.2+) on each app's kAudioHardwarePropertyProcessObjectList entry, routed through a private aggregate device with gain applied, while muting the original. Detect playing apps via kAudioProcessPropertyIsRunningOutput.

functions.name: Toggle Active App Mute / Active App Volume Up/Down
functions.what: Mutes or adjusts only the frontmost app's audio.
functions.macos_build: Same process-tap machinery as Volume Mixer, applied to the frontmost pid.

functions.name: Toggle Microphone Mute
functions.what: Mutes or unmutes all connected microphones.
functions.macos_build: Enumerate kAudioHardwarePropertyDevices with input streams and set kAudioDevicePropertyMute (input scope), or set the input volume scalar to 0 and restore it. Show a HUD.

functions.name: Toggle Camera Mute
functions.what: Blocks or restores camera access for all apps.
functions.macos_build: No public API to block other apps' camera access on macOS; it isn't feasible without a kernel or system extension. Skip, or only show camera-in-use state via CoreMediaIO.

functions.name: Show Desktop
functions.what: Moves all windows aside to show the desktop.
functions.macos_build: Post the user's Mission Control 'Show Desktop' shortcut (default F11/fn-F11) via CGEvent, or call private CoreDockSendNotification("com.apple.showdesktop.awake").

functions.name: Toggle System Appearance
functions.what: Switches between Light and Dark mode.
functions.macos_build: NSAppleScript: tell application "System Events" to tell appearance preferences to set dark mode to not dark mode.

functions.name: Toggle Stage Manager
functions.what: Turns Stage Manager on or off.
functions.macos_build: No public API. Write com.apple.WindowManager GloballyEnabled with CFPreferences and post a notification (unreliable), or use AX UI scripting of the Control Center Stage Manager toggle.

functions.name: Toggle Night Shift / Night Light
functions.what: Turns warm display tint on or off (called Night Light on Windows).
functions.macos_build: Private CoreBrightness CBBlueLightClient setEnabled: loaded via dlopen/NSClassFromString. Private API.

functions.name: Toggle HDR
functions.what: Turns HDR on or off (mainly Windows).
functions.macos_build: No public macOS API for toggling HDR on external displays. Skip.

functions.name: Open Trash
functions.what: Opens the Trash in Finder.
functions.macos_build: NSWorkspace.shared.open(FileManager.default.urls(for: .trashDirectory, in: .userDomainMask)[0]).

functions.name: Empty Trash
functions.what: Empties the Trash, with an optional confirmation first.
functions.macos_build: NSAppleScript `tell application "Finder" to empty trash` (handles all volumes and locked items). NSAlert confirmation gated by a setting.

functions.name: Eject All Disks
functions.what: Ejects every mounted removable volume and disk image.
functions.macos_build: FileManager.mountedVolumeURLs(includingResourceValuesForKeys: [.volumeIsEjectableKey, .volumeIsRemovableKey, .volumeIsInternalKey]), then NSWorkspace.shared.unmountAndEjectDevice(at:) for each ejectable one (or DiskArbitration DADiskUnmount + DADiskEject).

functions.name: Toggle Hidden Files
functions.what: Shows or hides hidden files in Finder.
functions.macos_build: Flip the AppleShowAllFiles key in the com.apple.finder domain (CFPreferencesSetAppValue + synchronize), then relaunch Finder (terminate the com.apple.finder app; it restarts). Or post ⇧⌘. to a Finder window.

functions.name: Hide All Apps Except Frontmost
functions.what: Hides every other app.
functions.macos_build: Iterate NSWorkspace.shared.runningApplications where activationPolicy == .regular and it isn't the frontmost app, calling hide().

functions.name: Unhide All Hidden Apps
functions.what: Brings all hidden apps back.
functions.macos_build: For each running app with isHidden, call unhide().

functions.name: Quit All Apps / Quit All Apps Except Frontmost
functions.what: Quits every regular app (optionally keeping the front one), with a confirmation and an exclusion list.
functions.macos_build: terminate() each .regular app except Finder, self, exclusions and optionally the frontmost. NSAlert confirmation setting.

functions.name: Dismiss Notifications
functions.what: Clears notification banners on screen.
functions.macos_build: No public API. Use AX on the NotificationCenter process (bundle com.apple.notificationcenterui): find notification groups and perform the 'Close' or 'Clear All' AXAction. Breaks with OS updates.

functions.name: WiFi (connect to saved networks)
functions.what: Lists networks and joins saved ones.
functions.macos_build: CoreWLAN: CWWiFiClient.shared().interface()?.scanForNetworks(withName: nil), associate(to:password:). SSIDs require Location Services authorization (CLLocationManager) on macOS 14+. Known networks via CWConfiguration.networkProfiles.

functions.name: Toggle WiFi
functions.what: Turns Wi-Fi power on or off.
functions.macos_build: CWWiFiClient.shared().interface()?.setPower(Bool). May require admin depending on the 'Require administrator authorization to turn Wi-Fi on or off' system setting.

functions.name: Bluetooth (manage paired devices)
functions.what: Connects or disconnects paired Bluetooth devices.
functions.macos_build: IOBluetooth: IOBluetoothDevice.pairedDevices(), then openConnection()/closeConnection(), with isConnected for state. Needs NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription.

functions.name: Toggle Bluetooth
functions.what: Turns the Bluetooth controller on or off.
functions.macos_build: Private IOBluetoothPreferenceSetControllerPowerState(int) / IOBluetoothPreferenceGetControllerPowerState via dlsym (the approach blueutil uses).

functions.name: Toggle Airplane Mode
functions.what: Turns all radios off or on.
functions.macos_build: macOS has no Airplane Mode. Emulate it by turning off Wi-Fi (CoreWLAN) and Bluetooth (IOBluetooth private), then restoring the previous states.

notes: These are local OS controls, but several rely on private or undocumented APIs (lock, Night Shift, Bluetooth power, Show Desktop, Dismiss Notifications) or are impossible (camera block, HDR). Hibernate, Night Light, HDR and Airplane Mode are mainly Windows features in Raycast. Hardened-runtime apps need the Apple Events entitlement for AppleScript-based commands.

functions.name: Search Emoji & Symbols
functions.what: Grid of emoji, flags and Unicode symbols, searchable by name, category and your own keywords, with category filters and pinned items first.
functions.macos_build: Bundle Unicode emoji-test.txt (order and categories) plus CLDR annotations JSON (keywords, many languages). Get symbol names from Unicode.Scalar.Properties.name. Show in an NSCollectionView grid with a category NSPopUpButton.

functions.name: Paste / Copy / Paste and keep window open
functions.what: Inserts the emoji into the active field, copies it, or pastes while staying open to pick more.
functions.macos_build: NSPasteboard + synthetic ⌘V. Or CGEvent.keyboardSetUnicodeString for a single grapheme, which avoids touching the clipboard.

functions.name: Skin tones
functions.what: Sets a default skin tone, and lets you pick one per paste or copy for emoji that support it.
functions.keys: ⌥⌘V paste with tone; ⌥⌘C copy with tone
functions.macos_build: Check Unicode.Scalar.Properties.isEmojiModifierBase and append U+1F3FB…U+1F3FF. Multi-person sequences need emoji-zwj-sequences.txt.

functions.name: Copy Unicode
functions.what: Copies the code point(s) of the selected character.
functions.macos_build: Map unicodeScalars to String(format: "U+%04X").

functions.name: Pin / unpin and frecency
functions.what: Pinned emoji stay at the top, and the rest are ranked by how often and recently you used them.
functions.macos_build: SQLite usage table.

functions.name: Custom keywords
functions.what: Add your own search words to any emoji or symbol, optionally saving AI-suggested ones.
functions.macos_build: keywords table joined into search.

functions.name: AI / semantic emoji search
functions.what: Finds emoji by meaning when keywords don't match, and Tab shows AI alternatives.
functions.macos_build: Precompute EmbeddingGemma vectors for each emoji's annotation text and run cosine search on the query embedding. Fully local with DigUp's existing LlamaEmbedder.

functions.name: Inline ':' autocomplete in launcher text fields
functions.what: Typing ':' in the app's own text fields (notes, snippets, chat) suggests emoji inline. It doesn't work in other apps.
functions.macos_build: NSTextView delegate showing a completion popover (textView(_:completions:forPartialWordRange:indexOfSelectedItem:) or a custom NSPanel).

functions.name: Grid size and global hotkey
functions.what: Sets 6–10 columns (zoom with ⌘- / ⌘+, reset with ⌘0) and a global hotkey that can replace the system picker (⌃⌘Space / fn-E).
functions.macos_build: Collection view layout setting. Register ⌃⌘Space with Carbon, which takes priority over the per-app Edit › Emoji & Symbols menu shortcut.

notes: Raycast's AI emoji search uses Raycast AI (cloud) even when local models are configured. A native fork can do it fully on-device with EmbeddingGemma. Emoji history is exportable.

functions.name: Raycast Notes (toggle window)
functions.what: Shows or hides a lightweight note window that floats above other apps. Only one note is visible at a time.
functions.macos_build: NSPanel (titled, resizable, fullSizeContentView) with level .floating, collectionBehavior [.canJoinAllSpaces, .fullScreenAuxiliary], hidesOnDeactivate false, toggled by a Carbon hotkey. Set sharingType = .none to hide it from screen sharing.

functions.name: Create Note
functions.what: Starts a new note immediately. The first line becomes its title.
functions.macos_build: Insert a row in SQLite (id, body markdown, created, updated, pinned, deleted_at) and focus the editor.

functions.name: Search Notes
functions.what: Searches all notes by title and content.
functions.macos_build: SQLite FTS5 over note bodies. Optional semantic search with EmbeddingGemma.

functions.name: Browse Notes
functions.what: Lists your notes stack for quick switching.
functions.macos_build: Popover list in the panel.

functions.name: Back / forward between recent notes
functions.what: Navigates the history of opened notes.
functions.macos_build: Navigation stack of note IDs.

functions.name: Live Markdown editing
functions.what: Markdown syntax formats as you type: headings, lists, quotes, code, links, horizontal rules.
functions.macos_build: NSTextView (TextKit 2) with an NSTextStorage subclass or NSTextContentStorage delegate that re-parses edited paragraphs (Apple swift-markdown or regex) and applies attributes. Keep markdown as the source of truth.

functions.name: Formatting shortcuts
functions.what: Keyboard shortcuts for every block and inline format.
functions.keys: ⌥⌘1–3 headings; ⌥⌘C code block; ⇧⌘B quote; ⇧⌘7 ordered list; ⇧⌘8 bullets; ⇧⌘9 tasks; ⌘B bold; ⌘I italic; ⇧⌘S strikethrough; ⌘U underline; ⌘E inline code; ⌘L link
functions.macos_build: performKeyEquivalent on the text view, wrapping or prefixing the selection with markdown tokens.

functions.name: Slash menu and Format Bar
functions.what: A '/' command menu and a bottom toolbar for inserting formats.
functions.macos_build: Completion popover on '/' at line start. NSStackView toolbar of buttons.

functions.name: Task toggle
functions.what: Checks or unchecks a task item.
functions.macos_build: Toggle '[ ]' / '[x]' on the caret line.

functions.name: Pin note and quick open pinned
functions.what: Pins notes to the top of lists. ⌘0–9 opens pinned notes while the window is open.
functions.keys: ⇧⌘P pin; ⌘. pin from search; ⌘0–⌘9 open pinned
functions.macos_build: pinned_order column.

functions.name: Delete Note / Delete All Notes / Recently Deleted
functions.what: Deletes notes, keeping them in a Recently Deleted area for recovery.
functions.macos_build: Soft delete with deleted_at and a purge after N days.

functions.name: Zoom
functions.what: Scales note text.
functions.macos_build: Scale the font size attribute.

functions.name: Menu bar toggle button and Escape behavior
functions.what: Optional menu bar button to show or hide Notes. Esc can either close the window or just move focus away.
functions.macos_build: NSStatusItem. Handle cancelOperation: per setting.

functions.name: Inline emoji picker
functions.what: ':' opens emoji suggestions inside a note.
functions.macos_build: Reuse the emoji completion popover.

notes: Note sync across devices is Raycast Cloud Sync (Pro, cloud). The free tier limits the number of notes ('Unlimited Notes' is Pro). Dictate to Note is a Raycast AI dictation feature (see Dictation).

functions.name: Start Focus Session
functions.what: Form for a goal, a duration (5 min–24 h, 'until 4:30pm', or No Limit), and a block list or allow list of apps, websites and categories.
functions.macos_build: Form + session state machine persisted in SQLite. Parse the 'until' time with NSDataDetector.

functions.name: App blocking
functions.what: Blocked apps quit when the session starts and can't be reopened, unless snoozed.
functions.macos_build: At start, terminate() blocked running apps. Observe NSWorkspace.willLaunchApplicationNotification/didLaunchApplicationNotification and didActivateApplicationNotification, then forceTerminate() or hide() with an overlay. Allow-list mode blocks every .regular app not on the list (excluding Finder and self).

functions.name: Website blocking
functions.what: Blocked sites redirect to a block page.
functions.macos_build: Options: (a) poll the front browser tab URL via Apple Events and set it to a local block page (Automation per browser). (b) NetworkExtension content filter (NEFilterDataProvider system extension; needs com.apple.developer.networking.networkextension entitlement, user approval, notarization). (c) a browser extension with native messaging. (d) /etc/hosts edits through a root helper (coarse).

functions.name: Toggle Focus Session
functions.what: Starts a session with your last setup, or stops the current one.
functions.macos_build: Hotkey → state machine.

functions.name: Edit Focus Session
functions.what: Adds time, changes the lists, or edits the goal mid-session.
functions.macos_build: Form bound to the active session.

functions.name: Complete Focus Session
functions.what: Ends the session early. Timed sessions end on their own.
functions.macos_build: Stop blocking, then optionally relaunch terminated apps ('Restore Terminated Apps') with openApplication.

functions.name: Pause / Resume and breaks
functions.what: Suspends blocking for a preset break and reminds you when it's time to come back.
functions.macos_build: Timer + UNUserNotificationCenter notification.

functions.name: Snooze
functions.what: Grants temporary access to something blocked for 1, 3 (default), 5 or 10 minutes, or never.
functions.macos_build: Per-item expiry in the block engine.

functions.name: Create / Search Focus Categories
functions.what: Reusable groups of apps and sites. Built-in categories are read-only but can be duplicated.
functions.macos_build: Bundled JSON (Social, News, Games…) + user tables.

functions.name: Focus Bar and menu bar progress
functions.what: Small floating window with goal, progress and controls, which can move to the menu bar.
functions.macos_build: Non-activating NSPanel (level .floating) and/or NSStatusItem with a progress title.

functions.name: Sleep handling
functions.what: Pauses a running session when the Mac sleeps and reconciles it on wake.
functions.macos_build: NSWorkspace.willSleepNotification / didWakeNotification.

functions.name: macOS Focus Filters integration
functions.what: Starts a session automatically when a system Focus mode turns on (Ventura+).
functions.macos_build: AppIntents SetFocusFilterIntent subclass with parameters. perform() starts or stops the session.

functions.name: Apple Shortcuts actions and deeplinks
functions.what: Start or complete a session from Shortcuts, or from URLs like raycast://focus/start?goal=…&duration=…, /toggle and /complete.
functions.macos_build: AppIntents (AppIntent + AppShortcutsProvider) and URL scheme routes.

functions.name: Play Sound and Allow all Websites
functions.what: Sound at start or end. When a browser is allowed but no sites are listed, all sites are allowed.
functions.macos_build: NSSound; a block-engine rule.

notes: App blocking is easy and local. Robust website blocking needs Apple Events per browser, a Network Extension, or a browser extension. Ask Raycast Focus (@raycast-focus) is Raycast AI (cloud). Raycast doesn't say how it blocks websites.

functions.name: Search Screenshots
functions.what: Grid of your screenshots and recordings with preview, searchable by text inside the images. Filters: name:, text:, date: ('yesterday', 'last week').
functions.macos_build: Watched folders: the screencapture location (CFPreferencesCopyAppValue("location", "com.apple.screencapture"), default ~/Desktop), CleanShot's folder and user-added folders. Detect captures by Spotlight kMDItemIsScreenCapture == 1 or filename pattern. FSEvents for new files. Vision OCR into FTS5. Parse dates with NSDataDetector. DigUp's image and OCR pipeline already covers most of this.
functions.permission: Full Disk Access or Desktop/Documents/Downloads folder access

functions.name: Paste Latest Screenshot
functions.what: Pastes your most recent screenshot into the active app without opening a view.
functions.macos_build: Pick the newest file in the watched folders. NSPasteboard.writeObjects([NSImage, fileURL]) then ⌘V.

functions.name: Copy Text from Image
functions.what: Copies the OCR text of a screenshot.
functions.macos_build: Vision VNRecognizeTextRequest result from the index.

functions.name: Text Recognition (Fast / Accurate) and cloud files
functions.what: Indexes the text in screenshots, with an option to download cloud-only files (OneDrive/Dropbox) for OCR.
functions.macos_build: VNRecognizeTextRequest recognitionLevel. For iCloud/File Provider placeholders, FileManager.startDownloadingUbiquitousItem or NSFileCoordinator read to materialize.

functions.name: Include All Media
functions.what: Indexes all images and videos in watched folders, not only screenshots.
functions.macos_build: Relax the filter. For video thumbnails use AVAssetImageGenerator.

functions.name: Storage Duration auto-delete and pinning
functions.what: Deletes screenshots older than a chosen age (1 day to unlimited). Pinned ones are kept.
functions.macos_build: Daily job that trashes files with creationDate < cutoff and not pinned (FileManager.trashItem).

notes: Fully local (Raycast OCR is on-device). Raycast doesn't capture screenshots itself; capture could use ScreenCaptureKit SCScreenshotManager (Screen Recording permission). DigUp's semantic image search goes beyond this ('payment declined error' already finds screenshots).

functions.name: Translate (live)
functions.what: Source and target panes. Translation updates as you type, with language detection and word and character counts.
functions.macos_build: Apple Translation framework (macOS 15+): TranslationSession.translate(_:), obtained via SwiftUI .translationTask(configuration). macOS 26 adds a direct TranslationSession(installedSource:target:) initializer. Check LanguageAvailability().status(from:to:) and prepareTranslation() to download models. Detect with NLLanguageRecognizer.dominantLanguage. On-device once models are installed.
functions.permission: none (network only to download language models)

functions.name: Inline translation from root search
functions.what: Type text followed by 'in'/'into' and a language name (3+ characters, fuzzy-matched) to get a translation inline.
functions.macos_build: Regex '(.+) (in|into) (\w{3,})$' plus a language-name lookup via Locale.current.localizedString(forLanguageCode:) for all supported languages.

functions.name: Swap Languages / Change Source / Change Target
functions.what: Flips the direction, or picks languages with fuzzy search.
functions.macos_build: Picker list of LanguageAvailability().supportedLanguages.

functions.name: Copy Translation / Copy Source / Paste to Active App
functions.what: Output actions.
functions.macos_build: NSPasteboard + ⌘V.

functions.name: Use Selected Text as Source
functions.what: When opened by hotkey, fills the source with your current selection.
functions.macos_build: AX kAXSelectedTextAttribute.

functions.name: Custom fixed-pair Translate commands
functions.what: Saved commands for one language pair (e.g. EN→DE) with their own alias, hotkey and deeplink.
functions.macos_build: Command records with source and target.

functions.name: Continue in AI Chat
functions.what: Sends both texts to the AI for tone changes or explanations.
functions.macos_build: Hand off to the local LLM.

notes: Raycast labels Translate as Pro-exclusive and doesn't say which engine it uses (likely cloud). Apple's on-device Translation framework makes a free, offline native version practical.

functions.name: Create Script Command
functions.what: Generates a script from a language template (bash/zsh, AppleScript, Python, Node, Ruby, PHP, Swift) with the metadata header prefilled, saved into a script directory.
functions.macos_build: Write the template file, chmod +x (FileManager.setAttributes posixPermissions 0o755), and open it in the user's editor.

functions.name: Add Script Directory and metadata parsing
functions.what: Indexes the scripts in a folder and reads their '@raycast.*' comment headers (title, mode, icon, packageName, description, currentDirectoryPath, schemaVersion, plus argument1–3, needsConfirmation, refreshTime and author per the public script-commands repo). Edits are picked up automatically.
functions.macos_build: Scan the folder and parse lines matching /[#/-]+ @raycast\.(\w+) (.*)/. Arguments are JSON ({type: text|password|dropdown, placeholder, optional, percentEncoded, data}). Watch for edits with DispatchSource.makeFileSystemObjectSource or FSEvents.

functions.name: Run script with output modes
functions.what: Runs the script. Output can be shown in full, as a one-line toast or HUD (compact/silent), or inline in the root list with periodic refresh (inline + refreshTime).
functions.macos_build: Process with executableURL = the script (the shebang is honored) or /usr/bin/osascript for .applescript. Set currentDirectoryURL, env LANG, Pipe for stdout/stderr. fullOutput → monospaced NSTextView with ANSI color parsing. compact/silent → last line in a HUD. inline → Timer at refreshTime updates the row subtitle.
functions.permission: whatever the script touches (TCC is attributed to the launcher app)

functions.name: Arguments and confirmation
functions.what: Up to three inline arguments (text, password, dropdown) passed as $1–$3, plus an optional confirmation before running.
functions.macos_build: Inline argument fields → Process.arguments. NSAlert for needsConfirmation.

functions.name: Script as fallback, hotkey or deeplink
functions.what: A script whose first argument is text can be a fallback command. Any script can get a hotkey or a deeplink like raycast://script-commands/<slug>?arguments=….
functions.macos_build: Register with the fallback list, hotkey registry and URL router.

notes: Local. This is the most practical stand-in for Raycast's JS extension ecosystem in a native fork, since any language works. Scripts themselves are not cloud-synced (only their settings).

functions.name: Run command by URL
functions.what: raycast://extensions/<owner>/<ext>/<command>, raycast://script-commands/<slug> and raycast://ai-commands/<slug> run commands from anywhere, with fallbackText= to prefill and arguments= to pass parameters.
functions.macos_build: Register the scheme in Info.plist CFBundleURLTypes and handle it in NSApplicationDelegate.application(_:open:) (or NSAppleEventManager kAEGetURL). Route via URLComponents.queryItems.

functions.name: Deeplink confirmation
functions.what: Asks before running a command from a link, with an 'Always Open Command' option to skip it next time.
functions.macos_build: NSAlert with suppression button. Store trusted command IDs.

functions.name: Confetti
functions.what: raycast://confetti fires a full-screen confetti animation, for example at the end of a long script.
functions.macos_build: Borderless transparent NSWindow per screen (level .screenSaver, ignoresMouseEvents) hosting a CAEmitterLayer for ~3 s.

functions.name: Background deeplinks for window commands
functions.what: Opening with `open -g` keeps the launcher from stealing focus, so window commands act on the right app.
functions.macos_build: In the handler, don't activate the app for routes flagged as background.

notes: Local. Documented in the v1 manual. v2 adds focus/start|toggle|complete and customWindowManagementCommand routes.

functions.name: Export Settings & Data
functions.what: Writes one encrypted backup of AI chats and commands, clipboard history, quicklinks, snippets, notes, emoji history, MCP servers, extensions, settings, aliases, hotkeys and window layouts, protected by a passphrase of 8+ characters.
functions.macos_build: Serialize the stores into a zip/JSON bundle. Derive the key with PBKDF2 (CommonCrypto CCKeyDerivationPBKDF, SHA-256, high iteration count, random salt), since CryptoKit has no password KDF. Encrypt with CryptoKit AES.GCM.seal. Keep the passphrase in the Keychain.

functions.name: Import Settings & Data
functions.what: Restores from a backup with a per-category checklist. Merges without overwriting and skips duplicates.
functions.macos_build: Decrypt, then upsert per store with dedupe rules (quicklinks by link; snippets by text+keyword+name).

functions.name: Scheduled exports
functions.what: Automatic daily, weekly or monthly backups to a chosen folder, keeping the latest 1, 5 or 10, with an option to skip on battery.
functions.macos_build: NSBackgroundActivityScheduler (interval, qualityOfService .background) and an IOPSCopyPowerSourcesInfo battery check. Prune old files.

functions.name: Cloud Sync
functions.what: Keeps snippets, quicklinks, notes, AI commands and chats, themes, layouts, extensions and some settings in sync across devices, with per-category toggles, device management and remote data deletion. Clipboard history, script files and credentials are never synced.
functions.macos_build: Native alternatives: CloudKit (CKSyncEngine, macOS 14+) with a private database per record type, or NSPersistentCloudKitContainer. Simpler: write the encrypted export to an iCloud Drive or Dropbox folder and merge on change.

functions.name: Migrate from Raycast v1
functions.what: One-time import of v1 data, including clipboard history and emoji customizations.
functions.macos_build: Not applicable. A fork could instead import Raycast's JSON snippet and quicklink exports.

notes: Cloud Sync is a Raycast Pro, Raycast-server feature (beta) and can't be replicated without your own backend or CloudKit. Scheduled exports are Pro.

functions.name: Store (browse and install extensions)
functions.what: Browse thousands of community extensions by name, keyword or category and install them with Enter.

feature: Raycast AI (Quick AI, AI Chat, AI Commands)

functions.name: Quick AI
functions.what: Type a question in root search and press Tab to get a streamed answer in the same window. Follow-ups continue the thread, and ↵ pastes the answer.
functions.keys: Tab; ↵ paste; ⌘R regenerate; ⇧⌘R regenerate with another model; ⌘N new; ⌘[ / ⌘] recent chats; ⌘J continue in AI Chat; ⌃M dictate
functions.macos_build: Local LLM: Apple FoundationModels (macOS 26, Apple Intelligence Macs) LanguageModelSession.streamResponse(to:). Or llama.cpp text generation with a small instruct GGUF (DigUp already builds llama.cpp with Metal). Or an Ollama HTTP stream at http://localhost:11434/api/chat. Render markdown and code blocks in an NSTextView/WKWebView.

functions.name: AI Chat
functions.what: Full chat window with history sidebar, search, pinning, branching, archive, projects, attachments (files, notes, clipboard, browser tab, screenshots, calendar), model and creativity settings, and find-in-chat.
functions.keys: ⌘B / ⇧⌘S sidebar; ⇧⌘F search chats; ⌘1–⌘0 jump; ⌘F find; ⇧⌘A attach; ⇧⌘B branch; ⇧⌘M model; ⇧⌘Y creativity; ⇧⌘U reasoning; ⌥⌘A archive; ⌃⌘N new project; ⌃⌘M move to project

functions.name: Built-in AI Commands

functions.macos_build: Form + store. Output 'Replace Selection' via AX set or paste. Diff highlight with a simple word diff.

functions.name: Search AI Commands / Import AI Commands

functions.macos_build: List view + Codable import.

functions.name: Quick Fix

functions.name: AI Extensions / tools (@calendar, @clipboard, @file-search, @finder, @raycast-focus, @screen-awareness)

functions.macos_build: Post-process the transcript with a local LLM prompt chosen by the frontmost bundle ID.

functions.name: App Context

functions.macos_build: AX text of the focused window (and ScreenCaptureKit + Vision OCR) fed as context or contextual strings.

functions.macos_build: SFSpeechRecognitionRequest.contextualStrings, or SpeechAnalyzer AnalysisContext contextual strings. Whisper initial prompt.

functions.macos_build: SQLite table.

functions.macos_build: AVCaptureDevice.DiscoverySession for mics. CoreAudio output mute during capture. Post Return after paste for auto-submit.

Migration from Wispr Flow, Superwhisper and similar apps is a Raycast import feature. Fully on-device is feasible natively.

functions.name: Send Window to AI

functions.macos_build: Codable JSON, base64url in a custom-scheme URL.

feature: Windows-only launcher features (Run, Games / Game Mode)

functions.name: Open Run / Execute Run Command / Create Run Command
functions.what: Replacement for the Windows Run dialog: executables, .cpl, .msc, %VAR% paths, shell: URIs and custom aliases, with shared history.
functions.macos_build: Not applicable on macOS. The analogue is a 'run shell command' fallback that executes the query with Process(/bin/zsh -lc) and shows the output.

functions.name: Game Launcher / Treat as Game
functions.what: Lists installed games from Steam, Epic, GOG and others, and lets you reclassify apps as games.
functions.macos_build: On macOS, detect games by Info.plist LSApplicationCategoryType hasPrefix 'public.app-category' + 'games', and scan the Steam library (~/Library/Application Support/Steam/steamapps/*.acf).

functions.name: Game Mode (pause hotkeys while gaming)
functions.what: Temporarily disables all launcher hotkeys while a game is frontmost.
functions.macos_build: On didActivateApplicationNotification, if the app is a game (category or fullscreen), call UnregisterEventHotKey for all bindings and disable event taps. Re-register on deactivate.

notes: Run and Games are documented as Windows features in Raycast v2. Listed for completeness; on macOS only Game Mode-style hotkey pausing is worth borrowing.

Sources: manual.raycast.com/search-bar, /settings, /keyboard-shortcuts (raycast.com core-feature pages are thin and JS-light, so the manual was used). Root search is fully local. Cloud only: Raycast Cloud Sync of favorites, aliases, hotkeys and ranking across Macs (Pro), and AI Commands and built-in AI prompts appearing as root items (Raycast AI, Pro). DigUp already has the hotkey NSPanel, SQLite (with FTS5) and the semantic file provider. This feature turns that panel into a multi-provider launcher.

functions.name: Root Search (unified results list)
functions.what: When no command is open, one search field queries every source at once and shows grouped, ranked results: apps, commands, quicklinks, files, contacts, today's events, calculator answers, settings panes, URLs and colors.
functions.keys: Type in the search bar; ↵ runs the selected item's primary action
functions.macos_build: Define a `SearchProvider` protocol (`func results(for query: String) async -> [Item]`, `Item` carries id, title, subtitle, keywords, icon, section, actions). In DigUp's existing NSPanel/SwiftUI SearchPanelView, fan out to providers with a `withTaskGroup`, debounce about 30 ms, and merge into sections. Keep DigUp's semantic/FTS file search as one provider. Persist item metadata and usage in the existing SQLite database.

functions.name: Fuzzy matching
functions.what: Finds items from loose abbreviations and acronyms that skip letters, such as 'slk' for Slack or 'msg' for Messages.
functions.macos_build: Write an fzf/Smith-Waterman-style subsequence scorer in Swift. Give bonuses for word starts, camel-case and space boundaries, consecutive runs and prefix hits, and penalize gaps. Normalize with `String.folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: nil)`. Precompute folded titles at index time. No Apple API involved.

functions.name: Ranking with frecency
functions.what: Orders results by exact alias match, then alias prefix, then fuzzy title score, then subtitle and keyword matches, and finally by how often and how recently you picked each result, learned per query.
functions.macos_build: Add a SQLite table `usage(item_id, query_prefix, count, last_used)` and write to it on every launch. Compute frecency as Σ exp(-Δt/halfLife) per item, boosted when the stored query_prefix matches the current query. Sort by the tuple (aliasExact, aliasPrefix, titleScore, keywordScore, frecency).

functions.name: Reset Ranking
functions.what: Action that discards a command's learned usage, so it drops back to its default position.
functions.macos_build: `DELETE FROM usage WHERE item_id = ?`, then refresh the results.

functions.name: Root Search Sensitivity
functions.what: A Low/Medium/High setting for how strict fuzzy matching is. Low shows more loose matches and High shows fewer, closer ones.
functions.macos_build: Map each level to a minimum score threshold and a maximum gap length in the scorer. Store it in UserDefaults.

functions.name: Search history recall
functions.what: Pressing ↑ at the top of the list (or ↓ at the bottom) steps through previously typed queries. A setting clears the history.
functions.keys: ↑ at top of list / ↓ at bottom
functions.macos_build: Keep a ring buffer of about 50 submitted queries in UserDefaults. In the NSTextField delegate `control(_:textView:doCommandBy:)`, intercept `moveUp:`/`moveDown:` when the selection is at index 0 or at the end. Add a 'Clear Search History' button in Settings.

functions.name: Favorites
functions.what: Pins chosen items to a Favorites section that shows above everything else when the search field is empty. Favorites can be added, removed and reordered.
functions.keys: ⌘F (docs also say ⇧⌘F) add; ⇧⌘↑ / ⇧⌘↓ move favorite up/down
functions.macos_build: Store an ordered array of item IDs in SQLite. Render the section only when the query is empty. Move up/down swaps neighbours. Show it as an icon row in compact mode.

functions.name: Application search
functions.what: Indexes installed apps, including symlinked apps, Finder aliases and apps on mounted drives, and picks up newly installed apps without a restart.
functions.macos_build: Run a live `NSMetadataQuery` with predicate `kMDItemContentType == 'com.apple.application-bundle'`, scoped to /Applications, /System/Applications, /System/Applications/Utilities, ~/Applications, /System/Library/CoreServices/Applications and user scopes. Listen for `NSMetadataQueryDidUpdate` and add FSEvents on those folders as a backstop. Resolve aliases with `URL(resolvingAliasFileAt:)` and symlinks with `resolvingSymlinksInPath()`. Get the name from `FileManager.default.displayName(atPath:)` and the icon from `NSWorkspace.shared.icon(forFile:)`. Launch with `NSWorkspace.shared.openApplication(at:configuration:)`.

functions.name: Alternate names and Spotlight keywords for apps
functions.what: Also matches localized and legacy names, such as 'iCal' for Calendar or 'Preferences' for System Settings.
functions.macos_build: Read `kMDItemAlternateNames` and `kMDItemDisplayName` via `MDItemCreateWithURL` + `MDItemCopyAttribute`, CFBundleName/CFBundleDisplayName from `Bundle(url:)?.localizedInfoDictionary`, and a bundled JSON alias table for legacy names. Index these as keyword fields weighted below the title.

functions.name: System Settings panes
functions.what: Lists individual System Settings panes, and some subsections such as Zoom under Accessibility, as launchable results.
functions.macos_build: On macOS 13+, enumerate `/System/Library/ExtensionKit/Extensions/*.appex` and read each Info.plist bundle ID and localized display name. Open with `NSWorkspace.shared.open(URL(string: "x-apple.systempreferences:<extension bundle id>")!)`. Subsection anchors are undocumented and change between macOS versions, so keep a curated table per version. On macOS 12 and earlier, use /System/Library/PreferencePanes/*.prefPane.

functions.name: Search Contacts
functions.what: Filters your Apple Contacts as you type, with actions to copy details or open the contact card.
functions.macos_build: Request access with `CNContactStore().requestAccess(for: .contacts)`. Query `unifiedContacts(matching: CNContact.predicateForContacts(matchingName:), keysToFetch: [given/family/org name, emails, phones, thumbnailImageData])`. Copy through NSPasteboard. Open the card with `addressbook://<CNContact.identifier>` via NSWorkspace (an undocumented but long-standing scheme). Add NSContactsUsageDescription to Info.plist. Off by default, enabled under Customize Search.

functions.name: Today's calendar events
functions.what: Shows today's events that match the query, with actions to open the event, join the meeting link, or copy its details.
functions.keys: ⌘K for Open in Calendar / Join Meeting / Copy Event Details
functions.macos_build: Request access with `EKEventStore().requestFullAccessToEvents` (macOS 14+, NSCalendarsFullAccessUsageDescription), then call `events(matching: predicateForEvents(withStart: startOfDay, end: endOfDay, calendars: nil))` and filter by title. To find a join link, scan `event.url`, `notes` and `location` with `NSDataDetector(types: NSTextCheckingResult.CheckingType.link.rawValue)` for zoom.us, meet.google.com and teams.microsoft.com. Open in Calendar with `ical://ekevent/<eventIdentifier>?method=show&options=more` (undocumented), or just activate Calendar.

functions.name: Web URL detection
functions.what: Typing a URL or bare domain offers to open it in the browser, adding https:// when no scheme is given.
functions.macos_build: If the query has no spaces and either ends in a known TLD (bundled public-suffix list) or `NSDataDetector` with the `.link` type matches its full range, build `URL(string: "https://" + q)` and call `NSWorkspace.shared.open`.

functions.name: Color value preview
functions.what: Typing a hex, rgb, hsl, oklch or similar color value shows a swatch, with copy-as formats including NSColor and UIColor for Swift.
functions.macos_build: The Calculator feature's color parser provides this as a root-search provider. See the Calculator Color conversion entry.

functions.name: Settings searchable in root
functions.what: Raycast's own settings and each extension's preferences show up as root results that jump to the matching settings page.
functions.macos_build: Register each Settings tab and toggle as an Item. Its action opens the SwiftUI Settings window on that tab and scrolls to the control with `ScrollViewReader.scrollTo(id)`.

functions.name: Inline command arguments
functions.what: Commands, quicklinks and snippets can declare up to three inputs (text, password or dropdown). They appear inside the search bar and are filled in before running.
functions.keys: alias + Space focuses first field; ← / → (or Tab) move between fields; ↵ runs
functions.macos_build: In the search-bar HStack, render up to 3 SwiftUI `TextField` / `SecureField` / `Picker(.menu)` controls bound to an `[Argument]` model, with focus managed by `@FocusState`. Required fields block ↵ until filled, and defaults pre-fill.

functions.name: Disable Command (hide from Root Search)
functions.what: Removes a command or app from root results without uninstalling it. You can re-enable it in Settings.
functions.macos_build: Keep a per-item `disabled` flag in the settings store that providers filter on. The Settings → Shortcuts table shows it as a checkbox.

functions.name: Copy Deeplink
functions.what: Copies a URL that launches the selected command directly from other apps, scripts or quicklinks.
functions.macos_build: Register a custom URL scheme in Info.plist CFBundleURLTypes (e.g. `digup://commands/<id>?arguments=<json>`) and handle it in `NSApplicationDelegate.application(_:open:)`. Write the string with `NSPasteboard.general.setString`. A bare `digup://` opens the launcher.

functions.name: Customize Search sources
functions.what: Settings toggles that add or remove Files and Contacts as root-search sources.
functions.macos_build: Store a per-provider enabled flag in UserDefaults. The merger skips disabled providers.

notes: Fully local. The manual is inconsistent about some shortcuts (Favorites ⌘F vs ⇧⌘F, Configure Extension ⇧⌘, vs ⌥⌘, , Disable ⇧⌘D vs ⌃⇧⌘D). Pick one set and keep it consistent.

functions.name: Open Action Panel
functions.what: Opens a searchable popover with every action available for the selected item, grouped into sections such as Favorites, Configure, Deeplink and Manage.
functions.macos_build: Draw a SwiftUI overlay, or a borderless child NSPanel, anchored to the bottom-right of the launcher. It shows a sectioned `List` built from the selected Item's `actions() -> [ActionSection]`. Route keys with `.onKeyPress` (macOS 14+) or an `NSEvent.addLocalMonitorForEvents(matching: .keyDown)` monitor.

functions.name: Primary / secondary / tertiary actions
functions.what: Runs an item's first, second or third action directly without opening the panel. The footer shows the primary action's name and the ⌘K hint.
functions.macos_build: In `control(_:textView:doCommandBy:)`, catch `insertNewline:` and branch on `NSApp.currentEvent?.modifierFlags` (.command / .option) to run actions[0], [1] or [2].

functions.name: Search actions
functions.what: Typing while the panel is open fuzzy-filters actions by name into one flat list that ignores sections.
functions.macos_build: Reuse the root fuzzy scorer and flatten the sections when the filter text is non-empty.

functions.name: Sub-menus and inline views
functions.what: Some actions open a nested menu (e.g. Configure Command) or an inline custom view (e.g. the hotkey recorder). Esc steps back one level.
functions.macos_build: Keep an `[ActionPage]` navigation stack in @State. Push a page for sub-menus and pop on Esc.

functions.name: Per-action keyboard shortcuts
functions.what: Each action can have its own shortcut, shown next to it, that works from the list without opening the panel.
functions.macos_build: Store a `KeyboardShortcut` (keyCode/characters + modifiers) on each Action. A local keyDown monitor matches `event.charactersIgnoringModifiers` and `modifierFlags.intersection(.deviceIndependentFlagsMask)` against the selected item's actions. Render the shortcut with ⌘⌥⌃⇧ glyphs.

functions.name: Configure Command sub-menu
functions.what: Groups Set Hotkey, Set Alias, Delete Hotkey, Delete Alias (shown only when one is set), Open Command Settings and Configure Extension.
functions.keys: ⇧⌘, Configure Command (also listed as ⌘,); ⌥⌘, or ⇧⌘, Configure Extension
functions.macos_build: Push a page with these items. Set Hotkey pushes the recorder view and Set Alias pushes a TextField. Both write to the shortcuts store and re-register Carbon hotkeys.

functions.name: Add/Remove/Move Favorite actions
functions.what: Pins or unpins the selected item in the Favorites section and reorders it.
functions.macos_build: Mutate the favorites array described under Root Search.

functions.name: Item-type action sets
functions.what: Apps get Open, Show in Finder, Uninstall and Hide. Files get Open, Open With…, Show in Finder, Copy Path and Move to Trash. Calendar events get Open in Calendar, Join Meeting and Copy Event Details. Commands get Run.
functions.macos_build: Open With… lists `NSWorkspace.shared.urlsForApplications(toOpen: url)` (macOS 12+) in a sub-menu and calls `NSWorkspace.shared.open([url], withApplicationAt:configuration:)`. Reveal uses `NSWorkspace.shared.activateFileViewerSelecting([url])`. Trash uses `NSWorkspace.shared.recycle([url])`, never permanent delete.

functions.name: Destructive action styling
functions.what: Shows dangerous actions in red and asks for confirmation before running them.
functions.macos_build: Use `Button(role: .destructive)` styling, then show an inline confirmation page or an `NSAlert` before running.

feature: Command Aliases, Hotkeys and Hyper Key
notes: Also from manual.raycast.com/hyper-key and /settings. All local. Aliases and hotkeys sync across Macs only with Raycast Cloud Sync (Pro). The default launcher hotkey is ⌥Space on fresh installs per /settings, though other pages say ⌘Space. Hyper Key and modifier-only hotkeys need low-level keyboard event access, so they are the hardest part. DigUp's Hotkey.swift already wraps Carbon RegisterEventHotKey for one combo.

functions.name: Launcher hotkey
functions.what: A global shortcut that shows or hides the launcher from any app. It can be rebound, including to ⌘Space once Spotlight's shortcut is turned off.
functions.macos_build: Use DigUp's existing `RegisterEventHotKey` + `InstallEventHandler(kEventHotKeyPressed)`. Detect a clash with Spotlight by reading `CopySymbolicHotKeys` (Carbon HIToolbox) and walk the user to System Settings → Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts → Spotlight. Toggle the NSPanel with `orderFrontRegardless()` / `orderOut(_:)`.

functions.name: Set Alias
functions.what: Assigns a short lowercase keyword (a–z, 0–9, spaces) to a command. Typing it exactly puts that command first, a prefix of it gives a smaller boost, and a badge appears next to the command. Aliases are not fuzzy-matched.
functions.keys: ⌘K → Configure Command → Set Alias, or Settings → Shortcuts
functions.macos_build: Store a unique map `alias → item_id` in SQLite. Validate with the regex `^[a-z0-9 ]+$` and lowercase on save. Show spaces as ␣. The ranker checks exact and prefix alias matches before fuzzy scoring.

functions.name: Alias + Space jumps to arguments
functions.what: For commands that take arguments, typing the alias and a space moves focus into the first argument field.
functions.macos_build: When the query equals an alias followed by a space and the target has arguments, set `@FocusState` to the first argument field and remove the alias text.

functions.name: Per-command global hotkeys
functions.what: Any command, app, quicklink or setting can get a system-wide shortcut that runs it even while the launcher is hidden. The shortcut shows next to the selected command.
functions.macos_build: Call `RegisterEventHotKey` once per binding with a distinct `EventHotKeyID.id`. The handler looks up the item and runs its primary action, showing the panel only if the command has UI. Unregister and re-register on changes.

functions.name: Hotkey recorder
functions.what: An inline recorder that shows the pressed keys as keycaps in real time, auto-saves after about 1.5 s (or on ↵), clears with ✕ or Backspace, and lets you click a modifier to choose its left side, right side or either.
functions.macos_build: While recording, temporarily unregister all Carbon hotkeys and use a local `NSEvent` monitor for `.keyDown` and `.flagsChanged`. Get the side from keyCode (55 L⌘, 54 R⌘, 56 L⇧, 60 R⇧, 58 L⌥, 61 R⌥, 59 L⌃, 62 R⌃) and drive a `Timer` progress bar. Save as a spec like DigUp's `KeyCombo`.

functions.name: Modifier-only and special hotkeys
functions.what: Supports combos of modifiers only (e.g. ⌥⌘), a double tap of ⌘, a single tap of a right-side modifier (right ⌘ or right ⇧), holding both ⌘ keys (L⌘R⌘), fn alone or fn plus a key, and F13–F18.
functions.macos_build: Carbon hotkeys can't express these. Add a listen-only `CGEvent.tapCreate(tap: .cgSessionEventTap, place: .headInsertEventTap, options: .listenOnly, eventsOfInterest: flagsChanged|keyDown mask)` on the main run loop. Track per-keyCode down/up times: a tap is down→up under about 300 ms with no other key in between, and a double tap is two taps under about 350 ms apart. fn is keyCode 63 / `.function`, and it only works alone if the user sets 'Press 🌐 key to: Do Nothing'. F13–F20 work through RegisterEventHotKey (kVK_F13…).
functions.permission: Input Monitoring (listen-only event tap); Accessibility if using NSEvent global monitors

functions.name: Physical key vs key equivalent (international layouts)
functions.what: A per-shortcut choice: stick to the same physical key across layouts (the default), or to the same character. Built-in shortcuts always follow the character.
functions.keys: click the key in the recorder
functions.macos_build: Physical mode stores keyCode. Character mode maps the character to a keyCode for the current layout using `TISCopyCurrentKeyboardLayoutInputSource`, `kTISPropertyUnicodeKeyLayoutData` and `UCKeyTranslate` over all keycodes, then re-registers on the `kTISNotifySelectedKeyboardInputSourceChanged` distributed notification.

functions.name: Conflict detection and overwrite
functions.what: Marks a combo that is already in use in red and names its owner (another command, or the launcher hotkey, which can't be overwritten). It also flags gestures that can't coexist, such as a single ⌥ tap with a ⌥⌥ double tap. Overwriting moves the shortcut to the new command.
functions.macos_build: Check the app's own binding dictionary and an incompatibility table for tap gestures. Read system shortcuts with `CopySymbolicHotKeys`. `RegisterEventHotKey` returns `eventHotKeyExistsErr` when the combo is already registered. Show a red dot plus a tooltip on saved conflicts.

functions.name: Shortcuts settings page
functions.what: One table of every command with its alias and hotkey, editable in place, searchable by name and filterable by category (Applications, Extensions, Quicklinks, System…) or status (Hotkey Set, Alias Set, Enabled, Disabled).
functions.macos_build: SwiftUI `Table` with `.searchable`, a filter `Picker`, and inline alias `TextField` and recorder cells bound to the shortcuts store.

functions.name: Hyper Key
functions.what: Turns a rarely used key (Caps Lock, a left or right modifier, or F1–F12) into a combined ⌃⌥⌘ modifier, optionally plus ⇧, so you can make shortcuts that won't clash with apps. These shortcuts show a ✦ glyph.
functions.macos_build: Remap the source key at the HID level to an unused key (e.g. Caps Lock 0x700000039 → F18 0x70000006D) through the `UserKeyMapping` property, which is what `hidutil property --set` does via IOHIDEventSystemClient. Then an active `CGEventTap` (options `.defaultTap`) tracks F18 down/up and ORs `.maskControl|.maskAlternate|.maskCommand[|.maskShift]` into the flags of key events while it is held. Undo the mapping on quit or when the feature is turned off.
functions.permission: Accessibility (active event tap that modifies events)

functions.name: Hyper Key quick press
functions.what: When Caps Lock or a function key is the Hyper Key, tapping it alone can do nothing, act as the original key, or send Escape.
functions.macos_build: In the same event tap, treat Hyper down→up with no other key in between as a tap. For Escape, post `CGEvent(keyboardEventSource: nil, virtualKey: 0x35, keyDown: true/false)` to `.cghidEventTap`. For the original Caps Lock, toggle `IOHIDSetModifierLockState(connect, kIOHIDCapsLockState, …)` via IOKit.

functions.name: Hyper Key secure-input compatibility and diagnostics
functions.what: An option keeps Hyper shortcuts working while macOS Secure Input is on (e.g. in password fields), and a diagnostic panel shows whether Hyper Key is active, its key and any conflicts, with a restart button.
functions.macos_build: Detect Secure Input with `IsSecureEventInputEnabled()`. Event taps stop seeing keystrokes while it's on, so the fallback is a Carbon hotkey on a reserved key (Raycast reserves Right Control). The diagnostic re-checks `CGEvent.tapIsEnabled` and re-creates the tap. Warn when Karabiner-Elements is running (`NSRunningApplication` with bundle ID org.pqrs.*).

notes: Fully local. Cocoa's StandardKeyBinding already maps ⌃N/⌃P to moveDown:/moveUp: and ⌃F/⌃B to moveForward:/moveBackward: in the field editor. Handling these in `control(_:textView:doCommandBy:)` covers arrows and Emacs keys at once. The AI Chat shortcuts on this page belong to Raycast AI (cloud) and are left out.

functions.name: Move selection
functions.what: Moves through the results list. Emacs bindings are on by default and Vim bindings are optional.
functions.macos_build: Intercept `moveUp:`/`moveDown:` in the search NSTextField delegate's `control(_:textView:doCommandBy:)`. Vim mode needs explicit keyDown handling for ⌃J/⌃K in a local NSEvent monitor or with `.onKeyPress(keys:phases:)`. Choose the binding set in Settings → Keyboard → Navigation Bindings.

functions.name: Jump between sections
functions.what: Jumps to the first item of the previous or next section.
functions.macos_build: Keep section start indices and set the selection to the next or previous section start. Use `ScrollViewReader.scrollTo`.

functions.name: Page up/down
functions.what: Scrolls a page of results at a time. The page keys can be ⌥-arrows or square brackets.
functions.keys: ⌥↑ / ⌥↓ (or [ / ] when Page Navigation Keys = Square Brackets)
functions.macos_build: Move by visibleRowCount, computed from the list frame height divided by row height. Settings → Keyboard → Page Navigation Keys chooses the keys.

functions.name: Escape behavior
functions.what: Esc clears the search text, goes back one view, or closes the window when already at an empty root. A setting picks between going back one step and closing the window and popping to root. Another setting lets Esc close standalone windows.
functions.macos_build: Handle `cancelOperation:` in the field editor or panel. If the text is non-empty, clear it. Else if the navigation stack has more than one view, pop. Else `orderOut`. Read the behavior from UserDefaults.

functions.name: Backspace to go back
functions.what: Pressing Backspace in an empty search field inside a command returns to the previous view.
functions.macos_build: When the text is empty and the stack depth is greater than 1, handle `deleteBackward:` in `doCommandBy` by popping.

functions.name: Pop to Root
functions.what: Returns straight to root search from any depth.
functions.macos_build: Clear the navigation stack and the query.

functions.name: Close window
functions.what: Hides the launcher window.
functions.macos_build: `panel.orderOut(nil)` and give focus back to the previous app (`previousApp.activate()`).

functions.name: Open Settings / User Guide
functions.what: Opens the app's settings window or its online manual.
functions.macos_build: Open settings with `NSApp.sendAction(Selector(("showSettingsWindow:")), to: nil, from: nil)` or SwiftUI `openSettings` (macOS 14+). Open the guide URL with NSWorkspace.

functions.name: Common item action shortcuts
functions.what: Consistent shortcuts across item types: open, reveal in Finder, Open With, Quick Look, edit, show info, duplicate, pin/unpin, show hidden items.
functions.keys: ⌘O open; ⇧⌘O reveal; ⌥⌘O Open With…; ⌘Y Quick Look; ⌘E edit; ⌘I info; ⌘D duplicate; ⌘. pin; ⇧⌘. show hidden
functions.macos_build: Use shared `KeyboardShortcut` constants assigned to the matching Action kinds, matched by the action-panel key monitor.

functions.name: Copy / paste / delete conventions
functions.what: Standard shortcuts for the main copy, a secondary copy (e.g. the deeplink), paste into the front app, secondary paste, delete the item and delete all.
functions.macos_build: Write to NSPasteboard. Paste-to-app hides the panel, activates the previous app and posts ⌘V with `CGEvent(keyboardEventSource:virtualKey:kVK_ANSI_V,keyDown:)` + `.maskCommand` to `.cghidEventTap`.

functions.name: Form navigation
functions.what: In form views, ⌘↵ submits, Tab and ⇧Tab move between fields, and Esc cancels.
functions.macos_build: SwiftUI `Form` with `@FocusState`, `.keyboardShortcut(.return, modifiers: .command)` on the submit button, and `.onExitCommand` for Esc.

notes: Only the v1 manual documents this in detail. In v2 it is configured under Settings → Launcher → Fallback Commands. The default list is not documented. Examples given are Search Files, Google Search and the AI-extension fallbacks 'Use with Ask File Search' and 'Use with Ask Finder' (the AI ones need Raycast AI, which is cloud and Pro).

functions.name: Fallback results on no match
functions.what: When a query matches nothing, shows a list of commands that run with the typed text, such as searching the web or searching files.
functions.keys: ↵ runs the selected fallback with the query
functions.macos_build: When the merged results are empty (or always, as a trailing section), render the enabled fallbacks in order. Each takes the query as its single argument, e.g. a quicklink `https://www.google.com/search?q={argument}` expanded with percent-encoding, or DigUp's semantic file search.

functions.name: Manage Fallback Commands
functions.what: Settings with an enabled list and an available list. You can enable, remove and reorder fallbacks. Single-argument quicklinks and script commands are eligible.
functions.keys: Search 'Manage Fallback Commands'; reorder like favorites (⇧⌘↑/⇧⌘↓)
functions.macos_build: Store an ordered `[itemID]` in UserDefaults. The available list is every quicklink or script whose placeholder parser finds exactly one argument. Use a SwiftUI List with `.onMove`.

functions.name: Fallback section settings shortcut
functions.what: A gear in the fallback section header opens the fallback settings directly.
functions.macos_build: Add a header button that pushes the Manage Fallback Commands view.

notes: Local, except Favicon Provider (network to DuckDuckGo, Google or Raycast) and Export/Import (Raycast's .rayconfig is a password-encrypted file; Cloud Sync is the Pro alternative). Themes beyond light and dark are a Raycast Store item.

functions.name: Open at Login
functions.what: Starts the launcher automatically when you log in.
functions.macos_build: `SMAppService.mainApp.register()` / `unregister()` (macOS 13+). DigUp already imports ServiceManagement.

functions.name: Show in Menu Bar
functions.what: Shows or hides the menu bar icon.
functions.macos_build: Toggle `NSStatusItem.isVisible`. On macOS 26 the user may also need to allow the app in System Settings → Menu Bar.

functions.name: Appearance (follow system / theme)
functions.what: Matches system light or dark mode, or uses a fixed theme.
functions.macos_build: Set `NSApp.appearance = nil` (follow) or `NSAppearance(named: .darkAqua/.aqua)`. A theme is a set of color tokens in SwiftUI `Environment`.

functions.name: Interface Size
functions.what: Default, Large or Larger text and row sizes.
functions.macos_build: Apply a global scale factor to fonts and row heights via an Environment value. Optionally apply `.dynamicTypeSize` in SwiftUI.

functions.name: Window Mode: Compact / Expanded
functions.what: In compact mode only the search bar shows until you type or open the action panel, and the window collapses again when it loses focus. Favorites can show as an icon row in compact mode.
functions.macos_build: Animate the NSPanel height with `setFrame(_:display:animate:)` based on the query and panel state. Collapse in `windowDidResignKey`.

functions.name: Show launcher on screen
functions.what: Chooses where the launcher appears: the screen with the mouse, the screen with the active window, or the primary screen.
functions.macos_build: Mouse screen: the `NSScreen.screens` entry whose frame contains `NSEvent.mouseLocation`. Active-window screen: the frontmost app's top window bounds from `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo([.optionOnScreenOnly, .excludeDesktopElements], kCGNullWindowID)` filtered by `kCGWindowOwnerPID` (bounds need no Screen Recording permission). Primary: `NSScreen.screens.first`.

functions.name: Pop to Root Search delay
functions.what: How long the launcher keeps your last view after closing before it resets to root search, from immediately up to 180 s.
functions.macos_build: Record the hide timestamp. On the next show, if the elapsed time is past the delay, clear the stack and the query.

functions.name: Auto-switch Input Source
functions.what: Switches to a chosen keyboard input source while the launcher is open and restores the previous one when it closes.
functions.macos_build: On show, save `TISCopyCurrentKeyboardInputSource()` and call `TISSelectInputSource` with the chosen source (from `TISCreateInputSourceList`). Restore it on hide.

functions.name: Window Activation Behavior (Spaces)
functions.what: The launcher either moves to the current Space or switches to the Space where it was open.
functions.macos_build: Set `panel.collectionBehavior` to include `.moveToActiveSpace` (follow), or leave it out (switch). `.canJoinAllSpaces` and `.fullScreenAuxiliary` let it appear over full-screen apps.

functions.name: Favicon Provider
functions.what: Chooses where website icons come from: DuckDuckGo, Google, Raycast or none.
functions.macos_build: Fetch `https://icons.duckduckgo.com/ip3/<host>.ico` or `https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain=<host>&sz=64`, or use LinkPresentation `LPMetadataProvider` iconProvider. Cache PNGs in Application Support and convert with `NSImage(data:)`.

functions.name: Export & Import Settings
functions.what: Moves your whole configuration (aliases, hotkeys, quicklinks, favorites, preferences) to another Mac.
functions.macos_build: Serialize all stores to a JSON bundle with `JSONEncoder`, optionally encrypted with CryptoKit `AES.GCM` and a password-derived key (HKDF/PBKDF2 via CommonCrypto). Use NSSavePanel / NSOpenPanel.

functions.name: Connection (proxy / custom CA)
functions.what: Uses the system proxy for network features, or trusts a custom certificate authority.
functions.macos_build: URLSession follows system proxies by default. For a custom CA, implement `urlSession(_:didReceive:completionHandler:)`, call `SecTrustSetAnchorCertificates` with the user's DER cert, and evaluate with `SecTrustEvaluateWithError`.

notes: Local. The manual mixes macOS and Windows: Run as Administrator, Run as Different User and Show Advanced Options are Windows-only, and the Ctrl-based keys for New Application Window and Open Recent Files are Windows bindings. 'Treat as Game' ties into Raycast's Games feature. Uninstall on macOS is just moving the bundle to Trash plus optional leftover cleanup.

functions.name: Open Application
functions.what: Launches the app, or brings it to the front if it is already running.
functions.macos_build: `NSWorkspace.shared.openApplication(at: url, configuration: NSWorkspace.OpenConfiguration())`. Set `activates = true` (the default).

functions.name: Per-app hotkey with Toggle Visibility / Always Show
functions.what: A global shortcut per app. In the default mode it brings the app forward, or hides it if it's already in front. Always Show only ever brings it forward.
functions.macos_build: Register a Carbon hotkey. On press, if `NSWorkspace.shared.frontmostApplication?.bundleIdentifier == target`, call `NSRunningApplication.hide()`. Else activate the running instance (`activate()`, macOS 14) or launch it.

functions.name: Show in Finder
functions.what: Reveals the app bundle on disk.
functions.macos_build: `NSWorkspace.shared.activateFileViewerSelecting([appURL])`.

functions.name: Show Info in Finder
functions.what: Opens Finder's Get Info window for the app.
functions.macos_build: NSAppleScript: `tell application "Finder" to open information window of (POSIX file "<path>" as alias)` and activate Finder. DigUp already has the apple-events entitlement and NSAppleEventsUsageDescription.

functions.name: Show Package Contents
functions.what: Opens the app bundle's Contents folder in Finder.
functions.macos_build: `NSWorkspace.shared.open(appURL.appendingPathComponent("Contents"))`.

functions.name: Copy Path / Copy Name / Copy Bundle Identifier
functions.what: Copies the app's file path, display name or bundle ID (e.g. com.apple.Safari).
functions.macos_build: NSPasteboard `setString` with `url.path`, `FileManager.displayName(atPath:)` or `Bundle(url:)?.bundleIdentifier`.

functions.name: Hide Application
functions.what: Hides all windows of a running app.
functions.macos_build: `NSRunningApplication.runningApplications(withBundleIdentifier:).first?.hide()`.

functions.name: Quit Application
functions.what: Asks the app to quit normally.
functions.macos_build: `NSRunningApplication.terminate()`.

functions.name: Force Quit Application
functions.what: Kills an unresponsive app.
functions.macos_build: `NSRunningApplication.forceTerminate()`.

functions.name: Restart Application
functions.what: Quits the app and opens it again.
functions.macos_build: Call `terminate()`, wait with KVO on `isTerminated` (or `NSWorkspace.didTerminateApplicationNotification`), then `openApplication(at:)`. Time out to `forceTerminate()`.

functions.name: Open Recent Files…
functions.what: Lists the files recently opened in that app so you can reopen one.
functions.macos_build: Read `~/Library/Application Support/com.apple.sharedfilelist/com.apple.LSSharedFileList.ApplicationRecentDocuments/<bundleid>.sfl3` (sfl2 on older systems). It is an NSKeyedArchiver plist of bookmark data, an undocumented format, decoded with `URL(resolvingBookmarkData:)`. Fallback: an `NSMetadataQuery` on `kMDItemLastUsedDate`, filtered to UTIs the app can open.

functions.name: New Application Window
functions.what: Opens a new window of the app even when it's already running.
functions.macos_build: Activate the app, then press its File → New Window menu item via AX: walk `kAXMenuBarAttribute` and run `AXUIElementPerformAction(item, kAXPressAction)`. Alternatively post ⌘N with CGEvent.

functions.name: Auto Quit
functions.what: Quits chosen apps automatically after they've been unused for a set time. Each app can be enabled or disabled, and Manage Auto Quits opens the settings.
functions.keys: Enable/Disable Auto Quit action; 'Manage Auto Quits' command
functions.macos_build: Observe `NSWorkspace.didActivateApplicationNotification` and `didDeactivateApplicationNotification` to stamp each app's last-active time. A 1-minute `Timer` calls `terminate()` on listed apps idle past their threshold, skipping the frontmost app and apps with unsaved state (terminate lets them prompt).

functions.name: Uninstall Application / Uninstall Applications
functions.what: Removes an app, or browses all apps to remove unwanted ones.
functions.macos_build: `NSWorkspace.shared.recycle([appURL])` (an admin prompt appears for root-owned apps). Optionally list leftovers: ~/Library/Application Support/<bundleid>, Caches/<bundleid>, Preferences/<bundleid>.plist, Containers/<bundleid> and Saved Application State. Other apps' Containers are TCC-protected (App Data) on macOS 14+.
functions.permission: none (Full Disk Access for leftover cleanup in Containers)

functions.name: Treat as Game
functions.what: Tags the app so it appears in your games list.
functions.macos_build: Store a per-bundle-ID flag that a Games section reads.

functions.name: Search Scopes and Deep Search
functions.what: Add or remove folders scanned for apps. Standard folders can be turned off. Deep Search looks up to three folder levels inside added folders.
functions.macos_build: A user scope list fed into the NSMetadataQuery `searchScopes`. Deep Search uses `FileManager.enumerator(at:includingPropertiesForKeys:options:)` and stops at depth 3 with `enumerator.level`.

functions.name: Per-app alias, hotkey and visibility
functions.what: Each app can get a custom search name (e.g. 'music' for Spotify), a launch hotkey, and a checkbox to hide it from root search.
functions.macos_build: Reuses the alias, hotkey and disabled stores keyed by bundle ID.

notes: Local. Both commands depend on the Accessibility API. AX `kAXWindowsAttribute` usually returns only windows on the current Space.
