Listing windows on other Spaces needs `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo(.optionAll)` plus Screen Recording for titles, or the private `_AXUIElementCreateWithRemoteToken` brute-force technique used by AltTab (fragile).

functions.name: Switch Windows
functions.what: Lists every open window across apps, including several windows of one app, with window title and app name. Type to filter and press ↵ to bring that window forward. The list updates as windows open and close.
functions.macos_build: For each `NSWorkspace.shared.runningApplications` with `activationPolicy == .regular`, call `AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` → `kAXWindowsAttribute` and read `kAXTitleAttribute`, skipping minimized windows unless you want them. To focus, call `AXUIElementPerformAction(win, kAXRaiseAction)`, set `kAXMainAttribute` true, then `NSRunningApplication(processIdentifier:)?.activate()`. Live updates come from an `AXObserver` per app for `kAXWindowCreatedNotification`, `kAXUIElementDestroyedNotification` and `kAXTitleChangedNotification`, plus NSWorkspace launch/terminate notifications.

functions.name: Window actions (Minimize, Close, Enter Fullscreen, Hide Application)
functions.what: Acts on a listed window from the action panel without bringing it forward.
functions.macos_build: Minimize: `AXUIElementSetAttributeValue(win, kAXMinimizedAttribute, kCFBooleanTrue)`. Close: read `kAXCloseButtonAttribute` and run `kAXPressAction` on it. Fullscreen: set the string attribute "AXFullScreen" to true. Hide: `NSRunningApplication.hide()`.

functions.name: Search Menu Bar Items
functions.what: Puts every menu command of the frontmost app into one searchable list, shown with its current enabled state, and runs the one you pick.
functions.keys: ↵ runs the menu item; alias/hotkey assignable
functions.macos_build: Capture `NSWorkspace.shared.frontmostApplication` before showing the panel. Read `AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` → `kAXMenuBarAttribute` and walk `kAXChildrenAttribute` recursively (AXMenuBarItem → AXMenu → AXMenuItem), collecting `kAXTitleAttribute`, `kAXEnabledAttribute`, `kAXMenuItemCmdCharAttribute`/`kAXMenuItemCmdModifiersAttribute` (shortcut display) and the parent path ('File › Export as PDF…'). Run `AXUIElementPerformAction(item, kAXPressAction)` after re-activating the app. Cache per bundle ID and refresh in the background, since big menus take 100–500 ms to walk.

notes: The marketing page is thin, so the detail comes from manual.raycast.com/file-search. Raycast's v2 index is local-only and never synced. Cloud or AI-only parts are Ask File Search (@file-search), Ask Finder (@finder), their fallback commands, and Send to Quick AI / AI Chat (Raycast AI, Pro). In DigUp the semantic EmbeddingGemma index plus SQLite FTS can do the name and content side better than Spotlight. Raycast's Content Search uses Spotlight.

functions.name: File results in Root Search
functions.what: Typing a file or folder name shows matching files right in root search. Recently used files appear when the field is empty. A Launcher setting turns this off.
functions.macos_build: Add DigUp's IndexStore (name FTS + semantic) as a root provider, capped at about 5 results and ranked below apps and commands unless the score is high. For the empty state, see Recently Used.
functions.permission: Files & Folders prompts (Desktop/Documents/Downloads); Full Disk Access optional

functions.name: Search Files command (details panel)
functions.what: A dedicated, larger results view with a metadata side panel for the selected file: kind, size, dates, location and more.
functions.macos_build: Use a SwiftUI split view. Metadata comes from `url.resourceValues(forKeys: [.localizedTypeDescriptionKey, .fileSizeKey, .creationDateKey, .contentModificationDateKey, .contentAccessDateKey])` and `MDItemCopyAttribute` (kMDItemLastUsedDate, kMDItemWhereFroms, kMDItemPixelWidth/Height, kMDItemDurationSeconds). Generate thumbnails with `QLThumbnailGenerator` (DigUp already uses QuickLookThumbnailing).

functions.name: Recently Used files
functions.what: Lists files you opened recently when the search field is empty.
functions.macos_build: `NSMetadataQuery` with predicate `kMDItemLastUsedDate >= $time.today(-30)` (or `NSPredicate(format: "kMDItemLastUsedDate >= %@", date)`), `searchScopes = [NSMetadataQueryUserHomeScope]` and a sort descriptor on kMDItemLastUsedDate descending. Filter out app bundles and hidden paths.

functions.name: Filename search incl. hidden files
functions.what: Finds files and folders by name. Hidden files are left out by default and can be included with a toggle.
functions.macos_build: Use DigUp's crawler with a SQLite FTS5 table using the `trigram` tokenizer for substring and typo-tolerant name matching. Decide hidden status by leading dot or `URLResourceValues.isHiddenKey`. Settings: Include Hidden Files.

functions.name: Content Search
functions.what: Matches text inside files, using the operating system's search index. The setting is disabled when Spotlight doesn't cover the chosen folders, and a shortcut opens Spotlight settings to fix that.
functions.macos_build: Run `NSMetadataQuery` with `NSPredicate(format: "kMDItemTextContent CONTAINS[cd] %@", q)` scoped to the chosen folders (kMDItemTextContent can be queried but not read back). Check coverage with `mdutil -s <volume>` (Process) and open `x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.Spotlight-Settings.extension`. DigUp's own FTS and semantic index already does this without Spotlight.

functions.name: Index scopes and folder permission
functions.what: Indexes the home folder (plus /Applications) by default. You can grant only specific folders, which limits results with a one-time warning, and add or remove scopes such as project folders or external drives.
functions.macos_build: Use DigUp's FolderSelection, Crawler and FSEvents FolderWatcher, with NSOpenPanel (`canChooseDirectories`) to add scopes. List volumes with `FileManager.default.mountedVolumeURLs(includingResourceValuesForKeys: [.volumeIsRemovableKey, .volumeIsLocalKey, .volumeUUIDStringKey], options: [.skipHiddenVolumes])`.
functions.permission: Files & Folders; Removable Volumes / Network Volumes; Full Disk Access for protected locations

functions.name: Ignore rules (.gitignore / .ignore / .rayignore / global patterns)
functions.what: Skips paths listed in .gitignore, .ignore, git exclude files and a tool-specific ignore file, plus comma-separated global globs (e.g. '*.log, build/**'). Noise like node_modules, temp files, system caches and dev-tool caches is skipped automatically, while hand-written config inside those folders is kept.
functions.keys: Settings → File Search → Ignore Patterns / Use Ignore Files
functions.macos_build: Extend DigUp's Rules.swift (which already applies gitignore for code search) with a per-directory stack of gitignore-semantics matchers (negation, anchored, `**`) and its own ignore filename (e.g. `.digupignore`). Match global globs with `fnmatch(3)` and `FNM_PATHNAME`. Ship a built-in deny list (node_modules, .npm, .cargo/registry, .swiftpm, DerivedData, Caches) with an allow list for user files such as .claude/settings.json.

functions.name: Exclude from Index
functions.what: An action that writes a rule for the selected file or folder into the nearest ignore file, or creates one in its parent folder.
functions.macos_build: Walk up the parents to find the ignore file and append the relative path, creating the file if needed. Then delete matching rows and re-evaluate the subtree.

functions.name: Index Files / Stop Indexing
functions.what: Forces a fresh index scan, or pauses indexing from the progress toast.
functions.macos_build: Hook up DigUp's Engine rescan and pause (already in StatusMenu) as actions.

functions.name: Network/removable drives and removed volumes
functions.what: Optionally indexes network shares, removable drives and virtual filesystems, and can keep results for drives that are currently disconnected.
functions.macos_build: Store `volumeUUIDStringKey` on each row. Observe `NSWorkspace.shared.notificationCenter` for `didMountNotification` and `didUnmountNotification`, then mark rows offline (greyed out) or purge them depending on the setting.

functions.name: Excluded Automatically list
functions.what: Shows folders the indexer dropped on its own because they changed constantly, with a count of reindexes avoided.
functions.macos_build: Count FSEvents per directory over a sliding window. Past a threshold, add the folder to an auto-excluded table and list it in Settings with a re-include button.

functions.name: Low disk space guard
functions.what: An optional block that stops indexing when the index wouldn't fit on disk.
functions.macos_build: Compare `URLResourceValues.volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsageKey` on the index volume with DigUp's Estimator projection.

functions.name: Reset to Defaults
functions.what: Restores all File Search settings and re-indexes, after a confirmation.
functions.macos_build: Remove the File Search keys from UserDefaults, confirm with an NSAlert, then trigger a full rebuild.

functions.name: Quick Look
functions.what: Previews the file without opening it.
functions.macos_build: `QLPreviewPanel.shared()` with the panel as `QLPreviewPanelDataSource`/`Delegate` (DigUp already has this via Quartz).

functions.name: Open / Open With… / Show in Finder
functions.what: Opens the file in its default app or one you choose, or reveals it in Finder.
functions.macos_build: `NSWorkspace.shared.open(url)`. Open With uses `urlsForApplications(toOpen:)` and `open([url], withApplicationAt:configuration:)`. Reveal uses `activateFileViewerSelecting([url])`.

functions.name: Copy file / name / path
functions.what: Copies the file itself (pastable in Finder or Mail), its name, or its full path.
functions.macos_build: `NSPasteboard.general.clearContents()` then `writeObjects([url as NSURL])` for the file, and `setString` for the name or path.

functions.name: Move to Trash
functions.what: Deletes the file by moving it to the Trash.
functions.macos_build: `NSWorkspace.shared.recycle([url])`. Never call `removeItem`.

functions.name: Open in Terminal
functions.what: Opens a selected folder in your default terminal.
functions.macos_build: `NSWorkspace.shared.open([folderURL], withApplicationAt: terminalAppURL, configuration: .init())`. Terminal, iTerm and Ghostty open a shell in that folder. The default terminal is a setting.

functions.name: Save as Quicklink
functions.what: Turns the selected file or folder into a quicklink.
functions.macos_build: Prefill the Create Quicklink form with the path and the file's name and icon.

functions.name: Save as Duplicate
functions.what: Makes a copy of the file next to the original.
functions.macos_build: `FileManager.copyItem(at:to:)` to a free name such as 'name copy.ext' / 'name copy 2.ext'.

functions.name: Share…
functions.what: Opens the macOS share sheet for the file.
functions.macos_build: `NSSharingServicePicker(items: [url]).show(relativeTo: rowRect, of: view, preferredEdge: .minY)`.

functions.name: Show Details in File Search
functions.what: Jumps from a root-search file result to the Search Files view with its details panel open.
functions.macos_build: Push the Search Files view preselected to that path.

functions.name: Path browsing and Sort Folder By
functions.what: Typing a path shows that folder's contents and an Open in Finder item. ⇧Tab goes up to the parent. Folders can be sorted by Date Modified, Date Created or Name, and the choice is remembered.
functions.macos_build: Detect queries starting with '/' or '~' and expand with `NSString.expandingTildeInPath`. List with `FileManager.contentsOfDirectory(at:includingPropertiesForKeys: [.isDirectoryKey, .contentModificationDateKey, .creationDateKey], options: [.skipsHiddenFiles])`, prefix-filter on the last path component, and sort by the saved key.

functions.name: Send to Quick AI / AI Chat
functions.what: Attaches the file as context to an AI prompt or chat.
functions.macos_build: Pass DigUp's extracted text (and image or audio embeddings) to a local LLM (llama.cpp, which DigUp already vendors for embeddings) or to a user-configured API.
functions.permission: network if a cloud model is used

functions.name: Ask File Search / Ask Finder AI extensions
functions.what: Natural-language questions answered by an AI that calls the file index or Finder as tools (@file-search, @finder). They also appear as fallbacks when nothing matches.
functions.macos_build: A tool-calling LLM with tools such as `search(query)`, `metadata(path)`, `listFolder(path)` and `reveal(path)` backed by DigUp's semantic search. The model is local or remote.

notes: Also from manual.raycast.com/quicklinks. Cloud and Teams only: Shared Quicklinks (Raycast for Teams, visible to the whole organization with auto-sync), Move Quicklink between personal and organization accounts, the Organization filter, and Cloud Sync of personal quicklinks (Pro). Raycast hosts the Library of prebuilt links, which a fork can bundle as JSON. Everything else is local.

functions.name: Create Quicklink
functions.what: A form to save a link with name, URL/path/deeplink/search-URL, icon (the site's favicon by default), optional Open With app, and tags.
functions.macos_build: SwiftUI `Form` saving a Codable `Quicklink {id, name, link, iconName, openWith(bundleID), tags, alias, hotkey, pinned, hiddenInRoot}` to SQLite. The app picker uses the Applications index. Validate with `URL(string:)` or file existence after tilde expansion.

functions.name: Open Quicklink (from Root Search)
functions.what: Quicklinks are root-search items. ↵ opens the URL, file, folder, project or app deeplink, in the chosen app if one is set. Arguments are asked for inline first.
functions.macos_build: Expand placeholders, then call `NSWorkspace.shared.open(url)` or `open([url], withApplicationAt: appURL, configuration: NSWorkspace.OpenConfiguration())`. Build paths with `URL(fileURLWithPath: (path as NSString).expandingTildeInPath)`. Deeplinks (spotify:, slack:, raycast-style) go through NSWorkspace, which warns when `urlForApplication(toOpen:)` returns nil.

functions.name: Search Quicklinks
functions.what: Browses your quicklinks by name, filters by tag, keeps pinned ones on top, and can show website previews.
functions.macos_build: A List with a tag `Picker` in the search accessory. For previews, LinkPresentation `LPMetadataProvider().startFetchingMetadata(for:)` provides title and image in an `LPLinkView`, cached.

functions.name: Search-URL quicklinks with arguments
functions.what: Links with placeholders such as {argument name="Query" default="…"} prompt for values, up to three, and substitute them, e.g. a Google Translate link with source, target and word.
functions.macos_build: Use the Dynamic Placeholders parser to collect distinct argument names, render the inline argument fields, and percent-encode values by default with `addingPercentEncoding(withAllowedCharacters:)` using `.urlQueryAllowed` minus '&+=?#'.

functions.name: Quicklink Library (Find in Library / Add from Library)
functions.what: Hundreds of ready-made quicklinks, mostly web searches such as Google, Stack Overflow and X, that can be added in one click with an argument already set up.
functions.keys: Settings → Extensions → Quicklinks → Find in Library
functions.macos_build: Bundle a JSON catalog of {name, link with {argument}, icon} and show it in a searchable sheet that copies entries into the store.

functions.name: Quick Search / Pass Selected Text as Argument
functions.what: Select text in any app and press a quicklink's hotkey. The selection fills the quicklink's single argument and the link opens right away.
functions.macos_build: On the Carbon hotkey, read the selection with `AXUIElementCreateSystemWide()` → `kAXFocusedUIElementAttribute` → `kAXSelectedTextAttribute`. Fallback: save the pasteboard items, post ⌘C (`CGEvent(keyboardEventSource:virtualKey: CGKeyCode(kVK_ANSI_C), keyDown:)` with `.maskCommand` to `.cghidEventTap`), poll `NSPasteboard.general.changeCount` for about 150 ms, read the string, then restore the pasteboard.

functions.name: Autofill from browser tab or clipboard
functions.what: When Create Quicklink opens, the link and name are filled from the current browser tab, or from a URL on the clipboard.
functions.macos_build: Capture `NSWorkspace.shared.frontmostApplication` before showing the panel. Safari: NSAppleScript `tell application "Safari" to return {URL, name} of front document`. Chromium browsers (Chrome, Brave, Edge, Arc, Vivaldi): `tell application id "<bundle>" to return {URL, title} of active tab of front window`. Firefox has no tab scripting, so fall back to the clipboard. The clipboard path takes `NSPasteboard.general.string(forType: .string)` when it parses as a URL with a scheme. Needs NSAppleEventsUsageDescription and the apple-events entitlement, both already in DigUp.

functions.name: Prefer Existing Tabs
functions.what: If the URL is already open in a browser tab, switches to that tab instead of opening a new one (Chrome, Safari and other Chromium or WebKit browsers).
functions.macos_build: AppleScript over `every window` and `every tab`, matching the URL by prefix. Chrome: `set active tab index of w to i` + `set index of w to 1`. Safari: `set current tab of w to t`. Then activate the browser, or fall back to `NSWorkspace.open`.

functions.name: Quicklink actions
functions.what: Open With another app, Edit, Duplicate, Pin/Unpin, Copy Name, Copy Link, Hide in Root Search, Create Quicklink and Delete (with an optional confirmation).
functions.keys: ⌘K; ⌥⌘O open with; ⌘E edit; ⌘D duplicate; ⌘. pin; ⌘C / ⇧⌘C copy; ⌃X delete
functions.macos_build: Store mutations plus NSPasteboard writes. Deletion shows an NSAlert when 'Show Warning Before Deleting' is on.

functions.name: Tags
functions.what: Group quicklinks by project, client or purpose, with several tags per link, and filter by them.
functions.macos_build: A many-to-many `quicklink_tags` table and a token field in the form.

functions.name: Per-quicklink alias and hotkey
functions.what: Each quicklink can have its own alias and a global hotkey that opens it from anywhere.
functions.macos_build: Reuse the shared alias and Carbon hotkey stores keyed by quicklink ID.

functions.name: Import / Export Quicklinks
functions.what: Exports quicklinks to a file for backup, and imports a JSON array of {name, link, iconName?, openWith?}. It reports how many were added and how many duplicates (same title and link) were skipped.
functions.macos_build: Codable with `JSONDecoder` and `JSONEncoder` (prettyPrinted), using NSOpenPanel and NSSavePanel. Deduplicate on (name, link).

functions.name: Favicon icons
functions.what: Web quicklinks show the site's favicon automatically.
functions.macos_build: Use the Favicon Provider service (DuckDuckGo or Google favicon endpoint, or the LPMetadataProvider iconProvider) and cache to disk.

functions.name: Launcher-opening quicklink trick
functions.what: A quicklink pointing at the app's own URL scheme can open the launcher, which allows a second hotkey gesture for it.
functions.macos_build: Handle `digup://` with no path in `application(_:open:)` by showing the panel.

functions.name: Shared Quicklinks (Teams)
functions.what: Quicklinks shared with an organization, marked with the organization's avatar, synced to all members, and movable between personal and organization accounts.
functions.macos_build: Needs a sync backend. A CloudKit shared database with `CKShare` could replace Raycast's servers, or a simple shared JSON in iCloud Drive (`FileManager.url(forUbiquityContainerIdentifier:)`).

notes: Used by Quicklinks, Snippets and AI Commands. All local except {browser-tab} (needs Raycast's browser extension) and the AI Commands context ({selection} meaning 'previous message' in AI Chat, and the default triple-quote wrapping for AI). {clipboard offset=N} needs a Clipboard History store.

functions.name: {clipboard} and {clipboard offset=N}
functions.what: Inserts the latest copied text, or an older clipboard entry by position.
functions.macos_build: Read `NSPasteboard.general.string(forType: .string)`. Offsets read from a clipboard-history store fed by polling `NSPasteboard.general.changeCount` about every 0.5 s.

functions.name: {selection}
functions.what: Inserts the text selected in the frontmost app.
functions.macos_build: AX `kAXSelectedTextAttribute` on the focused element, with a ⌘C-and-restore fallback (see Quick Search).

functions.name: {date} {time} {datetime} {day}
functions.what: Insert the current date, time, both, or the weekday.
functions.macos_build: `DateFormatter` with dateStyle and timeStyle per token. `{day}` uses the 'EEEE' format.

functions.name: Date/time offsets
functions.what: Shifts any date token by signed amounts in minutes (m), hours (h), days (d), months (M) or years (y), several at once, e.g. offset="+2y +5M".
functions.macos_build: Parse each `[+-]\d+[mhdMy]` term (case-sensitive) and apply `Calendar.current.date(byAdding:value:to:)` in sequence.

functions.name: Custom date format
functions.what: Formats dates with a pattern string such as yyyy-MM-dd or EEEE, MMM d, yyyy, quoted literals included. It can be combined with offsets but not with locale.
functions.macos_build: `DateFormatter.dateFormat = pattern`. Unicode TR35 patterns match the documented syntax.

functions.name: Date locale
functions.what: Formats a date token for a given locale, e.g. fr-FR, or en-US-u-hc-h23 to force 24-hour time.
functions.macos_build: `DateFormatter.locale = Locale(identifier:)`. Reject identifiers missing from `Locale.availableIdentifiers`. BCP-47 extensions like -u-hc-h23 are honored.

functions.name: {uuid}
functions.what: Inserts a fresh unique identifier.
functions.macos_build: `UUID().uuidString`.

functions.name: {argument} with name / default / options
functions.what: Asks for a value in the search bar (up to 3 distinct arguments). Arguments are required unless they have a default. The same name shares one value, and options= shows a dropdown.
functions.macos_build: The parser collects argument specs in order and the inline argument UI renders TextField or Picker. Substitute after collection.

functions.name: {snippet name="…"}
functions.what: Embeds another snippet's text, one level deep only.
functions.macos_build: Look up the snippet store by name. Don't expand nested snippet tokens.

functions.name: {cursor}
functions.what: Snippets only: sets where the caret lands after pasting.
functions.macos_build: After pasting, post ← (kVK_LeftArrow) CGEvents for the number of characters after the marker, measured in UTF-16 units.

functions.name: {calculator}
functions.what: Evaluates a math expression and inserts the result.
functions.macos_build: Call the Calculator engine's `evaluate(_:)`.

functions.name: {browser-tab} with format / selector
functions.what: AI Commands only: inserts the focused browser tab's content as markdown, plain text or HTML, optionally limited to a CSS selector.
functions.macos_build: Without a browser extension: Safari `do JavaScript "document.querySelector(sel).innerText" in front document` (needs Develop › Allow JavaScript from Apple Events). Chrome: `execute active tab of front window javascript …` (needs View › Developer › Allow JavaScript from Apple Events). Convert HTML to markdown in Swift.

functions.name: Modifiers (uppercase, lowercase, trim, percent-encode, json-stringify, raw)
functions.what: Transform a placeholder's value with chainable pipes, e.g. {clipboard | trim | uppercase}. raw turns off the default formatting, which is percent-encoding in quicklinks and triple-quote wrapping in AI commands.
functions.macos_build: Pipeline of String transforms: `uppercased()`, `lowercased()`, `trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)`, `addingPercentEncoding(withAllowedCharacters:)`, and `JSONEncoder().encode(value)` with the outer quotes stripped. Apply the context's default only when raw is absent.

notes: Also from manual.raycast.com/calculator, the v1 manual and the changelog for Calculator History. Basic math, units, dates, time zones and colors work offline. Currency and crypto need network and Raycast serves the rates, so a fork needs its own source (ECB, Open Exchange Rates, CoinGecko). Shortcut docs disagree: the marketing page has ⌘↵ paste the answer into the search bar for a new calculation and ⌘⇧↵ replace the question with the answer, while the v2 manual has ⌘↵ paste into the active app, ⌥⌘C copy unformatted and ⌥⇧⌘C copy question and answer. History keeps entries for 3 months (pinned ones forever) per the Windows changelog. macOS retention isn't stated. Don't use NSExpression: it raises ObjC exceptions on bad input and has no units.

functions.name: Inline evaluation in Root Search
functions.what: Any expression typed in root search shows the question on the left and a live answer on the right, with no command to open.
functions.macos_build: A Calculator root provider runs a hand-written tokenizer and Pratt parser in Swift to an AST of `Quantity(value: Decimal|Double, unit: Dimension?, kind)`. It returns nil fast for non-math queries so other results aren't delayed. Render as a two-column card at the top.

functions.name: Arithmetic, powers, roots, trig
functions.what: Basic operators, powers ('2 power 10'), square roots ('square root of 625'), and trig including cot and csc with hyperbolic and inverse forms (sinh, acos…).
functions.macos_build: Map functions to Foundation/Darwin `pow`, `sqrt`, `sin`/`cos`/`tan`, `sinh`, `asin`, `acos`, with cot = 1/tan and csc = 1/sin. Handle degree/radian units through `UnitAngle`. Add an English-phrase grammar ('power', 'square root of', 'times').

functions.name: Percentages
functions.what: Percent of a value ('52% of 900'), discounts ('20% off 80'), percent added to a quantity ('19m + 47%'), and the percentage between two values.
functions.macos_build: Grammar rules: `x% of y` = y·x/100, `x% off y` = y·(1−x/100), `a ± x%` = a·(1±x/100), `a is what % of b` = a/b·100. Preserve the unit of `a`.

functions.name: Unit conversions
functions.what: Converts length, volume, temperature, mass and similar units ('10ft in m', '23C to F', '3 teaspoon in ml'), including compound rates like '8 dollars/hour in gbp'.
functions.macos_build: Foundation `Measurement` with UnitLength, UnitVolume, UnitTemperature, UnitMass, UnitArea, UnitSpeed, UnitDuration, UnitInformationStorage, UnitEnergy, UnitPressure, UnitAngle and UnitFrequency, plus an alias table ('ft/feet/foot', 'in/inch/inches', 'tsp/teaspoon', 'C/°C/celsius'). A rate is a (numerator, denominator) unit pair. Format with `MeasurementFormatter` (unitOptions .providedUnit).

functions.name: CSS and design units
functions.what: Converts rem/em to and from px using a configurable base (16 by default), and physical sizes to pixels at a given density ('2 inches in px at 72 ppi').
functions.macos_build: A custom `Dimension` subclass `UnitScreen` (px base, rem = basePx, em = basePx). Physical→px uses value_in_inches × ppi parsed from the 'at N ppi' clause.

functions.name: Currency conversion
functions.what: Converts between fiat currencies ('10 usd in gbp', '45 jpy to inr'), including shorthand like 'USD1K' and '10K'. Rates refresh in the background.
functions.macos_build: Fetch rates from the ECB daily reference XML (eurofxref-daily.xml, about 30 currencies) or a keyed API, cache JSON in Application Support, and refresh with `NSBackgroundActivityScheduler` every 1–6 h. Get codes from `Locale.commonISOCurrencyCodes` plus a symbol and name table ('$', '£', 'dollars', 'yen'). Use Decimal math and show the rate timestamp.

functions.name: Crypto conversion
functions.what: Converts cryptocurrencies to fiat or other coins, e.g. '5 btc in gbp'.
functions.macos_build: CoinGecko `/api/v3/simple/price?ids=…&vs_currencies=…` (or another free API) with a symbol→id map. Cache and refresh like fiat.

functions.name: Time zone conversion
functions.what: Converts a time between places ('5pm ldn in sf') and shows the current time somewhere ('time in Tokyo'). Accepts cities, multi-word names, airports (JFK) and tourist spots.
functions.macos_build: Use `TimeZone(identifier:)` with IANA IDs. Map place names to zones with a bundled gazetteer: GeoNames cities15000 (it has a timezone column), an IATA airport→tz list (OurAirports), and an alias table for 'ldn', 'sf' and 'nyc'. Unknown names can fall back to `CLGeocoder().geocodeAddressString` → `CLPlacemark.timeZone` (network, rate-limited). Display with `DateFormatter.timeZone`.

functions.name: Time difference
functions.what: Shows the offset between your zone and a place ('time diff Paris' or just 'diff Paris').
functions.macos_build: `tz.secondsFromGMT(for: now) - TimeZone.current.secondsFromGMT(for: now)`, formatted as ±h:mm.

functions.name: Relative time and time arithmetic
functions.what: Clock-time math, optionally in another city and safe across DST: 'time in 4 hours', 'time in 4 hours in San Francisco', 'time in brisbane + 4 hours', '3:45pm + 5'.
functions.macos_build: Build a `Calendar(identifier: .gregorian)` with `timeZone` set to the target and use `date(byAdding: .hour, …)`, so DST transitions are handled by Foundation.

functions.name: Date arithmetic and natural dates
functions.what: Works out dates from phrases: 'monday in 3 weeks', '35 days ago', 'August 5 + 5' (adds days), plus the keywords now, today, tomorrow, yesterday and time.
functions.macos_build: A grammar for weekday names, 'in N units', 'N units ago' and month-day literals. Use `Calendar.nextDate(after:matching:matchingPolicy:)` for weekdays and `date(byAdding:)` for offsets. `NSDataDetector(types: .date)` can parse loose date literals. Format with `DateFormatter` (dateStyle .full).

functions.name: Countdowns
functions.what: Days remaining until a date, e.g. 'days until 25 Dec' or a quarter-end.
functions.macos_build: `Calendar.current.dateComponents([.day], from: startOfToday, to: target).day`, rolling to next year if the date has passed.

functions.name: Durations to timespan
functions.what: Turns a raw duration into a readable span ('145 mins to timespan' gives 2 hours, 25 minutes).
functions.macos_build: `DateComponentsFormatter` with `unitsStyle = .full` and `allowedUnits = [.day, .hour, .minute, .second]`.

functions.name: Work planning
functions.what: Counts working hours in a year ('workhours in 2023') and converts hours into workdays ('55h in workdays').
functions.macos_build: Enumerate the year's dates with `Calendar.enumerateDates` and count weekdays 2–6 × 8 h. Workdays = hours / 8. Holidays are ignored unless you add a table.

functions.name: ISO 8601 timestamp parsing
functions.what: Recognizes Zulu timestamps like 2024-03-15T14:30:00Z and shows them in local time.
functions.macos_build: `ISO8601DateFormatter` with `[.withInternetDateTime, .withFractionalSeconds]` (try both option sets), then format locally.

functions.name: Color conversion and preview
functions.what: Detects colors in hex (3, 4, 6 or 8 digits), rgb/rgba, hsl/hsla, hwb, lab, lch, oklab and oklch and shows a swatch. ↵ opens Copy Color as… with 15 formats, including NSColor and UIColor initializers. Named colors like 'red' are not converted.
functions.macos_build: Regex parsers for the CSS Color 4 syntaxes (percentages, 'none', slash alpha). Convert through linear sRGB and XYZ-D65 (Lab/LCH use D50 with Bradford adaptation) and use the CSS Color 4 reference matrices for OKLab. Preview with `NSColor(srgbRed:green:blue:alpha:)`. Emit strings such as `NSColor(srgbRed: 1.0, green: 0.388, blue: 0.388, alpha: 1.0)` and `UIColor(red:green:blue:alpha:)`. Setting: Enable Color Conversion.

functions.name: Copy / paste result actions
functions.what: Copy the formatted answer, paste it into the active app (or, per the marketing page, back into the search bar to keep calculating), copy the unformatted number, copy question and answer, or replace the query with the answer.
functions.keys: ↵ copy; ⌘↵ paste; ⌥⌘C copy unformatted; ⌥⇧⌘C copy question+answer; ⌘⇧↵ replace query with answer (marketing page)
functions.macos_build: Use NSPasteboard. Paste-into-app hides the panel, calls `previousApp.activate()`, then posts ⌘V via CGEvent to `.cghidEventTap` after about 50 ms. Replace-query sets the search text to the raw result.

functions.name: Calculator History
functions.what: Saves every calculation and conversion so you can search, browse and pin them. Pinned items stay live, e.g. currency rates or a countdown, and you can copy the question or put it back in the search bar.
functions.keys: 'Calculator History' command; also openable from a result
functions.macos_build: SQLite table `calc_history(id, expression, result, kind, created_at, pinned)`. Re-evaluate currency, time and countdown rows when displayed. Prune rows older than 90 days unless pinned.
functions.permission: none (network to refresh live currency rows)

functions.name: Number format and syntax highlighting
functions.what: Decimal and grouping separators follow the system's Language & Region setting. Expression parts are color-highlighted (on by default).
functions.macos_build: Read `Locale.current.decimalSeparator` and `.groupingSeparator` in the tokenizer and `NumberFormatter`. Observe `NSLocale.currentLocaleDidChangeNotification`. Highlight via `AttributedString` runs per token type.

notes: Sources: manual.raycast.com/search-bar, /settings, /quickstart, /new-in-v2 (www.raycast.com/manual 308-redirects to manual.raycast.com). The default launcher hotkey is given as Option-Space on fresh installs in Settings, while the Search Bar page says Cmd-Space. Quick AI on Tab and 'Quick AI as fallback' use Raycast AI (cloud, Pro models), so they are cloud-dependent unless a local LLM is used. Windows-only root items (Windows Settings, Control Panel tasks, Start Menu apps) are left out. Calculator is listed here only as a root-search result type. Its unit, currency, time-zone and date details belong in the Calculator catalog entry.

functions.name: Open / Toggle Raycast (global launcher hotkey)
functions.what: A system-wide shortcut opens the launcher with focus in the search field. Pressing it again hides the launcher.
functions.keys: Option-Space default (Cmd-Space if replacing Spotlight); configurable in Settings > General > Raycast Hotkey
functions.macos_build: Carbon RegisterEventHotKey, which DigUp's HotkeyCenter in Sources/DigUpApp/Hotkey.swift already uses, toggles a non-activating NSPanel (styleMask .nonactivatingPanel, level .floating, collectionBehavior [.moveToActiveSpace, .fullScreenAuxiliary]), so the previously frontmost app keeps frontmost status for later paste and menu actions. Record NSWorkspace.shared.frontmostApplication before showing the panel. To use Cmd-Space, the user must first disable the Spotlight shortcut under System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts > Spotlight.

functions.name: Search Applications
functions.what: Matches installed apps as you type and launches the selected one with Enter. It covers /Applications, system apps, ~/Applications, symlinked apps, Finder aliases and apps on newly mounted volumes.
functions.macos_build: Build the app index with NSMetadataQuery (predicate kMDItemContentTypeTree == 'com.apple.application-bundle', scopes /Applications, /System/Applications, ~/Applications, /System/Library/CoreServices/Applications), plus a FileManager walk that resolves symlinks and aliases (URL(resolvingAliasFileAt:)). Refresh on NSMetadataQueryDidUpdate, FSEvents and NSWorkspace.didMountNotification. Take the name from FileManager.displayName(atPath:) and the icon from NSWorkspace.shared.icon(forFile:). Launch with NSWorkspace.shared.openApplication(at:configuration:). Fuzzy-match in memory.

functions.name: Alternate App Names / Spotlight keywords
functions.what: Apps also match their alternate or legacy names and keywords, so 'iCal' finds Calendar and 'Preferences' finds System Settings.
functions.macos_build: Index kMDItemAlternateNames and kMDItemKeywords from NSMetadataItem, every localized CFBundleDisplayName and CFBundleName from the bundle's *.lproj/InfoPlist.strings, and a small bundled synonym table keyed by bundle ID (com.apple.iCal -> 'ical', com.apple.systempreferences -> 'preferences').

functions.name: Search Commands
functions.what: Built-in commands, and extension commands in Raycast, appear in the root results next to apps.
functions.macos_build: A native command registry (protocol LauncherCommand { id, title, subtitle, keywords, icon, arguments, run(args) }) that every feature in this catalog registers into. Root search fuzzy-matches title, subtitle and keywords. A native fork does not need a JS extension runtime.

functions.name: Files & Folders in Root Search (+ recent files)
functions.what: With file indexing on, matching files and folders appear in root search. An empty query lists recently used files.
functions.macos_build: Merge DigUp's existing keyword and EmbeddingGemma semantic results into the root list as a lower-priority section. Debounce it, because embedding queries are slower than the in-memory app match. For recent files, query NSMetadataQuery sorted by kMDItemLastUsedDate descending (LaunchServices updates it on open), or log opens made through the launcher in DigUp's SQLite store.
functions.permission: none for folders DigUp already indexes; Files & Folders prompts for Desktop/Documents/Downloads; Full Disk Access for protected locations

functions.name: Go to Parent Directory
functions.what: With a file or folder selected, steps up to its enclosing folder and lists that folder's contents.
functions.macos_build: FileManager.contentsOfDirectory(at: url.deletingLastPathComponent(), includingPropertiesForKeys: [.isDirectoryKey, .contentModificationDateKey]) shown as a pushed list view on the navigation stack.
functions.permission: Files & Folders for protected user folders

functions.name: Upcoming Calendar Event in Root Search
functions.what: An empty query shows today's next event at the top, ready to join or open.
functions.macos_build: EventKit. Call EKEventStore.requestFullAccessToEvents on macOS 14+, with NSCalendarsFullAccessUsageDescription in Info.plist. Use predicateForEvents(withStart:end:calendars:) over the enabled calendars, filter out all-day events and events where the current user's EKParticipant status is declined, and refresh on .EKEventStoreChanged.

functions.name: Search Contacts
functions.what: Filters Apple Contacts inline as you type. Actions copy phone, email or address, or open the card in Contacts. Off by default.
functions.macos_build: Contacts.framework. Call CNContactStore.requestAccess(for: .contacts), with NSContactsUsageDescription in Info.plist. Query unifiedContacts(matching: CNContact.predicateForContacts(matchingName:), keysToFetch: name, organization, phones, emails, addresses, thumbnail), cache in memory and refresh on .CNContactStoreDidChange. Open a card with NSWorkspace.open(URL(string: "addressbook://" + contact.identifier)).

functions.name: Inline Calculator result
functions.what: Math expressions, conversions, date questions and currency questions typed into root search show an answer row you can copy.
functions.macos_build: Write a recursive-descent expression parser rather than using NSExpression, which raises ObjC exceptions on malformed input. Use Foundation Measurement/Dimension with MeasurementFormatter for units, NSDataDetector(.date) and Calendar.dateComponents for dates, and a cached exchange-rate feed for currency. The Calculator catalog has the details.

functions.name: Quicklinks in Root Search
functions.what: Saved links to URLs, files or folders are searchable root items.
functions.macos_build: Store rows of {name, template with {query}, openWith bundle ID, icon} in SQLite. Open with NSWorkspace.shared.open(_:withApplicationAt:configuration:), percent-encoding the substituted argument. The Quicklinks catalog has the details.

functions.name: System Settings panes
functions.what: Individual System Settings panes, such as Accessibility > Zoom, are root results that open directly to that pane.
functions.macos_build: Enumerate settings extensions in /System/Library/ExtensionKit/Extensions/*.appex on macOS 13+, reading the display name and bundle ID from each Info.plist, plus legacy *.prefPane bundles in /Library/PreferencePanes and ~/Library/PreferencePanes. Open with NSWorkspace.open(URL(string: "x-apple.systempreferences:<pane id>[?anchor]")). Sub-section anchors need a hand-maintained table, because they change between macOS releases.

functions.name: URL Detection
functions.what: Recognizes a typed URL or bare domain and offers to open it, adding https:// when the scheme is missing. Browsers and other URL-capable commands are shown as options.
functions.macos_build: Run NSDataDetector(types: NSTextCheckingResult.CheckingType.link.rawValue) on the query and require the match to cover the whole string. Prefix https:// when there is no scheme. List handlers with NSWorkspace.shared.urlsForApplications(toOpen:) on macOS 12+ and open with NSWorkspace.open(_:withApplicationAt:configuration:).

functions.name: Color Conversion
functions.what: A typed color value (hex, rgb, hsl, oklch) shows a preview swatch and can be copied in the other formats.
functions.macos_build: Regex parsers for each notation. Convert through sRGB: NSColor(srgbRed:green:blue:alpha:), hand-written HSL math, and Björn Ottosson's published OKLab/OKLCH matrices. Draw the swatch with NSColor and copy with NSPasteboard. The toggle lives under Calculator settings.

functions.name: Command Arguments
functions.what: A command can declare up to three inline inputs (text, password or dropdown). They appear in the search bar when the command is selected, and Enter runs it with those values.
functions.keys: Left/Right arrows move between fields; Enter runs; alias + Space jumps to the first field
functions.macos_build: A per-command argument schema. When the command is selected, render up to three NSTextField, NSSecureTextField or NSPopUpButton controls (or SwiftUI TextField/SecureField/Picker) to the right of the query field. Route arrow keys through NSEvent.addLocalMonitorForEvents(matching: .keyDown) and pass the values to run(args).

functions.name: Ranking & Frecency
functions.what: Orders results by exact alias match, then alias prefix, then fuzzy title score, then subtitle and keyword matches, then by how often and how recently you picked each item.
functions.macos_build: A SQLite table (DigUp already ships SQLite in DigUpKit/Database.swift) of (query_prefix, item_id, count, last_used). Score = fuzzy score + log(count) weighted by exponential time decay, with the alias tiers sorted first. Use an fzf-style subsequence scorer with word-boundary and camel-case bonuses.

functions.name: Reset Ranking
functions.what: An Action Panel action that clears the learned frecency and search terms for one command.
functions.macos_build: DELETE FROM frecency WHERE item_id = ?

functions.name: Root Search Sensitivity
functions.what: A Low/Medium/High setting for how loosely fuzzy matching admits results. Low shows more results and High shows fewer, closer matches.
functions.macos_build: Map each level to a minimum fuzzy-score threshold and to whether non-contiguous or any-substring matches are allowed. Store it in UserDefaults.

functions.name: Search History
functions.what: When the selection is at the top or bottom of the list, Up/Down cycles back through previously typed queries. The history can be reset in Settings.
functions.macos_build: Keep a ring buffer of the last N submitted queries in SQLite or UserDefaults. Intercept arrow keys when the selection index is at an edge.

functions.name: Compact Window Mode
functions.what: With an empty query, only the search field is shown. Results expand as you type or open the Action Panel, and the window collapses when it loses focus. Favorites can optionally show as an icon row.
functions.macos_build: Animate the NSPanel frame height between field-only and full size with setFrame(_:display:animate:) or NSAnimationContext, and collapse in windowDidResignKey. Store 'Compact' or 'Expanded' in UserDefaults.

functions.name: Pop to Root Search (timeout)
functions.what: Once the launcher has been inactive for a set time (Immediately up to 180 seconds), reopening it returns to root search instead of the last open command.
functions.macos_build: Store a timestamp when the panel hides. On the next show, compare it with the setting and reset the navigation stack if the timeout has passed.

functions.name: Show Raycast on (screen choice)
functions.what: Places the window on the screen containing the mouse, the screen with the active window, or the primary screen.
functions.macos_build: Mouse: the NSScreen whose frame contains NSEvent.mouseLocation. Active window: the first layer-0 entry for the frontmost pid in CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo([.optionOnScreenOnly, .excludeDesktopElements], kCGNullWindowID), using kCGWindowBounds converted from top-left to Cocoa coordinates. Bounds need no permission; only window titles require Screen Recording. Primary: NSScreen.screens[0].

functions.name: Customize Search (Files / Contacts toggles)
functions.what: Settings switches that add Files and Contacts to root results or remove them.
functions.macos_build: UserDefaults flags that gate each result provider in the root aggregator.

functions.name: Quick AI from Root Search
functions.what: Tab sends the current query to a quick one-off AI answer instead of running a command.
functions.macos_build: Either a cloud LLM over URLSession with streaming (needs an API key), or a local instruct GGUF run in DigUp's existing llama.cpp worker (LlamaRuntime). Show the answer in a pushed view with copy and paste actions.

notes: The manual gives conflicting shortcuts. Add to Favorites is Cmd-F on the Keyboard Shortcuts page but Shift-Cmd-F in the Action Panel summary. Move Up/Down is Shift-Cmd-Up/Down on one page and Cmd-Up/Down on another. All of this is local data, though Raycast syncs it through Cloud Sync (Pro).

functions.name: Favorites section in empty Root Search
functions.what: Pinned commands, apps or items stay at the top of an empty root search, in their own section above other results.
functions.macos_build: A favorites table (item_id, position) in SQLite. The empty-query provider renders this section first, in position order.

functions.name: Add to Favorites
functions.what: Pins the selected item to the favorites section.
functions.macos_build: INSERT the item into the favorites table with position = max+1, exposed as an action-model entry.

functions.name: Remove from Favorites
functions.what: Unpins the item.
functions.macos_build: DELETE from the favorites table and renumber positions.

functions.name: Move Favorite Up / Move Favorite Down
functions.what: Reorders a favorite within the favorites section.
functions.keys: Shift-Cmd-Up / Shift-Cmd-Down (Keyboard page); Cmd-Up / Cmd-Down (Action Panel page)
functions.macos_build: Swap the position values of adjacent rows in a single transaction.

functions.name: Show Favorites in Compact Mode
functions.what: In compact window mode, favorites can appear as a row of icons under the search field.
functions.macos_build: A horizontal icon strip (SwiftUI HStack) shown when the setting is on and the query is empty.

notes: Fully local. Raycast syncs aliases through Cloud Sync and includes them in .rayconfig export.

functions.name: Set Alias
functions.what: Gives a command a short keyword. Typing the keyword in root search puts that command at the top, and the alias shows as a tag next to the command.
functions.keys: Shift-Cmd-, (Configure Command) > Set Alias, then Enter; also Settings > Shortcuts 'Add Alias' field
functions.macos_build: Store an alias column on the command record. Validate and normalize to lowercase letters, numbers and spaces, and display spaces as the open-box symbol. Edit it from the Action Panel sub-view or a SwiftUI Table cell in Settings.

functions.name: Delete Alias
functions.what: Removes the alias from a command. Shown only when an alias is set.
functions.macos_build: Set the alias column to NULL.

functions.name: Alias prefix matching
functions.what: Aliases match by strict prefix, not fuzzy matching. An exact match ranks above everything and a partial prefix ranks lower.
functions.macos_build: Check aliases before fuzzy matching: an exact match gets tier 0 and query.hasPrefix gets tier 1. See Ranking.

functions.name: Alias + Space opens arguments
functions.what: Typing an alias followed by a space moves focus straight into the command's first argument field.
functions.macos_build: When the query equals 'alias ' and the command declares arguments, select that command and focus argument field 0.

notes: Ordinary key+modifier hotkeys need no permission through Carbon. Modifier-only, double-tap, side-specific, fn and both-sided hotkeys need a CGEventTap or NSEvent global monitor, which requires Input Monitoring or Accessibility. On Windows, Raycast also supports the Windows key as a modifier.

functions.name: Set Hotkey (recorder)
functions.what: Records a global shortcut that runs a command even when the launcher is hidden. Keys show live as you press them. It saves automatically after about 1.5 seconds, or immediately with Enter.
functions.keys: Configure Command > Set Hotkey; Enter saves; Backspace or the clear button clears; Settings > Shortcuts > Record Hotkey
functions.macos_build: A recorder view captures keyDown and flagsChanged with NSEvent.addLocalMonitorForEvents while the panel is key. Suspend existing Carbon hotkeys while recording (HotkeyCenter.suspend()), then register with RegisterEventHotKey(keyCode, carbonModifiers, EventHotKeyID, GetApplicationEventTarget(), 0, &ref). Persist (keyCode, modifiers) per command. F1-F24, arrows, Return, Tab, Escape, Delete, Home, End and Page Up/Down are all valid key codes.

functions.name: Delete Hotkey
functions.what: Removes a command's global shortcut.
functions.keys: Configure Command > Delete Hotkey; clear button in Settings
functions.macos_build: UnregisterEventHotKey(ref) and clear the stored combo.

functions.name: Hotkey conflict detection / overwrite
functions.what: Warns in red when another command already uses the combination, naming that command, and lets you overwrite it (the other command loses its hotkey). The launcher's own hotkey can't be overwritten ('Already used by Raycast'). Incompatible pairs, such as a single Option tap alongside an Option double tap, get a red dot.
functions.macos_build: Check the app's own registry first. Detect system-reserved combos with Carbon CopySymbolicHotKeys(), which lists enabled system shortcuts such as Spotlight and Mission Control, and treat RegisterEventHotKey returning eventHotKeyExistsErr as a conflict.

functions.name: Multi-modifier hotkeys (modifiers only)
functions.what: Hotkeys made only of modifiers, such as Option-Cmd.
functions.macos_build: Carbon can't register these. Use a listen-only CGEventTap on kCGEventFlagsChanged (request with CGRequestListenEventAccess) or NSEvent.addGlobalMonitorForEvents(matching: .flagsChanged). Fire on release when exactly that modifier set was down and no keyDown happened in between.
functions.permission: Input Monitoring (listen-only tap) or Accessibility (NSEvent global monitor)

functions.name: Double-tap modifier hotkeys
functions.what: Pressing the same modifier twice, releasing between presses, triggers the command (e.g. Cmd Cmd).
functions.macos_build: Use the same flagsChanged tap to detect two press/release cycles of one modifier within about 300 ms with no other key in between.

functions.name: Single-tap side-specific modifier hotkeys
functions.what: One modifier alone, with left and right keys treated as different hotkeys (e.g. Right Cmd). Clicking the key in the recorder cycles left, right and either side.
functions.macos_build: The flagsChanged keyCode identifies the side: kVK_Command 55 / kVK_RightCommand 54, kVK_Option 58 / kVK_RightOption 61, kVK_Shift 56 / kVK_RightShift 60, kVK_Control 59 / kVK_RightControl 62. The device-dependent CGEventFlags bits (NX_DEVICELCMDKEYMASK 0x08, NX_DEVICERCMDKEYMASK 0x10, and so on) also distinguish them.

functions.name: Both-sided modifier hotkeys
functions.what: Holding both keys of one modifier together, such as Left Cmd + Right Cmd, triggers the command. Adding a regular key turns it back into an ordinary shortcut.
functions.macos_build: In the flagsChanged tap, fire when both device-side bits for one modifier are set at the same time.

functions.name: fn and F13-F18 single-key hotkeys
functions.what: The fn key alone, or an extended-keyboard key such as F13-F18, can be a hotkey, alone or combined (e.g. fn-A, Cmd-F13).
functions.macos_build: F13-F18 register normally with RegisterEventHotKey (kVK_F13 = 105 and so on). For fn alone, watch flagsChanged with keyCode 63 (kVK_Function) and the .function flag in the event tap. The user must first set 'Press globe key to: Do Nothing' in System Settings > Keyboard.
functions.permission: none for F-keys; Input Monitoring for fn

functions.name: Physical key vs key-equivalent recording
functions.what: Hotkeys are recorded as physical key positions by default, so they stay in place across layouts. They can instead be bound to the character, which is marked with a blue dot.
functions.macos_build: Store the virtual keyCode for physical mode. For character mode, map character to keyCode for the current layout with TISCopyCurrentKeyboardLayoutInputSource + UCKeyTranslate, and re-register on the kTISNotifySelectedKeyboardInputSourceChanged distributed notification.

functions.name: Shortcuts settings page
functions.what: One settings table of every command with its alias and hotkey. It supports search, category filters and 'Hotkey Set' / 'Alias Set' filters for auditing, and you can edit inline.
functions.macos_build: A SwiftUI Table bound to the command registry with a searchable modifier, a filter Picker, and inline recorder and alias cells.

notes: The manual disagrees with itself on several shortcuts. Configure Command is Shift-Cmd-, on one page and Cmd-, on another. Configure Extension is Option-Cmd-, or Shift-Cmd-,. Disable Command is Shift-Cmd-D or Ctrl-Shift-Cmd-D. Extension-defined actions with destructive (red) styling belong to Raycast's JS extension API and aren't needed natively.

functions.name: Open / Close Action Panel
functions.what: Shows every action available for the selected item, grouped into sections such as Favorites, Configure, Deeplink and Manage.
functions.keys: Cmd-K toggles; Esc closes or leaves a sub-menu
functions.macos_build: A child NSPanel or popover anchored to the bottom-right of the launcher, with its own filter field. Each item type supplies [ActionSection]. Keep a small navigation stack for sub-menus.

functions.name: Primary Action
functions.what: The first action in the list runs immediately on Enter, e.g. Open for apps, Run Command for commands, Open for files.
functions.macos_build: actions.first?.perform() on Enter.

functions.name: Secondary Action
functions.what: The second action runs directly, for example Show in Finder for apps or Join for calendar events.
functions.macos_build: actions[1] on Cmd-Enter, via a keyDown monitor.

functions.name: Tertiary Action
functions.what: The third action runs directly.
functions.macos_build: actions[2] on Option-Enter.

functions.name: Search for actions
functions.what: Typing inside the panel fuzzy-filters actions by name into one flat list.
functions.macos_build: Flatten the sections and reuse the root fuzzy scorer.

functions.name: Sub-menus and inline views
functions.what: Some actions open a sub-menu (Configure Command) or a custom view inside the panel (the hotkey recorder). Esc returns to the main list.
functions.macos_build: Push and pop views on the panel's navigation stack.

functions.name: Configure Command
functions.what: A sub-menu with Set Hotkey, Set Alias, Open Command Settings and Configure Extension, plus Delete Hotkey and Delete Alias when those are set.
functions.macos_build: A sub-menu built from the command record. 'Open Command Settings' opens the Settings window scrolled to that command.

functions.name: Configure Extension
functions.what: Opens the settings page of the extension or feature that owns the command.
functions.macos_build: Open the Settings window at that feature's pane.

functions.name: Disable Command
functions.what: Hides a command from root search. It can be re-enabled in Settings > Extensions.
functions.macos_build: An enabled flag on the command record that root search filters on.

functions.name: Copy Deeplink
functions.what: Copies a URL that launches the command directly from anywhere, such as a browser, script or another launcher hotkey.
functions.macos_build: Declare CFBundleURLTypes (e.g. digup://commands/<id>?arguments=<json>) and handle it in NSApplicationDelegate application(_:open:) or with an NSAppleEventManager kAEGetURL handler. Copy with NSPasteboard. A quicklink to the app's own scheme also lets double-tap and both-sided hotkeys open the launcher.

functions.name: File/folder actions
functions.what: Open, Open With..., Show in Finder, Copy Path, Move to Trash and Quick Look for file results.
functions.keys: Cmd-O open; Option-Cmd-O Open With; Shift-Cmd-O reveal; Cmd-Y Quick Look
functions.macos_build: Open: NSWorkspace.open. Open With: list NSWorkspace.urlsForApplications(toOpen:), then open(_:withApplicationAt:configuration:). Reveal: activateFileViewerSelecting([url]). Copy Path: NSPasteboard. Trash: FileManager.trashItem(at:resultingItemURL:). Quick Look: QLPreviewPanel.shared(), and DigUp's SearchPanelWindow already implements QLPreviewPanelDataSource.

functions.name: Common item action slots
functions.what: Shared shortcuts across all item types: edit, show info, duplicate, pin/unpin, show hidden, copy and secondary copy, paste and secondary paste, delete, delete all.
functions.keys: Cmd-E edit; Cmd-I info; Cmd-D duplicate; Cmd-. pin; Shift-Cmd-. show hidden; Cmd-C / Shift-Cmd-C copy; Cmd-V / Shift-Cmd-V paste; Ctrl-X delete; Ctrl-Shift-X delete all
functions.macos_build: Add standard shortcut slots to the action model so each feature binds to them consistently. Paste works like this: write to NSPasteboard, hide the panel, call activate() on the previous NSRunningApplication, then post Cmd-V with CGEvent(keyboardEventSource:virtualKey: kVK_ANSI_V, keyDown:) with .maskCommand to .cghidEventTap. Check CGPreflightPostEventAccess and ask with CGRequestPostEventAccess.

notes: The v2 manual only says Settings > Launcher > Fallback Commands lets you add, reorder or remove them. The v1 page has the detail. Making Quick AI the fallback (new in v2) depends on Raycast AI (cloud). Web-search fallbacks need only a browser.

functions.name: Fallback results on no match
functions.what: When nothing matches, shows a configurable list of commands that take the typed text as input, such as web search or file search.
functions.keys: Enter runs the selected fallback with the query
functions.macos_build: When the result count is 0, render the enabled fallbacks in order and pass the query as their single argument. A web search is a quicklink template (e.g. https://www.google.com/search?q={query}) opened with NSWorkspace.open. A file-search fallback calls DigUp's semantic search.

functions.name: Manage Fallback Commands
functions.what: A command and settings section with an Enabled list and an Available list. Enter enables an item, and the favorites shortcuts reorder the list. It's also reachable from the gear icon in the no-results header.
functions.keys: Enter enable; reorder with the favorites move shortcuts
functions.macos_build: An ordered fallback table in SQLite. Any command with exactly one argument (quicklinks with {query}, script commands) is eligible.

functions.name: Quick AI as fallback
functions.what: Sends queries that match no command to an AI answer.
functions.macos_build: Register Quick AI as a fallback command. Use a cloud LLM via URLSession or a local llama.cpp model in DigUp's worker.

notes: Navigation bindings, the Escape behavior and page keys are Settings > Keyboard options. The AI Chat shortcuts on the same page (history sidebar, model switch, branch chat and so on) belong to the cloud AI feature and are left out here. LSUIElement/accessory apps have no main menu by default, so you must install NSApp.mainMenu with an Edit menu, or handle performKeyEquivalent, for Cmd-A/C/X/V/Z to work in text fields.

functions.name: Move selection
functions.what: Moves the selection up or down the list.
functions.macos_build: Handle these in the NSPanel subclass keyDown, an NSEvent local monitor, or SwiftUI .onKeyPress (macOS 14+), and update the selection index in the list model. Scroll with ScrollViewReader.scrollTo.

functions.name: Jump to previous / next section
functions.what: Moves the selection to the first item of the adjacent section.
functions.macos_build: Keep the section boundary indices in the list model.

functions.name: Jump to previous / next page
functions.what: Scrolls one visible page of results.
functions.keys: Option-Up / Option-Down (or square brackets, per Page Navigation Keys setting)
functions.macos_build: Move by the number of visible rows (row height / viewport height). A setting chooses '[' ']' or arrow keys.

functions.name: Emacs navigation bindings (default)
functions.what: Ctrl-N/P move down and up, and Ctrl-F/B move right and left.
functions.macos_build: Ctrl-key mapping in the local key monitor. NSTextField already supports Ctrl-F/B for the cursor.

functions.name: Vim navigation bindings (optional)
functions.what: Ctrl-J/K move down and up, and Ctrl-L/H move right and left.
functions.macos_build: An alternate keymap toggled in Settings > Keyboard > Navigation Bindings.

functions.name: Escape / go back (with Escape Key Behavior setting)
functions.what: Esc clears the query, goes back a level, or closes the window from root. A setting chooses between 'Navigate back or close window' and 'Close window and pop to root', and another can stop Esc from closing the window.
functions.macos_build: cancelOperation(_:) in the panel pops the navigation stack, clears the query, or calls orderOut, depending on settings.

functions.name: Pop to Root
functions.what: Returns to root search from any depth.
functions.macos_build: Reset the navigation stack and clear the query.

functions.name: Backspace on empty query goes back
functions.what: Backspace on an empty search field navigates back one level.
functions.macos_build: In the key monitor, if the field text is empty and keyCode == kVK_Delete, pop the stack.

functions.name: Close window
functions.what: Closes the launcher window.
functions.macos_build: Call orderOut(nil) on the panel and restore focus to the previous app.

functions.name: Open Settings / Open User Guide
functions.what: Opens the preferences window or the manual.
functions.macos_build: Show a SwiftUI Settings scene or NSWindow. Open the help URL with NSWorkspace.open.

functions.name: Form navigation
functions.what: Tab and Shift-Tab move between form fields, Cmd-Enter submits, and Esc cancels.
functions.macos_build: NSWindow key-view loop (nextKeyView) or SwiftUI @FocusState, plus a Cmd-Enter handler.

notes: Account, Organizations, plan and billing, Cloud Sync, AI provider settings and Store themes depend on Raycast's cloud and are not replicable locally. Windows-only options (Use the Windows Key, Open Folders in Tabs, Run Accessibility Helper Elevated) are left out.

functions.name: Open at Login
functions.what: Starts the launcher automatically when you log in.
functions.macos_build: SMAppService.mainApp.register() / unregister() on macOS 13+.

functions.name: Show in Menu Bar
functions.what: Shows or hides the menu bar icon.
functions.macos_build: Set NSStatusItem.isVisible; DigUp already has StatusMenu.swift. On macOS 26 the user must also allow the item under System Settings > Menu Bar.

functions.name: Follow System Appearance / Themes
functions.what: Matches system light or dark mode automatically, or uses a chosen theme.
functions.macos_build: Set NSApp.appearance = nil to follow the system, or NSAppearance(named: .darkAqua / .aqua). Define custom themes as JSON color-token sets injected through the SwiftUI environment, and observe effectiveAppearance with KVO.

functions.name: Interface Size
functions.what: Default, Large or Larger UI scale for text and rows.
functions.macos_build: Apply a scale factor to font sizes and row heights (SwiftUI dynamicTypeSize or custom metrics).

functions.name: Window Activation Behavior
functions.what: Choose 'Move to Active Space', where the window appears on the current Space, or 'Switch Space'.
functions.macos_build: Toggle NSPanel.collectionBehavior between .moveToActiveSpace and the default. Add .fullScreenAuxiliary so the panel can appear over full-screen apps.

functions.name: Auto-switch Input Source
functions.what: Switches to a chosen keyboard input source while the launcher is open (useful for CJK users), and restores the previous one afterwards.
functions.macos_build: List sources with TISCreateInputSourceList filtered on kTISPropertyInputSourceIsSelectCapable. On show, save TISCopyCurrentKeyboardInputSource() and call TISSelectInputSource(chosen). Restore it on hide.

functions.name: Favicon Provider
functions.what: Chooses where website icons for quicklinks and URLs come from: DuckDuckGo, Google, Raycast or None.
functions.macos_build: Fetch https://icons.duckduckgo.com/ip3/<host>.ico or https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain=<host>&sz=64 with URLSession and cache the files in ~/Library/Caches.

functions.name: Proxy & custom certificate authority
functions.what: Uses the system proxy settings and optionally trusts an extra CA certificate (.crt, .cer or .pem).
functions.macos_build: URLSession uses the system proxy by default (CFNetworkCopySystemProxySettings). For an extra CA, implement urlSession(_:didReceive:completionHandler:) and evaluate SecTrust after SecTrustSetAnchorCertificates and SecTrustSetAnchorCertificatesOnly(false).

functions.name: Settings search
functions.what: Searches across all settings, extensions and commands.
functions.macos_build: Index setting labels and keywords, filter the sidebar and content, and scroll to the match.

functions.name: Extensions pane (enable/disable commands)
functions.what: Lists built-in commands, quicklinks and scripts with on/off switches and per-command preferences. Disabled commands are hidden from root search.
functions.macos_build: A SwiftUI List or Table over the command registry, with Toggle bound to each command's enabled flag.

notes: Fully local, but it is the most system-invasive feature in this catalog. Conflicts are likely with Karabiner-Elements and other HID remappers. Secure Event Input (password fields, some terminals) blocks event taps.

functions.name: Set Hyper Key
functions.what: Turns a rarely used key (Caps Lock, one side of a modifier, or F1-F12) into a key that sends Ctrl-Option-Cmd together. 'None' turns the feature off and restores Caps Lock.
functions.macos_build: At the HID layer, remap the source key to an unused one (Caps Lock 0x700000039 -> F18 0x70000006D) per keyboard service with IOHIDEventSystemClientCreateSimpleClient + IOHIDServiceClientSetProperty(service, 'UserKeyMapping', ...), the same mechanism as 'hidutil property --set'. Then install an active CGEventTap on keyDown, keyUp and flagsChanged that ORs .maskControl | .maskAlternate | .maskCommand into every key event while F18 is held, and swallows F18 itself. Re-apply the mapping when keyboards attach (IOHIDManager matching callback), and clear it on quit.

functions.name: Include Shift
functions.what: Adds Shift to the Hyper combination.
functions.macos_build: Also OR .maskShift into the event flags.

functions.name: Quick Press action
functions.what: Applies when the Hyper Key is Caps Lock or a function key. A lone tap can do nothing, act as the original key, or send Escape.
functions.macos_build: If the key goes down and up with no other keyDown in between and within about 200 ms, post a CGEvent for kVK_Escape, or toggle Caps Lock with IOHIDSetModifierLockState(connect, kIOHIDCapsLockState, ...).

functions.name: Secure Input Compatibility
functions.what: Keeps Hyper shortcuts working while another app holds Secure Input. The cost is that Right Control is reserved for Hyper.
functions.macos_build: Event taps receive nothing while IsSecureEventInputEnabled() is true. Instead, map the key to Right Control (0x7000000E4) through UserKeyMapping so a real Ctrl is held, and treat the right-control device bit as Hyper in the hotkey layer.

functions.name: Hyper glyph display
functions.what: Shows Ctrl-Option-Cmd shortcuts as a single star glyph. A 'Replace Ctrl-Option-Cmd with glyph' option does this even when no Hyper Key is set.
functions.macos_build: A shortcut-label formatter that collapses the modifier set.

functions.name: Hyper Key Diagnostic
functions.what: Shows whether the Hyper Key is active, what it's bound to, and any detected conflicts. A restart button reinstalls it without quitting the app.
functions.macos_build: Report the tap state (CGEvent.tapIsEnabled), the current UserKeyMapping, and IsSecureEventInputEnabled(). Detect Karabiner and similar tools by bundle ID in NSWorkspace.runningApplications. Restart tears down and recreates the tap and mapping.

notes: Windows-only actions are left out: Run as Administrator, Run as Different User, Show Advanced Options, and Microsoft Store uninstall. 'New Application Window' and 'Open Recent Files...' are listed with Ctrl shortcuts and look Windows-first. A macOS route is described below. The 'Run' feature (manual /run) is a Windows Run-dialog replacement and has no macOS equivalent to port. 'Treat as Game' feeds Raycast's Games feature.

functions.name: Open Application
functions.what: Launches the app, or brings it to the front if it's already running.
functions.macos_build: NSWorkspace.shared.openApplication(at:configuration:) with activates = true. If the app is already running, call NSRunningApplication.activate().

functions.name: Show in Finder
functions.what: Reveals the app bundle in Finder.
functions.macos_build: NSWorkspace.shared.activateFileViewerSelecting([appURL])

functions.name: Show Info in Finder
functions.what: Opens Finder's Get Info window for the app.
functions.macos_build: NSAppleScript: tell application "Finder" to open information window of (POSIX file "/Applications/X.app" as alias). Requires the com.apple.security.automation.apple-events entitlement and NSAppleEventsUsageDescription.

functions.name: Show Package Contents
functions.what: Opens the app bundle's Contents folder.
functions.macos_build: NSWorkspace.shared.open(appURL.appendingPathComponent("Contents"))

functions.name: Copy Path / Copy Name / Copy Bundle Identifier
functions.what: Copies the app's path, display name or bundle ID.
functions.keys: Option-Cmd-C path; Ctrl-Cmd-C name; Shift-Cmd-C bundle ID
functions.macos_build: Bundle(url:)?.bundleIdentifier and FileManager.displayName(atPath:), copied with NSPasteboard.general.setString.

functions.name: Hide Application
functions.what: Hides a running app.
functions.macos_build: NSRunningApplication.hide()

functions.name: Quit Application
functions.what: Quits the app normally.
functions.macos_build: NSRunningApplication.terminate()

functions.name: Force Quit Application
functions.what: Kills an unresponsive app.
functions.macos_build: NSRunningApplication.forceTerminate()

functions.name: Restart Application
functions.what: Quits the app and launches it again.
functions.macos_build: Call terminate(), then wait for NSWorkspace.didTerminateApplicationNotification for that pid, with a timeout that offers force quit. Then call openApplication(at:configuration:).

functions.name: Uninstall Application / Uninstall Applications command
functions.what: Removes an app from its action, or from a dedicated command that lists apps to browse and uninstall.
functions.macos_build: FileManager.trashItem(at:resultingItemURL:) on the bundle. Optionally sweep leftovers in ~/Library/{Application Support, Caches, Preferences, Logs, Saved Application State, HTTPStorages, WebKit}/<bundle id>. Root-owned bundles need admin rights; fall back to Finder AppleScript 'delete', which prompts.
functions.permission: App Management (macOS 13+) to delete other apps' bundles; App Data / Full Disk Access for ~/Library/Containers and Group Containers

functions.name: Per-app alias, hotkey and root-search visibility
functions.what: Each installed app can have an alias (e.g. 'music' for Spotify) and a global hotkey. A checkbox removes the app from root search.
functions.macos_build: Per-bundle-ID rows in SQLite, with the hotkey registered through RegisterEventHotKey.

functions.name: App Hotkey Action (Toggle Visibility / Always Show)
functions.what: Sets what an app hotkey does when the app is already frontmost: hide it (toggle) or keep showing it.
functions.macos_build: If NSWorkspace.shared.frontmostApplication?.bundleIdentifier matches, call hide(); otherwise activate or launch the app.

functions.name: Search Scopes & Deep Search
functions.what: Adds or removes folders scanned for apps. Deep Search looks up to three levels down inside added folders.
functions.macos_build: Use FileManager.enumerator(at:includingPropertiesForKeys:options:[.skipsPackageDescendants]), stopping at enumerator.level > 3, or NSMetadataQuery.searchScopes with those folders.

functions.name: Treat as Game
functions.what: Tags an app so it appears in the Games list.
functions.macos_build: A boolean tag column on the per-app row.

functions.name: New Application Window / Open Recent Files...
functions.what: Opens a new window of the app, or lists the app's recent documents.
functions.macos_build: Activate the app, then press its File > New Window or Open Recent menu item through Accessibility (AXUIElementPerformAction kAXPressAction). Recent documents can also be read from ~/Library/Application Support/com.apple.sharedfilelist/com.apple.LSSharedFileList.ApplicationRecentDocuments/<bundle id>.sfl3, an undocumented NSKeyedArchiver file of bookmark data.
functions.permission: Accessibility (menu route) / Full Disk Access may be needed for sfl3

notes: Fully local. The private MediaRemote now-playing API is locked down for third-party apps since macOS 15.4, so media detection should use per-app AppleScript or Core Audio activity. 'Quit Apps Closed to Tray' is Windows-only.

functions.name: Enable Auto Quit / Disable Auto Quit
functions.what: An app action that marks an app to quit automatically after a period of inactivity, or removes the mark.
functions.macos_build: Per-bundle-ID rows {enabled, timeout} in SQLite. Finder (com.apple.finder) and the launcher itself are always excluded.

functions.name: Manage Auto Quits
functions.what: A command that opens the Auto Quit settings list.
functions.macos_build: Opens Settings > Applications > Auto Quit, a SwiftUI list with per-app duration pickers.

functions.name: Inactivity timer
functions.what: Quits an app once it has been in the background (hidden or deactivated) for the chosen time. Returning to the app resets the timer.
functions.macos_build: Start a per-app DispatchSourceTimer on NSWorkspace.didDeactivateApplicationNotification or didHideApplicationNotification, and cancel it on didActivateApplicationNotification. When it fires and the app isn't frontmost, call NSRunningApplication.terminate(). Ignore apps whose activationPolicy is not .regular.

functions.name: Default and per-app durations
functions.what: A global default of 1, 3 (default), 5, 10 or 15 minutes, with optional per-app overrides. Changing the default updates every app that uses it.
functions.macos_build: Store a nullable per-app timeout that falls back to the UserDefaults default.

functions.name: Pause while recording or playing media
functions.what: Postpones quitting while the system is recording audio or video, or while a media player is playing.
functions.macos_build: Microphone in use: kAudioDevicePropertyDeviceIsRunningSomewhere on input devices (Core Audio). Camera in use: kCMIODevicePropertyDeviceIsRunningSomewhere (CoreMediaIO). Spotify or Music playing: AppleScript 'player state'. Reschedule instead of quitting while any of these is true.
functions.permission: none for CoreAudio/CMIO; Automation (Spotify, Music) for player state

notes: Fully local. The per-action shortcuts for window actions aren't listed in the manual. On macOS 27, the Accessibility pane is renamed 'Device Control and Data Access'.

functions.name: Switch Windows
functions.what: Lists every open window across all apps, including several windows of the same app, with title and app name. Enter brings the selected window to the front.
functions.keys: Enter switches; Cmd-K for window actions
functions.macos_build: For each NSWorkspace.runningApplications entry with .regular policy, call AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid) and read kAXWindowsAttribute, then kAXTitleAttribute and kAXMinimizedAttribute for each window. Focus with NSRunningApplication.activate() + AXUIElementPerformAction(win, kAXRaiseAction) and set kAXMainAttribute. AX only returns windows on the current Space. Windows on other Spaces need CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo(.optionAll), whose titles require Screen Recording, plus private _AXUIElementGetWindow / CGS calls, as AltTab does.
functions.permission: Accessibility (+ Screen Recording for CGWindowList titles)

functions.name: Minimize Window
functions.what: Minimizes the selected window to the Dock.
functions.macos_build: AXUIElementSetAttributeValue(win, kAXMinimizedAttribute, kCFBooleanTrue)

functions.name: Close Window
functions.what: Closes the selected window.
functions.macos_build: Copy kAXCloseButtonAttribute, then AXUIElementPerformAction(button, kAXPressAction).

functions.name: Enter Fullscreen
functions.what: Puts the selected window into full screen.
functions.macos_build: AXUIElementSetAttributeValue(win, "AXFullScreen" as CFString, kCFBooleanTrue), or press kAXFullScreenButtonAttribute.

functions.name: Hide Application (from window list)
functions.what: Hides the app that owns the selected window.
functions.macos_build: NSRunningApplication(processIdentifier:)?.hide()

functions.name: Search Menu Bar Items
functions.what: Fuzzy-searches the frontmost app's menu bar commands (e.g. Export as PDF, Merge Cells) and runs the chosen one.
functions.macos_build: Capture the frontmost pid before the non-activating panel shows. Call AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid), read kAXMenuBarAttribute, and walk kAXChildrenAttribute recursively (AXMenuBarItem > AXMenu > AXMenuItem). Collect the title path, kAXEnabledAttribute, and kAXMenuItemCmdCharAttribute / kAXMenuItemCmdModifiersAttribute / kAXMenuItemCmdVirtualKeyAttribute for shortcut labels. Skip separators. Run with AXUIElementPerformAction(item, kAXPressAction). Cache per app and set AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout, because large menus (Office, Xcode) take hundreds of ms to walk.

notes: Sources: www.raycast.com/core-features/calendar and manual.raycast.com/calendar. Calendar data comes from macOS Calendar accounts (iCloud, Google, Exchange, Yahoo, CalDAV via Internet Accounts), so EventKit covers reading, creating, deleting and blocking time. Not replicable through EventKit: Accept/Decline RSVP and sending invitations to attendees, since EKParticipant is read-only. Those need provider APIs (Google Calendar, Microsoft Graph) with OAuth. Auto Transcribe depends on the third-party Granola app. Ask Calendar (@calendar) depends on Raycast AI (cloud).
