The marketing FAQ mentions notifications, reminders and time tracking, but the manual describes none of them. Menu bar agenda on macOS 26 requires allowing the item in System Settings > Menu Bar.

functions.name: My Schedule
functions.what: Lists upcoming events in groups: this week by day, next week, the rest of the month, then later months, up to three months ahead. A summary of the next meeting sits at the top, and the search bar filters by title.
functions.macos_build: Call EKEventStore.events(matching: predicateForEvents(withStart: now, end: now + 3 months, calendars: enabled)) and group by Calendar.dateInterval(of: .weekOfYear / .month). Refresh on .EKEventStoreChanged. Filter titles client-side.

functions.name: Join Events (next meeting in Root Search)
functions.what: The next event appears at the top of root search during a window around its start time (2, 5, 10 by default, 15 or 30 minutes). Enter opens the call in the provider's native app when installed, otherwise in the browser.
functions.macos_build: Find the conference URL with a regex over EKEvent.url, location and notes: zoom.us/j, meet.google.com, teams.microsoft.com/l/meetup-join, *.webex.com, app.slack.com/huddle, facetime.apple.com/join, join.skype.com, bluejeans.com, chime.aws, whereby.com, meet.jit.si, around.co, chorus.ai, riverside.fm, streamyard.com. When the app is installed (check NSWorkspace.urlForApplication(withBundleIdentifier:)), rewrite to its native scheme, e.g. zoommtg://zoom.us/join?confno=<id>&pwd=<pwd> or msteams:<path>. Open with NSWorkspace.open.

functions.name: Join Conference Call (action)
functions.what: Joins the selected event's meeting from My Schedule or root search.
functions.macos_build: Same URL detection and native-app rewrite as Join Events.

functions.name: Open Event in Default Application
functions.what: Opens the event in the chosen calendar app: Calendar, Fantastical, Notion Calendar, Amie, BusyCal or Outlook, whichever are installed.
functions.macos_build: For Calendar.app, use the undocumented ical://ekevent/<calendarItemIdentifier>?method=show&options=more URL, or AppleScript 'tell application "Calendar" to show' on the event found by its uid (calendarItemExternalIdentifier). Fantastical: x-fantastical3://show?date=yyyy-MM-dd. Other apps: activate them. Detect installed apps with NSWorkspace.urlForApplication(withBundleIdentifier:).
functions.permission: Calendars; Automation (Calendar) for the AppleScript route

functions.name: Create Event
functions.what: A form for title, start and end, calendar, attendees, location, URL, notes and reminders. The event is saved to macOS Calendar and syncs to that account.
functions.macos_build: Create EKEvent(eventStore:), set its fields and calendar, call addAlarm(EKAlarm(relativeOffset:)), then store.save(_:span: .thisEvent, commit: true). EventKit can't add attendees or send invitations. Use Calendar AppleScript 'make new attendee' (unreliable) or the provider API.

functions.name: Block Time
functions.what: Reserves a busy block (e.g. focus time) in your calendar from a free slot.
functions.macos_build: Create EKEvent with availability = .busy in the chosen calendar for the selected slot and save it.

functions.name: Email All Attendees
functions.what: Starts an email to everyone invited to the event.
functions.macos_build: Collect EKEvent.attendees and their EKParticipant.url (mailto:) into mailto:a@x,b@y?subject=<title> and open it, or use NSSharingService(named: .composeEmail) with recipients.

functions.name: Accept / Decline invitation
functions.what: Responds to a pending invitation.
functions.macos_build: Not possible with public EventKit, because participantStatus is read-only. It needs CalDAV, Google Calendar or Microsoft Graph APIs with the user's OAuth, or fragile UI scripting of Calendar.app through Accessibility.

functions.name: Copy Availability
functions.what: Copies your free time slots as text to paste into a message.
functions.macos_build: Merge busy intervals from enabled calendars over the next N days, subtract them from working hours, format the remaining slots with DateIntervalFormatter, and copy with NSPasteboard.

functions.name: Copy Event Details / Copy Event Title / Copy Event Attendees
functions.what: Copies the full event summary, just the title, or the attendee list.
functions.keys: Cmd-. details; Shift-Cmd-. title; Shift-Cmd-, attendees
functions.macos_build: Format title, DateIntervalFormatter range, location, URL and attendees, and copy with NSPasteboard.

functions.name: Delete Event
functions.what: Deletes the selected event.
functions.macos_build: Confirm with NSAlert, then store.remove(event, span: .thisEvent or .futureEvents, commit: true).

functions.name: Auto-Join Meetings (+ Confirm before joining)
functions.what: Off by default. Joins meetings you're attending as they start. A confirmation prompt is on by default and can be turned off.
functions.macos_build: Schedule a DispatchSourceTimer for the next qualifying event's startDate, where the current user's EKParticipant (isCurrentUser) has accepted and a conference URL exists. Re-plan on .EKEventStoreChanged and NSWorkspace.didWakeNotification. When it fires, show a floating NSPanel with Join and Skip if confirmation is on, then open the URL.

functions.name: Camera Preview before joining
functions.what: Shows a camera preview so you can check yourself before a call.
functions.macos_build: AVCaptureSession with AVCaptureDevice.default(for: .video), shown through AVCaptureVideoPreviewLayer in a small floating NSPanel. Requires NSCameraUsageDescription.

functions.name: Show Events in Menu Bar (menu bar agenda)
functions.what: Shows the current or next event in the menu bar. Options: Never (default), When it starts, 2/5/10/15/30/60 minutes before, Upcoming events, or Always. 'Only show events with a conference link' is on by default, and 'Hide Current Event' hides it automatically or 2/5/10/15 minutes after start. The menu offers Open My Schedule, Open Calendar app, Join meeting and Dismiss event.
functions.macos_build: A second NSStatusItem whose button title shows the event title and countdown, updated by a 30-second Timer, with an NSMenu for the four actions. Keep dismissed event IDs in memory.

functions.name: Enabled Calendars
functions.what: Chooses which macOS calendars feed root search, My Schedule and the menu bar.
functions.macos_build: EKEventStore.calendars(for: .event) grouped by EKSource, with the selected calendarIdentifiers persisted.

functions.name: Google Services browser
functions.what: Chooses which browser opens Google Meet and other Google links.
functions.macos_build: NSWorkspace.shared.open([url], withApplicationAt: browserURL, configuration:)

functions.name: Auto Transcribe Meetings (+ Exclude keywords)
functions.what: Saves meeting transcripts to notes through the Granola app. Meetings whose titles contain excluded keywords (case-insensitive, partial match) are skipped.
functions.macos_build: Raycast hands this off to Granola. A native version would capture system and app audio with ScreenCaptureKit (SCStreamConfiguration.capturesAudio) or Core Audio process taps, plus the microphone, and transcribe locally with the Speech framework (SFSpeechRecognizer with requiresOnDeviceRecognition) or whisper.cpp.
functions.permission: Screen & System Audio Recording, Microphone, Speech Recognition

functions.name: Ask Calendar (@calendar in AI Chat)
functions.what: Natural-language questions about your schedule, plus creating, editing and deleting events through AI.
functions.macos_build: LLM tool-calling over EventKit functions (list, create, update, delete). Use a cloud model, or a local llama.cpp instruct model with function calling.

notes: Sources: www.raycast.com/core-features/system (16 commands, Monterey+, with Finder and System Events Automation prompts on first run) and manual.raycast.com/system-commands (about 40 commands in the 'System Actions' extension, shared with Windows). Windows-flavored items with no public macOS API: Hibernate, Toggle HDR, Toggle Camera Mute, Toggle Airplane Mode (macOS has none; emulate it). Several macOS equivalents rely on private frameworks: Lock Screen (login.framework SACLockScreenImmediate), Night Shift (CoreBrightness CBBlueLightClient), Toggle Bluetooth (IOBluetoothPreferenceSetControllerPowerState), Show Desktop (CoreDockSendNotification). None of them need cloud services.

functions.name: Lock Screen
functions.what: Locks the Mac immediately.
functions.macos_build: Post Ctrl-Cmd-Q, the standard lock shortcut, as a CGEvent to .cghidEventTap. Alternatively dlopen /System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/login.framework and call SACLockScreenImmediate(), which is private but needs no permission.

functions.name: Sleep
functions.what: Puts the Mac to sleep.
functions.macos_build: Run /usr/bin/pmset sleepnow through Process (no root needed), or use IOKit IOPMSleepSystem(IOPMFindPowerManagement(kIOMainPortDefault)), or AppleScript 'tell application "System Events" to sleep'.
functions.permission: none (Automation: System Events for AppleScript route)

functions.name: Sleep Displays
functions.what: Turns the displays off without sleeping the Mac.
functions.macos_build: /usr/bin/pmset displaysleepnow

functions.name: Restart
functions.what: Restarts the Mac.
functions.macos_build: Send a kAERestart Apple Event to loginwindow (bundle com.apple.loginwindow) with AESendMessage, per Apple Tech Q&A QA1134, or AppleScript 'tell application "System Events" to restart'. Needs the com.apple.security.automation.apple-events entitlement under the hardened runtime.

functions.name: Shut Down
functions.what: Quits open apps and shuts the Mac down.
functions.macos_build: kAEShutDown Apple Event to loginwindow (QA1134), or System Events 'shut down'.

functions.name: Log Out
functions.what: Logs the current user out.
functions.macos_build: kAEReallyLogOut to loginwindow (no prompt), kAELogOut (shows the confirmation dialog), or System Events 'log out'.

functions.name: Show Screen Saver
functions.what: Starts the screen saver.
functions.macos_build: NSWorkspace.shared.openApplication(at: URL(fileURLWithPath: "/System/Library/CoreServices/ScreenSaverEngine.app"), configuration:)

functions.name: Hibernate
functions.what: Hibernates the computer. This is effectively a Windows command.
functions.macos_build: There is no user-level hibernate on macOS. The nearest is 'pmset -a hibernatemode 25' (root, through an SMAppService privileged daemon) followed by sleep, and it changes the system power policy.

functions.name: Toggle Energy Saver (Low Power Mode)
functions.what: Turns the power-saving mode on or off.
functions.macos_build: Read the state with ProcessInfo.processInfo.isLowPowerModeEnabled. Setting it needs root, 'pmset -a lowpowermode 1/0', through an SMAppService.daemon helper, or 'do shell script ... with administrator privileges', which asks for a password every time.

functions.name: Play / Pause, Next Track, Previous Track
functions.what: Controls whichever app is currently playing media.
functions.macos_build: Synthesize media-key system-defined events with NSEvent.otherEvent(with: .systemDefined, ..., subtype: 8, data1: (keyType << 16) | (0xA << 8)) for key down and 0xB for key up, where keyType is NX_KEYTYPE_PLAY 16, NX_KEYTYPE_NEXT 17 or NX_KEYTYPE_PREVIOUS 18. Post event.cgEvent to .cghidEventTap. macOS routes it to the Now Playing app.

functions.name: Toggle Mute
functions.what: Mutes or unmutes system output.
functions.macos_build: Core Audio: read kAudioHardwarePropertyDefaultOutputDevice from kAudioObjectSystemObject, then AudioObjectSetPropertyData with kAudioDevicePropertyMute (scope kAudioDevicePropertyScopeOutput, element kAudioObjectPropertyElementMain). HDMI/DisplayPort devices without a mute property need a fallback.

functions.name: Turn Volume Up / Turn Volume Down
functions.what: Raises or lowers system volume by a few percent.
functions.macos_build: Get and set kAudioHardwareServiceDeviceProperty_VirtualMainVolume (Float32 0-1, AudioToolbox) on the default output device in steps of 1/16. To get the native volume HUD, post NX_KEYTYPE_SOUND_UP (0) / NX_KEYTYPE_SOUND_DOWN (1) media-key events instead, which needs Accessibility.

functions.name: Set Volume / Set Volume to 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%
functions.what: Sets the volume to a typed value or one of five presets.
functions.macos_build: Write the same VirtualMainVolume property. Set Volume takes a numeric command argument.

functions.name: Volume Mixer
functions.what: Lists apps in Playing and Idle sections, with per-app volume and mute.
functions.keys: + or = raise; - lower; Ctrl-M mute selected app; Left/Right adjust when search is empty
functions.macos_build: macOS has no per-app volume API. List audio processes with kAudioHardwarePropertyProcessObjectList and kAudioProcessPropertyIsRunningOutput / kAudioProcessPropertyBundleID. To control volume, create a Core Audio process tap on macOS 14.2+ (CATapDescription(stereoMixdownOfProcesses:) with muteBehavior .mutedWhenTapped, AudioHardwareCreateProcessTap), route it through a private aggregate device, and scale the samples in an IOProc before playing to the output.

functions.name: Toggle Active App Mute / Turn Active App Volume Up / Down
functions.what: Mutes or steps the volume of only the frontmost app.
functions.macos_build: The same process-tap machinery, targeting the frontmost app's audio object from kAudioHardwarePropertyTranslatePIDToProcessObject.

functions.name: Toggle Microphone Mute
functions.what: Mutes or unmutes every connected microphone.
functions.macos_build: Enumerate kAudioHardwarePropertyDevices, keep devices with input streams (kAudioDevicePropertyStreams on the input scope), and set kAudioDevicePropertyMute on the input scope. If a device doesn't support mute, save kAudioDevicePropertyVolumeScalar, set it to 0, and restore it later. Show the state in the menu bar.

functions.name: Toggle Camera Mute
functions.what: Blocks or restores camera access for every app.
functions.macos_build: There is no public macOS API, because camera TCC is per-app and controlled by the user. At most, detect camera use with CoreMediaIO kCMIODevicePropertyDeviceIsRunningSomewhere. Treat it as not replicable.

functions.name: Show Desktop
functions.what: Moves all windows aside to show the desktop.
functions.macos_build: No public API. Either call private CoreDockSendNotification("com.apple.showdesktop.awake" as CFString, 0), or post the user's Show Desktop shortcut (symbolic hotkey 36 in com.apple.symbolichotkeys, default F11) as a CGEvent.

functions.name: Toggle System Appearance
functions.what: Switches between light and dark mode.
functions.macos_build: NSAppleScript: tell application "System Events" to tell appearance preferences to set dark mode to not dark mode. Read the current state from UserDefaults 'AppleInterfaceStyle' or NSApp.effectiveAppearance.

functions.name: Toggle Stage Manager
functions.what: Turns Stage Manager on or off.
functions.macos_build: Flip com.apple.WindowManager 'GloballyEnabled' with CFPreferencesSetAppValue + CFPreferencesAppSynchronize. Whether this applies live has varied by macOS version. A reliable fallback is to run a bundled Shortcuts shortcut that uses the 'Set Stage Manager' action, via /usr/bin/shortcuts run.

functions.name: Toggle HDR
functions.what: Turns HDR on or off. This is a Windows-oriented command.
functions.macos_build: No public API. The macOS Displays HDR switch uses private SkyLight/CoreDisplay calls.

functions.name: Toggle Night Light (Night Shift on Mac)
functions.what: Turns the warm-color display filter on or off.
functions.macos_build: Private CoreBrightness.framework: load CBBlueLightClient with dlopen + NSClassFromString, then call getBlueLightStatus: and setEnabled:.

functions.name: Open Trash
functions.what: Opens the Trash in Finder.
functions.macos_build: NSWorkspace.shared.open(FileManager.default.url(for: .trashDirectory, in: .userDomainMask, appropriateFor: nil, create: false)), or Finder AppleScript 'open trash'.

functions.name: Empty Trash (+ Show Warning Before Emptying Trash)
functions.what: Permanently empties the Trash. A setting can ask for confirmation first.
functions.macos_build: NSAppleScript 'tell application "Finder" to empty trash', which covers every volume's trash and handles locked items, with an optional NSAlert first. Deleting ~/.Trash directly would require Full Disk Access.

functions.name: Eject All Disks
functions.what: Ejects every mounted external disk and disk image.
functions.macos_build: FileManager.default.mountedVolumeURLs(includingResourceValuesForKeys: [.volumeIsEjectableKey, .volumeIsRemovableKey, .volumeIsInternalKey], options: [.skipHiddenVolumes]), filtered to ejectable or removable volumes, then NSWorkspace.shared.unmountAndEjectDevice(at:) for each. DiskArbitration DADiskUnmount + DADiskEject can report which process blocks an eject.

functions.name: Toggle Hidden Files
functions.what: Shows or hides hidden files in Finder.
functions.macos_build: CFPreferencesSetAppValue("AppleShowAllFiles", flag, "com.apple.finder") + CFPreferencesAppSynchronize, then relaunch Finder: terminate the com.apple.finder NSRunningApplication and reopen it. Alternatively post Shift-Cmd-. to Finder, which flips the setting live.

functions.name: Hide All Apps Except Frontmost
functions.what: Hides every app except the one in front.
functions.macos_build: Capture NSWorkspace.shared.frontmostApplication before the panel shows. Call hide() on every runningApplications entry with .regular policy and a different pid.

functions.name: Unhide All Hidden Apps
functions.what: Brings back every hidden app.
functions.macos_build: NSWorkspace.shared.runningApplications.filter(\.isHidden).forEach { $0.unhide() }

functions.name: Quit All Apps (+ warning, Excluded Applications)
functions.what: Quits every running app except excluded ones. A confirmation is on by default.
functions.macos_build: Call terminate() on regular apps, excluding self, Finder and the user's excluded bundle IDs, with an optional NSAlert first. Apps with unsaved documents show their own save sheets.

functions.name: Quit All Apps Except Frontmost
functions.what: Same as Quit All Apps, but keeps the frontmost app open.
functions.macos_build: Same as above, also excluding the captured frontmost pid.

functions.name: Dismiss Notifications
functions.what: Clears the notifications currently on screen.
functions.macos_build: No public API. Use Accessibility on the Notification Center process (com.apple.notificationcenterui): walk its windows and perform each notification group's custom 'Close' or 'Clear All' action, found with AXUIElementCopyActionNames. Action names vary by macOS version, so this is fragile.

functions.name: WiFi (connect to saved networks)
functions.what: Lists nearby and saved Wi-Fi networks and connects to one.
functions.macos_build: CoreWLAN: get CWWiFiClient.shared().interface(), call scanForNetworks(withName: nil), read saved profiles from configuration?.networkProfiles, and connect with associate(to:password:). Saved passwords come from CWKeychainFindWiFiPassword, which may prompt. SSIDs are redacted unless the app has Location Services authorization (CLLocationManager) on macOS 14+.

functions.name: Toggle WiFi
functions.what: Turns Wi-Fi on or off.
functions.macos_build: CWWiFiClient.shared().interface()?.setPower(!powerOn())
functions.permission: none (admin if 'require administrator to turn Wi-Fi on/off' is set)

functions.name: Bluetooth (manage paired devices)
functions.what: Lists paired devices and connects or disconnects them. It doesn't turn Bluetooth on or off.
functions.macos_build: IOBluetooth: IOBluetoothDevice.pairedDevices(), isConnected(), openConnection() / closeConnection(). Requires NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription.

functions.name: Toggle Bluetooth
functions.what: Turns Bluetooth on or off.
functions.macos_build: No public API. Use the private IOBluetoothPreferenceGetControllerPowerState() and IOBluetoothPreferenceSetControllerPowerState(Int32) from IOBluetooth.framework, as blueutil does.

functions.name: Toggle Airplane Mode
functions.what: Turns all radios off or back on.
functions.macos_build: macOS has no airplane mode. Emulate it by turning off Wi-Fi (CoreWLAN setPower) and Bluetooth (private IOBluetooth call) together, remembering their previous states, and restoring them.

notes: Sources: manual.raycast.com/emoji-symbols (the /emoji-picker manual URL returns 404) and www.raycast.com/core-features/emoji-picker. The marketing page's claims about working in Gmail, GitHub and Linux look like SEO copy. The manual says ':' autocomplete works only inside Raycast text fields. Raycast's 'AI Results' and AI-generated keywords use Raycast AI (cloud). Natively, DigUp's local EmbeddingGemma can do the same semantic search offline. The Primary Action setting exists, but the manual doesn't list its options; Paste and Copy are the obvious pair.

functions.name: Search Emoji & Symbols
functions.what: A grid of emoji, flags and Unicode symbols, searchable by name, category and custom keywords.
functions.macos_build: Bundle Unicode emoji-test.txt (order, groups, skin-tone sequences) and CLDR annotations (keywords and short names) as a JSON resource. For symbols, iterate Unicode scalar ranges and read Unicode.Scalar.Properties.name and generalCategory from the Swift standard library, which works fully offline. Render with a SwiftUI LazyVGrid or NSCollectionView using Apple Color Emoji.

functions.name: AI / semantic emoji results
functions.what: When nothing matches directly, AI-suggested emoji appear. Tab shows AI alternatives even when there are direct matches.
functions.macos_build: Embed each emoji's name and CLDR keywords once with DigUp's EmbeddingGemma, store the vectors next to the emoji table, and run cosine search on the query. Everything stays local.

functions.name: Category filter
functions.what: A dropdown filter by category, such as Smileys & People, Symbols or Flags.
functions.macos_build: Group or subgroup values from emoji-test.txt, shown in a toolbar Picker.

functions.name: Pin / Unpin Emoji
functions.what: Pinned emoji always stay at the top of the grid.
functions.macos_build: A pinned table (emoji, position) in SQLite.

functions.name: Frecency ranking
functions.what: Emoji you use often and recently rank higher. This usage history is exported with settings.
functions.macos_build: Reuse the root frecency table, keyed by emoji.

functions.name: Grid column count
functions.what: Changes how many emoji fit per row (6-10), from the keyboard or in Settings.
functions.keys: Cmd-- smaller / Cmd-+ larger / Cmd-0 reset
functions.macos_build: Bind GridItem count to a UserDefaults value.

functions.name: Default Emoji Skin Tone
functions.what: Sets the skin tone applied to every emoji that supports it.
functions.macos_build: Append U+1F3FB-U+1F3FF to the base when Unicode.Scalar.Properties.isEmojiModifierBase is true. Multi-person sequences (handshake, couples) need the fully-qualified variants from emoji-test.txt.

functions.name: Paste with Skin Tone... / Copy with Skin Tone...
functions.what: Picks one of six tone variants for a single paste or copy without changing the default.
functions.macos_build: An inline sub-view showing the 6 variants, then the paste or copy routine.

functions.name: Paste (default primary action)
functions.what: Inserts the emoji into the app you were typing in.
functions.macos_build: Write to NSPasteboard and hide the panel so the previous app becomes key again (call activate on the captured NSRunningApplication). Post Cmd-V with CGEvent to .cghidEventTap. Optionally restore the previous clipboard contents afterwards.

functions.name: Copy to Clipboard
functions.what: Copies the emoji without pasting it.
functions.macos_build: NSPasteboard.general.setString

functions.name: Paste and Keep Window Open
functions.what: Pastes into the target app and leaves the picker open for more selections.
functions.macos_build: Keep the panel visible (hidesOnDeactivate = false, floating level) but call resignKey and activate the previous app. Post Cmd-V, then makeKey on the panel again.

functions.name: Copy Unicode
functions.what: Copies the code point notation, e.g. U+1F600.
functions.macos_build: Join the unicodeScalars as 'U+' + String(value, radix: 16, uppercase: true).

functions.name: Assign / Edit Custom Keywords
functions.what: Adds your own search words to an emoji.
functions.macos_build: An emoji_keywords table in SQLite, merged into the search index and re-embedded for semantic search.

functions.name: Save AI-generated custom keywords
functions.what: When an emoji found through AI or semantic search is used, the query is saved as a keyword for that emoji.
functions.macos_build: On paste or copy from a semantic result, insert the query into emoji_keywords.

functions.name: Primary Action setting
functions.what: Chooses what Enter does in the picker.
functions.macos_build: A UserDefaults enum that swaps actions[0] and actions[1].

functions.name: Inline ':' emoji autocomplete
functions.what: Typing ':' plus a word in any launcher text field (notes, snippet editor, AI composer) opens emoji suggestions. Ranking uses pinned status, frecency and name match, and respects the skin tone. It doesn't work in other apps.
functions.macos_build: Use NSTextViewDelegate textDidChange to detect ':' followed by a word, and show a popover anchored at firstRect(forCharacterRange:actualRange:). Insert with insertText on Enter.

functions.name: Replace system emoji picker hotkey
functions.what: Makes the picker open from the usual system emoji shortcut.
functions.macos_build: The user first sets 'Press globe key to: Do Nothing' and frees the Character Viewer shortcut in System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts. Then register Ctrl-Cmd-Space with RegisterEventHotKey. fn-E needs the flagsChanged event tap.

feature: Import & Export of Settings and Data
notes: The .rayconfig format is proprietary and encrypted, so a native fork needs its own format. Scheduled backups are Pro-only in Raycast. Cloud Sync is a separate cloud feature. Migration from Raycast v1 to v2 is Raycast-specific. Importing from Alfred or Spotlight isn't documented.

functions.name: Export Settings & Data
functions.what: Bundles snippets, quicklinks, clipboard history, notes, emoji history, AI chats and commands, extension list, settings with aliases and hotkeys, and window layouts into one passphrase-encrypted file.
functions.macos_build: Serialize each store to Codable JSON and combine them into one archive (AppleArchive or a JSON container). Encrypt with CryptoKit AES.GCM.seal using a 256-bit key derived from the passphrase (8+ characters) with PBKDF2 (CommonCrypto CCKeyDerivationPBKDF, random salt, high iteration count), since CryptoKit has no password KDF. Save through NSSavePanel.

functions.name: Import Settings & Data (selective)
functions.what: Shows a checklist so only chosen categories are imported. Data is merged, and duplicate snippets (same text, keyword and name), duplicate quicklinks (same link) and keyword collisions are skipped.
functions.macos_build: NSOpenPanel, decrypt, then a per-category checkbox sheet. Merge with UNIQUE constraints and INSERT OR IGNORE in SQLite.

functions.name: Snippets / Quicklinks JSON export
functions.what: Exports snippets or quicklinks as unencrypted JSON for sharing.
functions.macos_build: JSONEncoder written through NSSavePanel.

functions.name: Scheduled Backups
functions.what: Exports automatically on a daily, weekly or monthly schedule to a chosen folder, such as iCloud Drive. Backups are skipped when no valid passphrase is set.
functions.macos_build: NSBackgroundActivityScheduler (interval, repeats = true). Keep the passphrase in the Keychain (SecItemAdd, kSecClassGenericPassword) so backups can run unattended. Keep a security-scoped bookmark if the app is ever sandboxed.
